definition_zh: 沼泽；湿地；淹没（土地）；使（船）灌水；使应接不暇
definition_en: an area of low, wet ground where water collects and trees or tall plants grow; to flood land or fill a boat with water; to overwhelm someone with too much of something
core_image: 一片低洼地常年积水，柳树干和芦苇把根泡在浑黄的静水里
scene: 连日暴雨后，河水漫过低地，柳树和芦苇都泡在齐膝深的浑水里。After days of rain the river spread over the low field and turned it into a swamp.
sceneCN: 这里 swamp 指「长着树木或高草的积水低地」（第 1 个义项：以木本植物为主的湿地）；句意：连日降雨后河水漫过低地，把它变成了一片沼泽。图中可辨识物件：齐膝的浑水、柳树干、芦苇丛、漫过田埂的河面。

pos.zh: 沼泽；湿地（木本或草本植物茂盛的积水低地）
淹没（土地）；使（船）灌满水；使应接不暇、被大量事物压垮
（土地）积水成沼；（船）进水下沉

collocations.zh: 以大量低价商品冲击市场

derivatives.zh: 沼泽沼气（湿地有机物腐烂产生的气体）
蒸发式冷风机（北美口语，因靠水蒸发降温而得名）

senses.title: Forested wetland with standing water
senses.titleCN: 长着树木的积水低地（木本沼泽）
senses.definition: a low area of land where water stands for much of the year and trees such as willows or cypresses grow in it
senses.definitionCN: 常年积水的低洼地，柳树、落羽杉等树木生长其中
senses.example: After days of rain the river spread over the low field and turned it into a swamp.
senses.exampleCN: 连日降雨后，河水漫过低地，把它变成了一片沼泽。
senses.why: the noun names the ground itself, and the defining features are low position, standing water and rooted plants that tolerate wet soil.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指地面本身，其要点是地势低、常年积水、并且长着耐湿的扎根植物。

senses.title: Any marshy or boggy ground
senses.titleCN: 广义的湿地、泥泞低地
senses.definition: broadly, any soft wet ground that gives way underfoot, whether or not trees grow on it
senses.definitionCN: 泛指任何踩上去会下陷的湿软地面，无论其上是否长树
senses.example: The path crossed a reed swamp before it reached the dunes.
senses.exampleCN: 小路穿过一片芦苇荡，才到达沙丘。
senses.why: the tree sense is the prototype, but speakers extend the word to reedy and grassy wetlands because the shared feature is saturated ground, not woodiness.
senses.whyCN: 树木只是原型特征；说话人把它扩展到芦苇沼泽与草甸，因为共同点是土壤饱和，而非有树。

senses.title: Flood dry land
senses.titleCN: 淹没旱地，使变成沼泽
senses.definition: to cover an area of land with water so that it becomes marshy or impassable
senses.definitionCN: 用水覆盖一片土地，使其变成沼泽或无法通行
senses.example: The burst canal swamped the lower pastures within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 运河决口后一小时内就淹没了下游的牧场。
senses.why: the verb reverses the noun's usual state: land that was dry is made into the thing the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词的状态倒转过来：原本干燥的土地被造成名词所指的那种地方。

senses.title: Fill a boat with water
senses.titleCN: （水）灌满船只，使其下沉
senses.definition: to fill a small boat with water so that it sinks or is in danger of sinking
senses.definitionCN: 使小船灌满水而下沉或濒临下沉
senses.example: A following sea swamped the dinghy just beyond the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 一道尾随浪在礁石外把小艇灌满了水。
senses.why: a boat swamped by water is in the same condition as land swamped by a flood, so the same verb serves both objects.
senses.whyCN: 被水灌满的船与被洪水淹没的地处在同一种状态，因此同一个动词可以带两类宾语。

senses.title: Overwhelm with too much work
senses.titleCN: 被大量工作或事务压得应接不暇
senses.definition: to give someone far more work, requests or information than they can handle
senses.definitionCN: 给某人的工作、请求或信息远超其所能处理的数量
senses.example: The small office was swamped with applications in the final week.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一周，这家小办公室被申请材料淹没了。
senses.why: the metaphor is water over land: an amount that rises above capacity is felt as flooding, so the object is buried rather than merely busy.
senses.whyCN: 隐喻来自水淹陆地：超出承受量的东西像水上涨，人被埋在其中，而不只是忙碌。

senses.title: Defeat by sheer numbers
senses.titleCN: 以数量压倒、使无法招架
senses.definition: to defeat or outnumber an opponent so heavily that resistance collapses
senses.definitionCN: 以绝对数量击败或压过对手，使其抵抗崩溃
senses.example: Cheap imports swamped the local makers within two seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价进口货在两个销售季内就压垮了本地制造商。
senses.why: from flooding the physical sense passes to competition: a market or an army is 'drowned' by numbers it cannot match.
senses.whyCN: 从淹没实物的用法过渡到竞争：市场或军队被无法匹敌的数量「淹掉」。

senses.title: A situation that traps and slows you
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：使人陷住、难以脱身的困境
senses.definition: a difficult situation that absorbs time and energy and prevents progress, as mud holds a walker
senses.definitionCN: 耗费时间精力、使人无法前进的困难处境，如泥沼拖住行人
senses.example: The project sank into a swamp of approvals and revisions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目陷进了审批与改稿的泥沼。
senses.why: wet ground that pulls at the feet is a natural image for bureaucracy or debt, so the noun is used for any sticky predicament.
senses.whyCN: 会拽住双脚的湿地是官僚程序或债务的天然意象，因此名词可指任何黏住人的困境。

senses.title: Flood a market with goods
senses.titleCN: 以大量商品涌入并冲击市场
senses.definition: to supply a market with so much of a product that prices or rivals are forced down
senses.definitionCN: 向市场投入过多某种产品，压低价位或挤垮对手
senses.example: Two firms swamped the market with low-cost panels that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天，两家公司用低价板材淹没了市场。
senses.why: this is sense 3 applied to commerce: the market is the land, goods are the water, and excess is the flood.
senses.whyCN: 这是第 3 个义项在商业上的投射：市场是陆地，商品是水，过量就是洪水。

intro.en: Swamp is a Middle English noun for wet low ground, first recorded around 1500. Its deeper origin is not settled: a Middle Dutch or Middle Low German source has been proposed, and a link with the Germanic word for 'sponge' is plausible but unproven.
intro.cn: swamp 是中古英语指湿低地的名词，约 1500 年首次见于记载。其更深来源尚无定论：有人提出它来自中古荷兰语或中古低地德语，也有人把它与日耳曼语中「海绵」一词联系起来，但均未得到证实。

items.en: Swampe is recorded around 1500 with the sense 'watery land, marsh', the earliest use of the word in English.
items.cn: swampe 约在 1500 年以「积水地、沼泽」义进入记载，这是该词在英语中最早的用法。

items.en: A Middle Dutch or Middle Low German swamp 'marsh, sponge' is often suggested as the source; the geographic spread of the form makes a borrowing likely but not demonstrated.
items.cn: 常有人认为来源是中古荷兰语或中古低地德语的 swamp「沼泽、海绵」；该词形的地理分布使借入说较可信，但尚未被证明。

items.en: The comparison with the Germanic word for sponge rests on the idea of ground that soaks up water; this is a semantic hypothesis, not a proven cognate relation.
items.cn: 与日耳曼语「海绵」词的比较建立在「会吸水的土地」这一想法上；这只是语义假说，并非已证实的同源关系。

items.en: By the seventeenth century swamp was used as a verb meaning 'to submerge or flood', and the nautical sense 'to fill a boat with water' grew from it.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，swamp 已用作动词，意为「淹没、灌水」，航海义「使船灌满水」由此产生。

items.en: The figurative use 'to overwhelm with numbers or quantity' appears later and is now the most frequent meaning in news and business writing.
items.cn: 「以数量压倒」的比喻义出现较晚，如今已成为新闻与商业写作中最常见的用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Germanic form is reconstructed, and no single ancestor can be named with confidence.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：其日耳曼语之前的形式属重构，无法有把握地指认单一祖形。

note.en: Group one holds words that resemble swamp in spelling or sound but are unrelated; group two holds wetland and flooding words that share part of its meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是与 swamp 拼写或读音相近但并无词源关系的词；第二组是共享部分词义的湿地与淹没类词。

entries.definition: A mass of insects or people moving together; it differs from swamp by one letter and has its own Germanic origin.
entries.definitionCN: 指成群移动的昆虫或人；与 swamp 只差一个字母，但另有日耳曼语来源。

entries.definition: To bring the foot down hard, or a printed mark; the shared -amp ending is accidental, not etymological.
entries.definitionCN: 指用力跺脚，或印出的标记；共同的 -amp 词尾只是巧合，并非同源。

entries.definition: To trade one thing for another; it sounds close to swamp but comes from a separate Germanic root.
entries.definitionCN: 指以物易物；读音接近 swamp，但来自另一条日耳曼语词根。

entries.definition: To strike a small insect with something flat; the similarity is only phonetic.
entries.definitionCN: 指用扁平物拍打小虫；相似之处仅在读音。

entries.definition: Low wet ground usually covered with grass and reeds rather than trees; swamp often implies woody growth.
entries.definitionCN: 通常长草与芦苇而非树木的低湿地面；swamp 往往暗示有木本植物。

entries.definition: Wet ground built of partly decayed plant matter, soft enough to swallow a walker; it stresses peat, swamp stresses standing water.
entries.definitionCN: 由半腐植物堆积成的湿地，软到能吞住行人；它强调泥炭，swamp 强调积水。

entries.definition: The scientific umbrella term for all saturated land, including swamps, marshes and bogs; it is neutral and policy-oriented.
entries.definitionCN: 对所有饱和土地的科学统称，包括沼泽、草沼与泥炭地；语气中立，多用于政策文本。

entries.definition: To cover land with a flood, or to overwhelm with a quantity; it is the formal Latin-based counterpart of the verb swamp.
entries.definitionCN: 指洪水淹没土地，或以大量事物压倒；是动词 swamp 的拉丁语系正式对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real collocations of the word, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The everyday phrase 'be swamped with work' carries the flooding metaphor: work rises like water over the desk.
normal.cn: 常用短语 be swamped with work 带着洪水的隐喻：工作像水一样涨过桌面。

normal.en: Wetland types line up as swamp, marsh, bog and fen, each with a different dominant plant and water chemistry.
normal.cn: 湿地类型可以排成 swamp、marsh、bog、fen，各自优势植物与水质不同。

normal.en: The adjective swampy is the regular -y derivative, as in 'swampy ground' and 'a swampy smell'.
normal.cn: 形容词 swampy 是规则的 -y 派生，如「泥泞的地面」「沼泽的气味」。

normal.en: 'Drain the swamp' is a fixed political idiom for removing entrenched corruption.
normal.cn: drain the swamp 是固定的政治习语，指清除盘根错节的腐败。

normal.en: Nautical use survives in 'the boat was swamped by a wave', where water fills the hull.
normal.cn: 航海用法仍见于 the boat was swamped by a wave，指浪把水灌进船体。

abstract.en: Picture a desk where papers rise like floodwater until only the top of the lamp shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，文件像洪水上涨，最后只剩台灯顶部露出水面。

abstract.en: Picture a market stall buried under identical cheap goods until no other seller can be seen.
abstract.cn: 想象一个摊位被一模一样的便宜货埋住，别的卖家都看不见了。

abstract.en: Picture boots pulled deeper with every step, so progress costs more than it returns.
abstract.cn: 想象每走一步靴子就陷得更深，前进的代价大于收获。

examples.en: The cypress swamp stays under water for most of the year.
examples.cn: 这片落羽杉沼泽一年中大部分时间都泡在水里。

examples.en: The office was swamped with complaints after the new timetable began.
examples.cn: 新时刻表启用后，办公室被投诉淹没了。

examples.en: One heavy wave swamped the dinghy before the crew could bail.
examples.cn: 船员还没来得及舀水，一个大浪就把小艇灌满了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「swamp」读似「水漫坡」——水漫上低坡，坡地就成了沼泽；工作堆成水，人也被淹没

root: 中古英语 swampe「积水低地」（约 1500 年），更深来源不确定；常被联系到中古荷兰语或中古低地德语 swamp「沼泽、海绵」，仅为假说，未证实。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: water standing where it should not. The noun names the ground, the verb floods land or fills a hull, and from that flooding come the senses of being overwhelmed, outnumbered, trapped and swamped in a market.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个意象展开：水停在它本不该停的地方。名词指那片地面，动词指淹没土地或灌满船体，再由「淹没」引申出被压垮、被数量压倒、被困住以及冲击市场等义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: low ground where water stands among rooted plants.
core.cn: 核心意象：低洼地里，水停在扎根植物之间。

branches.en: WETLAND TYPES: the noun splits by dominant plants, from trees to reeds.
branches.cn: 湿地类型：名词按优势植物分为有树与有苇两类。

branches.en: LAND FLOODED: dry ground is made into the noun's own condition.
branches.cn: 淹地：干燥地面被造成名词所指的状态。

branches.en: HULL FILLED: a boat takes on water as land does in a flood.
branches.cn: 灌船：船进水，与洪水中的陆地同理。

branches.en: OVERWHELMED: quantity or difficulty rises above capacity and pins the person down.
branches.cn: 被压垮：数量或难度超过承受力，把人困住。

branches.en: MARKET FLOODED: goods behave like floodwater and force prices down.
branches.cn: 市场被淹：商品像洪水，压低了价格。

intro.en: Swamp is a native Germanic noun with no productive prefix; its family is built by the adjective suffix -y, the noun-forming -ness, and noun compounds such as swampland and swamp gas.
intro.cn: swamp 是日耳曼语本族名词，没有能产的前缀；其词族由形容词后缀 -y、名词后缀 -ness 以及 swampland、swamp gas 这类复合名词构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for swamp. Latin palus 'marsh' and stagnum 'pool' translate the idea but are semantic equivalents, not cognates, so latinEntries is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: swamp 没有拉丁语来源。拉丁 palus「沼泽」与 stagnum「水塘」只是语义对应词，并非同源词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.meaning: wet ground; to flood or overwhelm
items.example: The swamp lies below the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 沼泽位于山脊之下。

items.meaning: like a swamp; soft and waterlogged
items.example: The trail turned swampy after the storm.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨后小路变得泥泞积水。

items.example: Much of the swampland was drained for farms.
items.exampleCN: 大片沼泽地被排干改为农田。

items.example: The swampiness of the field delayed the harvest.
items.exampleCN: 田里的泥泞积水延误了收割。

items.meaning: methane rising from decaying wetland plants
items.example: Swamp gas flickered over the marsh at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 黄昏时沼泽沼气在草沼上方闪动。

items.example: A swamp cooler kept the dry room bearable.
items.exampleCN: 一台蒸发式冷风机让干燥的房间勉强可待。

items.meaning: woodland rooted in permanent standing water
items.example: The swamp forest floods every spring.
items.exampleCN: 这片沼泽林每年春天被水淹没。

items.meaning: a North American oak of wet soils
items.meaningCN: 沼生白栎（北美湿生栎树）
items.example: Swamp white oak tolerates seasonal flooding.
items.exampleCN: 沼生白栎能耐季节性水淹。

definition_zh: 水生的；水中生长的；与水有关的；水上运动的；（名词）水生生物
definition_en: living or growing in water, or connected with water, water environments and water sports
core_image: 睡莲的根扎在塘泥里，叶片浮出水面，水下的鱼在叶影间穿行
scene: 池塘里的睡莲把根扎在泥中，叶片浮在水面上。Water lilies in the pond are aquatic plants that root in the mud and float on the surface.
sceneCN: 这里 aquatic 指「生长在水中的」（第 2 个义项：植物扎根水中或浮于水面）；句意：池塘里的睡莲是水生植物，根扎在泥里、叶浮在水面。图中可辨识物件：浮出水面的圆叶、塘底淤泥、游动的鱼、映着天光的池水。

pos.zh: 水生的；水中生长的；与水有关的；水上运动的
水生生物（常作复数 aquatics，指水生动植物或水上运动项目）

forms.label: 复数名词（水生生物／水上运动）

derivatives.zh: 水上运动项目；水生生物（总称）

senses.title: Animals that live in water
senses.titleCN: 生活在水中的动物
senses.definition: describing animals that spend their lives in water, whether fresh or salt
senses.definitionCN: 描述一生都在淡水或咸水中度过的动物
senses.example: Fish, turtles and frogs are aquatic animals with very different body plans.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼、龟和蛙都是水生动物，身体结构却大不相同。
senses.why: the Latin root aqua simply means water, so the adjective marks the medium an organism lives in rather than any particular body shape.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 aqua 就是「水」，因此这个形容词标记的是生物生活的介质，而不是某种特定体型。

senses.title: Plants that grow in or on water
senses.titleCN: 扎根水中或浮在水面的植物
senses.definition: describing plants that root in water or mud below water and may float their leaves at the surface
senses.definitionCN: 描述根扎在水中或水下泥里、叶片可浮到水面的植物
senses.example: Water lilies in the pond are aquatic plants that root in the mud and float on the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘里的睡莲是水生植物，根扎在泥里、叶浮在水面。
senses.why: botany extends the same medium-based label to plants, and the key contrast is with terrestrial, dry-land growth.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把同一个「按介质命名」的标签用于植物，关键对照是陆生的 dry-land 生长。

senses.title: Relating to water environments
senses.titleCN: 与水环境、水体有关的
senses.definition: connected with the physical or chemical conditions of rivers, lakes, wetlands and seas
senses.definitionCN: 与河流、湖泊、湿地和海洋的物理或化学条件有关
senses.example: The survey measured aquatic oxygen levels along the whole river.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查测量了整条河的水体含氧量。
senses.why: once the word is detached from a particular organism it can describe any process or measurement whose setting is water.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词脱离具体生物，就可以描述任何以水为场景的过程或测量。

senses.title: Water sports and activities
senses.titleCN: 水上运动与水上项目
senses.definition: connected with sports practised in or on water, such as swimming, rowing and diving
senses.definitionCN: 与在水中或水面上进行的运动有关，如游泳、划船和跳水
senses.example: The new centre hosts all aquatic events except open-water swimming.
senses.exampleCN: 新中心承办除公开水域游泳以外的全部水上项目。
senses.why: sports administration borrowed the adjective as a neutral cover term for events held in a pool or on a lake.
senses.whyCN: 体育管理借用这个形容词，作为在泳池或湖面上举行的项目的统称。

senses.title: A water-dwelling organism
senses.titleCN: （名词）水生生物
senses.definition: a plant or animal that lives in water, often used in the plural for a collection of such organisms
senses.definitionCN: 生活在水中的植物或动物，复数常指一类水生生物的总称
senses.example: The reserve protects rare aquatics in the spring-fed pools.
senses.exampleCN: 保护区保护着这些泉水池中的珍稀水生生物。
senses.why: the noun is a straightforward conversion of the adjective, naming whatever the adjective describes.
senses.whyCN: 名词由形容词直接转化而来，指形容词所描述的那类事物。

senses.title: Kept in an aquarium
senses.titleCN: 水族箱饲养的
senses.definition: describing animals or plants kept in tanks for display or hobby use rather than in the wild
senses.definitionCN: 描述养在水箱中供展示或爱好之用、而非野生状态的动植物
senses.example: The shop sells aquatic supplies for both beginners and breeders.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店为新手和繁殖者都提供水族用品。
senses.why: the hobby trade narrowed the adjective to tank-kept life, a smaller world that still shares the water medium.
senses.whyCN: 水族爱好把这个形容词收窄到水箱中的生物，范围更小，但介质仍是水。

senses.title: Of aquatic ecology as a field
senses.titleCN: 水生生态学意义上的
senses.definition: used in ecology for studies of communities that live in water, as opposed to terrestrial ones
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中用于研究水中生物群落，与陆生群落相对
senses.example: Her thesis compares aquatic and terrestrial carbon cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 她的论文比较水生与陆生碳循环。
senses.why: the adjective became a standard term of division in ecology, pairing with terrestrial to split the living world by medium.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词成为生态学的标准划分用语，与 terrestrial 配对，按介质把生物界一分为二。

senses.title: Rare figurative use: fluid and flowing
senses.titleCN: 罕见的修辞义：如水般流畅
senses.definition: rarely, describing movement or style that is smooth and flowing like water
senses.definitionCN: 罕见用法，形容动作或风格像水一样平滑流动
senses.example: Her aquatic grace on the beam surprised the judges.
senses.exampleCN: 她在平衡木上如水般的优雅让裁判惊讶。
senses.why: the metaphor is occasional and stylistic; dictionaries usually mark it as extended rather than a settled sense.
senses.whyCN: 这一隐喻只是偶发的修辞用法；词典通常把它标为引申用法，而非稳定义项。

intro.en: Aquatic comes from Latin aquaticus 'living in water', built on aqua 'water' plus the adjective suffix -aticus. It entered English in the early fifteenth century.
intro.cn: aquatic 来自拉丁 aquaticus「生活在水中的」，由 aqua「水」加形容词后缀 -aticus 构成，15 世纪初进入英语。

items.en: Aqua 'water' is one of the best-attested Latin nouns; its reconstructed Indo-European base is *akwa-, a form recovered by comparison rather than recorded anywhere.
items.cn: aqua「水」是拉丁语中记载最充分的名称之一；其重构的印欧语词根为 *akwa-，这一形式靠比较构拟，并无实际记录。

items.en: The suffix -aticus formed adjectives of place or belonging, so aquaticus meant 'of water, living in water'.
items.cn: 后缀 -aticus 构成表示场所或归属的形容词，因此 aquaticus 意为「水的、生活在水中的」。

items.en: English took the adjective in the early 1400s, at first in medical and natural-history writing about creatures and humours.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪初借入该形容词，最初见于医学与博物学著作，谈生物与体液。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries aquatic was applied to swimming, rowing and diving, giving the fixed phrase aquatic sports.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，aquatic 被用于游泳、划船与跳水，形成固定短语 aquatic sports。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology paired aquatic with terrestrial as the two basic media of life, turning the adjective into a technical division.
items.cn: 20 世纪的生态学把 aquatic 与 terrestrial 配对为两种基本生活介质，使该形容词成为技术分类用语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the *akwa- base is a reconstruction, and the exact first English citation is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：*akwa- 词根属重构形式，英语最早书证的年代也只能大致确定。

note.en: Group one separates aquatic from words built on the same aqua root but naming other things, and from one look-alike with a different root; group two contrasts it with neighbouring habitat terms.
note.cn: 第一组把 aquatic 与同出 aqua 词根却指别物的词区分开，并辨明一个词根不同的形近词；第二组对照相邻的栖息地词语。

entries.definition: A printmaking technique that mimics washes of tone; it is built on Italian acqua tinta 'tinted water', so it shares aqua but names no living thing.
entries.definitionCN: 一种模仿水墨浓淡的版画技法；由意大利语 acqua tinta「染色之水」构成，与 aqua 同源，却并不指生物。

entries.definition: A rock layer that holds groundwater; Latin aqua plus ferre 'to carry', so the water root is shared but the referent is stone, not life.
entries.definitionCN: 储存地下水的地层；由拉丁 aqua 加 ferre「携带」构成，水词根相同，所指却是岩层而非生命。

entries.definition: The farming of fish, shellfish and water plants; aqua plus cultura 'cultivation', so it names an industry rather than a habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 养殖鱼、贝类与水生植物；由 aqua 加 cultura「耕作」构成，指产业而非栖息地。

entries.definition: Hooked like an eagle's beak; it comes from Latin aquila 'eagle', not aqua 'water', so the resemblance is misleading.
entries.definitionCN: 像鹰喙一样钩曲的；来自拉丁 aquila「鹰」而非 aqua「水」，因此形近并不同源。

entries.definition: Living in or relating to the sea; it is the salt-water half of aquatic and excludes rivers and lakes.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在海中或与海有关的；它是 aquatic 的咸水一半，不含河流湖泊。

entries.definition: Living in or relating to non-salty inland water; it is the other half of aquatic, defined by low salinity.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在淡水或与淡水有关的；是 aquatic 的另一半，以低盐度为界定。

entries.definition: Able to live both on land and in water; aquatic says one medium, amphibious adds the second.
entries.definitionCN: 能在陆地与水中两种环境生活；aquatic 只说一种介质，amphibious 则加上第二种。

entries.definition: Carried or spread by water, as a disease or a craft; it describes transport, not habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 由水携带或传播的，如疾病或船只；它描述运输，而非栖息。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real aqua root, real derivatives and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 aqua 词根、真实派生词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Aqua is Latin for water, and it survives in aquarium, aqueduct, aquifer and aquaculture.
normal.cn: aqua 是拉丁语的「水」，仍见于 aquarium、aqueduct、aquifer、aquaculture。

normal.en: The fixed pair aquatic / terrestrial divides life by medium in ecology textbooks.
normal.cn: 生态学教材用 aquatic / terrestrial 这一固定对立，按介质划分生命。

normal.en: Aquatic plants and aquatic animals are the two standard collocations in field guides.
normal.cn: aquatic plants 与 aquatic animals 是野外图鉴中的两个标准搭配。

normal.en: Aquatic sports is the administrative phrase for pool and lake events.
normal.cn: aquatic sports 是泳池与湖面赛事的行政管理用语。

normal.en: The noun aquatics names either water sports collectively or water-dwelling organisms.
normal.cn: 名词 aquatics 可指水上运动的总称，也可指水生生物。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf that lives half in air and half in water, its root never leaving the mud.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子一半在空气里、一半在水里，根始终不离开泥。

abstract.en: Picture a whole lake turned into a single room with its own weather.
abstract.cn: 想象整片湖被看成一间有自己天气的房间。

abstract.en: Picture a swimmer whose lines are so smooth that the water seems to move with her.
abstract.cn: 想象一位泳者的线条如此流畅，仿佛水随她而动。

examples.en: Aquatic plants filter the pond water and shelter young fish.
examples.cn: 水生植物过滤池水，也为幼鱼提供藏身处。

examples.en: The lake supports an aquatic community that changes with the seasons.
examples.cn: 这片湖养育着一个随季节变化的水生群落。

examples.en: She competes in three aquatic events at the national games.
examples.cn: 她在全国运动会上参加三个水上项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「aqua（水）+ tic」——aqua 是水，加 -tic 成形容词：属于水的、活在水里的

root: 拉丁 aquaticus「生活在水中的」= aqua「水」+ -aticus（形容词后缀）；aqua 的印欧词根 *akwa- 为重构形式。英语 aquatic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one medium: water. The adjective first marks animals, then plants, then any condition or measurement set in water, then sports and tank keeping, then a technical ecological division; the noun simply names the organisms, and the last sense is a rare stylistic metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一个介质「水」辐射开来：形容词先指动物，再指植物，随后指任何以水为场景的条件或测量、水上运动与水族饲养，再成为生态学的技术分类；名词直接指那类生物，最后一个义项是偶见的修辞隐喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life and activity whose whole setting is water.
core.cn: 核心意象：整个场景都泡在水里的生命与活动。

branches.en: LIVING IN WATER: animals and plants are labelled by the medium, not by shape.
branches.cn: 生于水中：动物与植物按介质而非体型被命名。

branches.en: WATER AS SETTING: measurements and ecological divisions treat water as the frame of study.
branches.cn: 以水为场景：测量与生态分类把水当作研究框架。

branches.en: SPORT IN WATER: the adjective becomes an administrative cover term for pool and lake events.
branches.cn: 水上运动：形容词成为泳池与湖面赛事的统称。

branches.en: THE ORGANISMS THEMSELVES: noun conversion names the life, including tank-kept life.
branches.cn: 生物本身：名词化后指这些生命，也包括水箱中饲养的。

branches.en: FLUID STYLE: the water image is borrowed for smooth motion, a marginal use.
branches.cn: 流畅风格：水的意象被借来形容平滑动作，属边缘用法。

intro.en: Aquatic is built from the Latin noun aqua plus the adjective suffix -aticus; the same root supplies a large family of water words in English.
intro.cn: aquatic 由拉丁名词 aqua 加形容词后缀 -aticus 构成；同一词根在英语中衍生出一大批与水有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin aqua 'water' and its adjective aquaticus are the direct ancestors; aquarium and aquarius belong to the same word family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 aqua「水」及其形容词 aquaticus 是直接祖形；aquarium 与 aquarius 属于同一词族。

items.example: The aqua prefix marks water in technical terms.
items.exampleCN: aqua 前缀在技术术语中标记「水」。

items.example: Aquaticus means of water or living in water.
items.exampleCN: aquaticus 意为水的或生活在水中的。

items.example: Aquatic plants root below the surface.
items.exampleCN: 水生植物在水面下扎根。

items.example: The club runs aquatics for all ages.
items.exampleCN: 俱乐部为各年龄层开设水上项目。

items.example: The larvae live aquatically before they emerge.
items.exampleCN: 幼虫出水前过水生生活。

items.meaning: a tank or building for water life
items.example: The aquarium holds native river fish.
items.exampleCN: 水族馆养着本地河鱼。

items.example: The old aqueduct still carries spring water.
items.exampleCN: 古老渡槽仍输送泉水。

items.example: The aquifer supplies the whole valley.
items.exampleCN: 含水层供给整个山谷。

items.example: Aquaculture now supplies half the fish sold.
items.exampleCN: 水产养殖如今供应售出鱼类的一半。

latinEntries.meaning: a watering place; a water container

definition_zh: 陆地的；陆生的；地球的；陆栖的；类地的
definition_en: relating to the land or the earth, living on land rather than in water or in trees, or belonging to the planet Earth
core_image: 森林地面的苔藓间爬着甲虫，头顶是树冠，几步之外的溪水里另有生物
scene: 林下的苔藓和甲虫都生活在陆地上，与溪水里的生物全然不同。Mosses and beetles on the forest floor are terrestrial life, unlike the creatures in the stream.
sceneCN: 这里 terrestrial 指「生活在陆地上的」（第 1 个义项：陆生动物，与水生相对）；句意：林下的苔藓与甲虫是陆生生命，和溪水中的生物不同。图中可辨识物件：苔藓层、甲虫、落叶、几步外的溪流。

pos.zh: 陆地的；陆生的；地球的；陆栖的；类地的
陆地生物；地球人（少见，多用于科幻或生态分类）

derivatives.zh: 陆生动物饲养箱；玻璃花房

senses.title: Animals that live on land
senses.titleCN: 生活在陆地上的动物
senses.definition: describing animals that live mainly on dry land rather than in water
senses.definitionCN: 描述主要在干燥陆地上而非水中生活的动物
senses.example: Mosses and beetles on the forest floor are terrestrial life, unlike the creatures in the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 林下的苔藓与甲虫是陆生生命，和溪水中的生物不同。
senses.why: the Latin root terra means dry land, and ecology uses the adjective to mark the medium an animal occupies, contrasting it with aquatic.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 terra 意为干燥陆地，生态学用这个形容词标记动物所占的介质，与 aquatic 相对。

senses.title: Plants that grow on land
senses.titleCN: 生长在陆地上的植物
senses.definition: describing plants rooted in soil in the air rather than submerged or floating in water
senses.definitionCN: 描述扎根土壤、暴露在空气中，而非沉水或浮水的植物
senses.example: Terrestrial plants had to evolve a waxy cuticle to hold moisture.
senses.exampleCN: 陆生植物必须演化出蜡质角质层来保住水分。
senses.why: botany applies the same land-and-air label to plants, where the decisive contrast is with aquatic and epiphytic growth.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把同一个「陆地加空气」的标签用于植物，关键对照是水生与附生。

senses.title: Of the planet Earth
senses.titleCN: 属于地球这个行星的
senses.definition: relating to the earth as a planet, especially in contrast with other worlds
senses.definitionCN: 与作为行星的地球有关，尤与其它世界相对
senses.example: Terrestrial life may be the only life in this solar system.
senses.exampleCN: 地球生命也许是这个太阳系里唯一的生命。
senses.why: the adjective moves from land to the whole globe when the comparison shifts from water to space.
senses.whyCN: 当比较对象从水变成太空时，这个形容词便从陆地扩展到整个地球。

senses.title: Land as opposed to sea
senses.titleCN: 陆地（相对于海洋）的
senses.definition: belonging to dry land as a physical realm, as in terrestrial transport or terrestrial borders
senses.definitionCN: 属于干燥陆地这一物理领域，如陆路运输、陆地边界
senses.example: The isthmus is the narrowest terrestrial link between the two seas.
senses.exampleCN: 这条地峡是两海之间最窄的陆上通道。
senses.why: this sense treats land as a surface for movement and boundaries, so terrestrial pairs with maritime and aerial.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把陆地看作通行与划界的表面，因此 terrestrial 与 maritime、aerial 构成系列。

senses.title: Rocky planets like Earth
senses.titleCN: 类地行星（以岩石为主的行星）
senses.definition: describing planets made mainly of rock and metal, with solid surfaces, rather than gas giants
senses.definitionCN: 描述主要由岩石与金属构成、有固体表面的行星，区别于气态巨行星
senses.example: Mars and Venus are the other terrestrial planets of the inner system.
senses.exampleCN: 火星与金星是内太阳系另外两颗类地行星。
senses.why: astronomy reuses the land word for bodies with a solid surface, since a rocky planet is land writ large.
senses.whyCN: 天文学把「陆地」一词用于有固体表面的天体，因为岩石行星就是放大的陆地。

senses.title: Ground-based broadcasting or networks
senses.titleCN: 地面（而非卫星）的广播与通信
senses.definition: describing communication systems based on land stations rather than satellites or cables
senses.definitionCN: 描述以陆地站点而非卫星或海底光缆为基础的通信系统
senses.example: Terrestrial broadcasting still reaches farms beyond the fibre network.
senses.exampleCN: 地面广播仍能覆盖光纤网络之外的农场。
senses.why: the sense extends land-based physical infrastructure to radio and television, where the ground station anchors the network.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把陆基实体设施扩展到广播电视，地面站是网络的锚点。

senses.title: Ground-dwelling rather than tree-dwelling
senses.titleCN: （生态学）地栖的，与树栖相对
senses.definition: in ecology, describing species that forage or live on the ground rather than in the canopy
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中指在地面觅食或栖息、而非在树冠层的物种
senses.example: The reserve protects both terrestrial and arboreal primates.
senses.exampleCN: 保护区同时保护地栖与树栖的灵长类。
senses.why: within land habitats the adjective is narrowed further: ground is the medium, and arboreal is its opposite.
senses.whyCN: 在陆地生境内部，这个形容词进一步收窄：地面是介质，树栖是它的对立面。

senses.title: Of land ecosystems as a category
senses.titleCN: 陆地生态系统的（与水域生态相对）
senses.definition: used for ecosystems, carbon pools and biodiversity found on land, as opposed to aquatic or marine ones
senses.definitionCN: 指陆地上的生态系统、碳库与生物多样性，与水生态或海洋生态相对
senses.example: Terrestrial carbon storage depends heavily on soil depth.
senses.exampleCN: 陆地碳储量在很大程度上取决于土壤深度。
senses.why: global-change science needs a cover term for all land systems, so terrestrial becomes the standard label for that pool.
senses.whyCN: 全球变化研究需要统称所有陆地系统，terrestrial 因而成为这一集合的标准标签。

intro.en: Terrestrial comes from Latin terrestris 'of the earth', built on terra 'dry land, earth' plus the suffix -estris. English adopted it in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: terrestrial 来自拉丁 terrestris「大地的」，由 terra「干燥陆地、大地」加后缀 -estris 构成，16 世纪进入英语。

items.en: Terra meant 'dry land, earth, soil'. Its own origin is debated; a connection with a root meaning 'to dry' is often proposed but remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: terra 意为「干燥陆地、大地、土壤」。其自身来源有争议；常有人提出它与表示「干燥」的词根有关，但这仍是假说。

items.en: The adjective terrestris 'of the earth, earthly' was formed with -estris, and it contrasted with marine and celestial things.
items.cn: 形容词 terrestris「大地的、尘世的」由 -estris 构成，与海洋的、天界的事物相对。

items.en: English took terrestrial in the 1500s, first for earthly things in theology and then for land-dwelling creatures in natural history.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 terrestrial，最初在神学中指尘世之物，随后在博物学中指陆生生物。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the word was applied to solid, earth-like planets, giving the modern term terrestrial planet.
items.cn: 19 世纪，该词被用于有固体表面、类似地球的行星，形成现代术语 terrestrial planet。

items.en: Twentieth-century engineering used terrestrial for ground-based stations and networks, in contrast with satellite systems.
items.cn: 20 世纪的工程用语用 terrestrial 指地面站点与网络，与卫星系统相对。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Latin history of terra is unsettled, so any Indo-European root given for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：terra 在拉丁语之前的历史无定论，凡为其给出的印欧词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one separates terrestrial from same-root words naming terrain, tanks and planets, and from one look-alike from a different root; group two contrasts it with habitat terms.
note.cn: 第一组把 terrestrial 与同根却指地形、饲养箱、行星的词区分开，并辨明一个词根不同的形近词；第二组对照栖息地词语。

entries.definition: The physical surface of an area of land; it descends from Latin terrenum 'earth', so it shares terra but names ground shape, not habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 指一片土地的物质表面；源自拉丁 terrenum「土地」，与 terra 同源，但指地面形态而非栖息环境。

entries.definition: A glass container for land plants or small land animals; the -arium suffix makes it a place, not an adjective of habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 养陆生植物或小动物的玻璃容器；-arium 后缀使它指场所，而非栖息地形容词。

entries.definition: A crustal block with a geological history distinct from its neighbours; it is a technical geology term from the same terra stock.
entries.definitionCN: 地质历史与邻区不同的地壳块体；是同一 terra 词族的地质学专门术语。

entries.definition: Very good or very intense; it comes from Latin terrere 'to frighten', not terra 'earth', so the resemblance is deceptive.
entries.definitionCN: 极好的或极强烈的；来自拉丁 terrere「使害怕」而非 terra「大地」，因此形近而不同源。

entries.definition: Living or growing in water; it is the direct opposite of terrestrial in ecology.
entries.definitionCN: 在水中生活或生长的；生态学中与 terrestrial 直接相对。

entries.definition: Living in trees; it narrows the land habitat further and contrasts with ground-dwelling terrestrial species.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在树上的；它把陆地生境进一步收窄，与地栖的陆生物种相对。

entries.definition: Relating to a continent or to the interior of one; it names scale, while terrestrial names the medium.
entries.definitionCN: 与大陆或大陆内部有关的；它命名尺度，而 terrestrial 命名介质。

entries.definition: Belonging to this world rather than heaven; it is the theological and poetic cousin of terrestrial.
entries.definitionCN: 属于今生此世而非天界的；是 terrestrial 在神学与诗歌中的近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real terra root, real compounds and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 terra 词根、真实复合词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Terra is Latin for earth, and it also gives terrain, terrarium, territory and Mediterranean.
normal.cn: terra 是拉丁语的「大地」，也构成 terrain、terrarium、territory 与 Mediterranean。

normal.en: The fixed ecology pair is terrestrial / aquatic, dividing habitats by medium.
normal.cn: 生态学的固定配对是 terrestrial / aquatic，按介质划分生境。

normal.en: Extraterrestrial adds extra- 'outside' to the same adjective, so it means 'outside the earth'.
normal.cn: extraterrestrial 在同一形容词前加 extra-「之外」，意为「地球之外的」。

normal.en: Terrestrial planets are the rocky four: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.
normal.cn: 类地行星是四颗岩石行星：水星、金星、地球与火星。

normal.en: Subterranean puts sub- 'under' before the same terra stock, meaning 'under the earth'.
normal.cn: subterranean 在同一 terra 词族前加 sub-「在下」，意为「地下的」。

abstract.en: Picture a beetle that never touches water and a fish that never touches soil, each complete in its own element.
abstract.cn: 想象一只从不沾水的甲虫与一条从不沾土的鱼，各自在自己的元素里完整无缺。

abstract.en: Picture a globe small enough to hold, with dry land painted on it as a single colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一个可以捧在手里的地球仪，干燥陆地被涂成同一种颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a radio mast rooted in soil while a satellite floats above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根扎在土里的广播天线，而卫星在它上方漂浮。

examples.en: Terrestrial animals must conserve water in dry seasons.
examples.cn: 陆生动物在旱季必须节约用水。

examples.en: The telescope search focuses on terrestrial planets in nearby systems.
examples.cn: 这台望远镜的搜寻聚焦于邻近星系中的类地行星。

examples.en: Terrestrial carbon pools respond slowly to changes in land use.
examples.cn: 陆地碳库对土地利用变化的反应很慢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「terra（土地）+ e（的）」——terra 是土地，terrestrial 就是「属于土地的」

root: 拉丁 terrestris「大地的」= terra「干燥陆地、大地」+ -estris（形容词后缀）；terra 的更深来源不确定，与「干燥」词根的联系仅为假说。英语 terrestrial。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move outward from soil: animals, plants, the whole planet, land as opposed to sea, rocky planets, ground-based networks, the ground layer of a forest, and land ecosystems as a global category.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从土壤向外扩展：动物、植物、整个行星、与海相对的陆地、岩石行星、地面网络、森林的地面层，以及作为全球类别的陆地生态系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life and structures rooted in dry ground rather than water.
core.cn: 核心意象：扎根于干燥陆地而非水中的生命与设施。

branches.en: LAND-DWELLING LIFE: animals and plants are classified by the ground they occupy.
branches.cn: 陆生生命：动物与植物按所占地面被分类。

branches.en: LAND AS A REALM: the adjective widens from soil to the whole planet and to land transport.
branches.cn: 陆地领域：形容词从土壤扩展到整个行星与陆路运输。

branches.en: SOLID WORLDS: a rocky planet is land written at planetary scale.
branches.cn: 固体世界：岩石行星就是行星尺度的陆地。

branches.en: GROUND INFRASTRUCTURE: stations on land anchor broadcast networks.
branches.cn: 地面设施：陆地站点锚定广播网络。

branches.en: ECOLOGICAL DIVISIONS: ground versus canopy inside land, and land versus water globally.
branches.cn: 生态划分：陆地内部地面与树冠相对，全球范围内陆地与水相对。

intro.en: Terrestrial is a Latin adjective from terra, and that root also supports terrain, territory, terrarium and subterranean, while extra- builds its best-known opposite.
intro.cn: terrestrial 是由 terra 构成的拉丁形容词，这个词根还支撑 terrain、territory、terrarium 与 subterranean，而 extra- 构成它最知名的反义词。

latinIntro.en: Latin terra 'earth' and terrestris 'of the earth' are the direct ancestors; terrenus 'earthy' belongs to the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 terra「大地」与 terrestris「大地的」是直接祖形；terrenus「土质的」属于同一词族。

items.example: Terra appears in many scientific compound terms.
items.exampleCN: terra 出现在许多科学复合术语中。

items.meaning: belonging to; of the nature of
items.example: Terrestris means of the earth.
items.exampleCN: terrestris 意为大地的。

items.example: The terrestrial habitat lies above the tideline.
items.exampleCN: 陆生栖息地位于潮线之上。

items.example: The probe listens for extraterrestrial signals.
items.exampleCN: 探测器监听外星信号。

items.example: The terrain rises sharply east of the river.
items.exampleCN: 河以东的地势陡然升高。

items.example: The terrarium mimics a damp forest floor.
items.exampleCN: 饲养箱模拟湿润的森林地面。

items.example: The terrane drifted in from another plate.
items.exampleCN: 这块地体从另一板块漂移而来。

items.example: Subterranean rivers cut through the limestone.
items.exampleCN: 地下河切穿石灰岩。

items.example: The wolves defend a fixed territory.
items.exampleCN: 狼群守卫固定的领地。

definition_zh: 海的；海洋的；海生的；航海的；（名词）海军陆战队员
definition_en: relating to the sea, living in the sea, or connected with shipping and naval forces; as a noun, a soldier trained to serve at sea and on coasts
core_image: 退潮后的礁池里，海藻贴着石面，小蟹在浅水里横着走
scene: 退潮后的礁石间满是海藻和小蟹，是一处微缩的海洋群落。Between the rocks at low tide lived seaweed and crabs, a marine community in miniature.
sceneCN: 这里 marine 指「海洋的、海生的」（第 2 个义项：生活在海中的生物群落）；句意：退潮后的礁石间住着海藻与小蟹，是一个微缩的海洋群落。图中可辨识物件：礁池、贴石的海藻、小蟹、退潮留下的水线。

pos.zh: 海的；海洋的；海生的；航海的；海军的
海军陆战队员；（大写)美国海军陆战队成员

forms.label: 复数名词（海军陆战队员）

senses.title: Of the sea as an environment
senses.titleCN: 海洋环境的、与海有关的
senses.definition: relating to the sea as a physical environment, including its water, floor and shores
senses.definitionCN: 与作为物理环境的海洋有关，包括海水、海底与海岸
senses.example: The marine environment absorbs a large share of human carbon emissions.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋环境吸收了人类碳排放的很大一部分。
senses.why: Latin mare means sea, so the adjective marks the sea as a setting for any process, not only for living things.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 mare 意为「海」，因此这个形容词标记海洋作为任何过程的场景，而不只用于生物。

senses.title: Living in the sea
senses.titleCN: 海生的（海洋生物）
senses.definition: describing plants and animals that live in salt water, especially in open sea habitats
senses.definitionCN: 描述生活在咸水中、尤指开阔海域生境的动植物
senses.example: Between the rocks at low tide lived seaweed and crabs, a marine community in miniature.
senses.exampleCN: 退潮后的礁石间住着海藻与小蟹，是一个微缩的海洋群落。
senses.why: the adjective attaches to the organism by its medium, and marine contrasts with freshwater and terrestrial.
senses.whyCN: 形容词按介质附着于生物，marine 与 freshwater、terrestrial 形成对照。

senses.title: Connected with shipping and seafaring
senses.titleCN: 海运的、航海的
senses.definition: relating to ships, navigation and commerce by sea
senses.definitionCN: 与船舶、航行和海上贸易有关
senses.example: Marine insurance covers cargo lost overboard in heavy weather.
senses.exampleCN: 海运保险承保恶劣天气中落水的货物。
senses.why: sea transport is the oldest commercial use of the sea, so marine became the standard adjective in shipping and insurance law.
senses.whyCN: 海上运输是海洋最古老的商业用途，因此 marine 成为航运与保险法中的标准形容词。

senses.title: Naval and marine forces
senses.titleCN: 海军的；陆战队的
senses.definition: relating to naval forces, especially soldiers trained to fight at sea or on coasts
senses.definitionCN: 与海军力量有关，尤指受训在海上或海岸作战的士兵
senses.example: Marine units were the first to reach the flooded port.
senses.exampleCN: 海军陆战队是最先抵达被淹港口的部队。
senses.why: the noun marine 'soldier serving at sea' arose because such troops belong to the sea service, so the adjective and the soldier share one form.
senses.whyCN: 名词 marine「在海上服役的士兵」之所以出现，是因为这类部队属于海上军种，因此形容词与士兵同名。

senses.title: Of the sea floor and its deposits
senses.titleCN: 海洋地质与沉积的
senses.definition: describing sediments, rocks and layers formed on or under the sea floor
senses.definitionCN: 描述在海底或海底之下形成的沉积物、岩石与层理
senses.example: Marine sediments record thousands of years of climate change.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋沉积物记录了几千年的气候变化。
senses.why: geology needed a term for deposits laid down by water, and marine specifies salt-water basins rather than lakes.
senses.whyCN: 地质学需要指「由水沉积」的术语，marine 则进一步限定为咸水盆地而非湖泊。

senses.title: Moderate climate influenced by the sea
senses.titleCN: 受海洋调节的（海洋性气候）
senses.definition: describing a climate with small temperature swings because the sea moderates the air above it
senses.definitionCN: 描述因海洋调节其上方空气而温差较小的气候
senses.example: The island's marine climate keeps winters mild and summers cool.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的海洋性气候使冬天温和、夏天凉爽。
senses.why: climatology applies the sea adjective to places whose weather is dominated by nearby water, in contrast with continental climates.
senses.whyCN: 气候学把「海」的形容词用于受近海支配的天气，与大陆性气候相对。

senses.title: Of marine science as a discipline
senses.titleCN: 海洋科学的
senses.definition: used for the scientific study of the sea, as in marine biology, marine chemistry and marine geology
senses.definitionCN: 用于海洋科学研究，如海洋生物学、海洋化学与海洋地质学
senses.example: The station runs a marine science programme for local schools.
senses.exampleCN: 该站为本地学校开设海洋科学课程。
senses.why: each sea-related discipline prefixed its name with marine, making the adjective a stable label for a whole field.
senses.whyCN: 各门与海有关的学科都在名称前加 marine，使该形容词成为整个领域的稳定标签。

senses.title: A soldier of the marine corps
senses.titleCN: （名词）海军陆战队员
senses.definition: a member of a military force trained for operations at sea, on coasts and in amphibious landings
senses.definitionCN: 受训执行海上、海岸与两栖登陆作战任务的军人
senses.example: Two marines guarded the gangway while the cargo was checked.
senses.exampleCN: 货物检查时，两名陆战队员守着舷梯。
senses.why: the noun is a shortened form of marine soldier, and it survives as the everyday name of the corps in several navies.
senses.whyCN: 该名词是 marine soldier 的缩略，至今仍是若干海军中这支兵种的日常称呼。

intro.en: Marine comes from Latin marinus 'of the sea', from mare 'sea'. English borrowed it through Old French in the fifteenth century, and the soldier sense followed in the seventeenth.
intro.cn: marine 来自拉丁 marinus「海的」，源于 mare「海」。英语经古法语在 15 世纪借入，士兵义在 17 世纪随后出现。

items.en: Mare was the ordinary Latin word for sea. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and the Indo-European form sometimes cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: mare 是拉丁语中表示「海」的常用词。其更深来源不确定，有时为其引用的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: Marinus 'of the sea' was formed from mare, and it described sea creatures, sea water and sea-going matters.
items.cn: marinus「海的」由 mare 构成，用于描述海洋生物、海水与航海事务。

items.en: Old French marin brought the adjective into English around 1400, first in natural history and then in shipping.
items.cn: 古法语 marin 在 15 世纪初把该形容词带入英语，最初见于博物学，随后进入航运。

items.en: In the seventeenth century marine was used as a noun for soldiers raised to serve aboard ships, the origin of the modern marine corps.
items.cn: 17 世纪，marine 用作名词，指招募到舰上服役的士兵，这是现代海军陆战队的源头。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century oceanography prefixed its subfields with marine, fixing the adjective in names such as marine biology and marine geology.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪的海洋学给各分支冠以 marine，使该形容词固定出现在 marine biology、marine geology 等名称中。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin history of mare is unsettled, and the earliest English citation is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：mare 在拉丁语之前的历史无定论，英语最早书证的年代也只能大致确定。

note.en: Group one distinguishes marine from same-root words for sailors, harbours and sea law, and from a look-alike with a different root; group two contrasts it with other sea-related adjectives.
note.cn: 第一组把 marine 与同根却指水手、码头、海事法的词区分开，并辨明一个词根不同的形近词；第二组对照其它与海有关的形容词。

entries.definition: A sailor; it comes from Latin marinarius through French, so it shares mare but names a person, not a habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 水手；经法语来自拉丁 marinarius，与 mare 同源，但指人而非生境。

entries.definition: A basin for pleasure boats; the -a ending makes it a place, while marine is the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 供游艇停泊的小港；-a 词尾使它指场所，而 marine 是形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to the sea in law, trade and defence; from Latin maritimus, it is the formal legal cousin of marine.
entries.definitionCN: 在法律、贸易与防务上与海有关的；来自拉丁 maritimus，是 marine 的正式法律近亲。

entries.definition: Relating to marriage; it comes from Latin maritus 'husband', not mare 'sea', so the resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 与婚姻有关的；来自拉丁 maritus「丈夫」而非 mare「海」，因此形近只是巧合。

entries.definition: Relating to the open ocean, especially far from coasts; marine is broader and includes shelves and shores.
entries.definitionCN: 与开阔大洋有关，尤指远离海岸；marine 范围更广，包含陆架与海岸。

entries.definition: Relating to a navy and its ships; marine covers civil and biological senses as well.
entries.definitionCN: 与海军及其舰船有关的；marine 还覆盖民用与生物义。

entries.definition: Relating to sailors, ships and navigation; it stresses seamanship rather than the sea itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与水手、船舶和航行有关的；它强调航海术而非海洋本身。

entries.definition: Describing salty water or organisms in it; it names the chemical condition that marine assumes.
entries.definitionCN: 描述咸水或其中的生物；它点明 marine 所预设的化学条件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real mare root, real derivatives and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 mare 词根、真实派生词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Mare is Latin for sea, and it survives in marine, mariner, marina and maritime.
normal.cn: mare 是拉丁语的「海」，仍见于 marine、mariner、marina、maritime。

normal.en: Marine life, marine ecosystem and marine biology are the standard biology collocations.
normal.cn: marine life、marine ecosystem、marine biology 是生物学的标准搭配。

normal.en: Marine insurance and marine law keep the shipping sense alive in legal English.
normal.cn: marine insurance 与 marine law 让航运义在法律英语中延续。

normal.en: The proper noun Marine Corps explains why a soldier is simply 'a marine'.
normal.cn: 专名 Marine Corps 解释了为什么士兵直接被称为 a marine。

normal.en: Marine climate is the climatology partner of continental climate.
normal.cn: marine climate 是大陆性气候在气候学中的配对词。

abstract.en: Picture a tide pool that holds an entire ocean's logic in a bowl of water.
abstract.cn: 想象一个潮池，用一盆水装下整片大洋的逻辑。

abstract.en: Picture a cargo crate whose insurance policy never leaves the shore.
abstract.cn: 想象一只货箱，它的保单从未离开海岸。

abstract.en: Picture a soldier trained on a beach, halfway between land and sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一名在海滩受训的士兵，站在陆地与海洋之间。

examples.en: Marine plastic debris accumulates in mid-ocean gyres.
examples.cn: 海洋塑料垃圾在洋流环流中积聚。

examples.en: The marine climate keeps the island green through winter.
examples.cn: 海洋性气候让这座岛整个冬天保持绿色。

examples.en: Marines secured the dock before the aid ships arrived.
examples.cn: 海军陆战队员在救援船到达前控制了码头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mare（海）+ ine」——mare 是海，marine 就是「海的、海里的」；大写 Marine 又一跃成了陆战队员

root: 拉丁 marinus「海的」= mare「海」+ -inus（形容词后缀）；mare 的更深来源不确定。英语 marine；同族有 mariner、maritime、marina。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one body of salt water: the sea as environment, the life in it, shipping, naval troops, sea-floor deposits, sea-moderated climate, marine science, and finally the soldier whose name is the noun form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一片咸水辐射开来：作为环境的海洋、其中的生命、海运、海军部队、海底沉积、受海调节的气候、海洋科学，最后是以名词形式出现的陆战队员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the salt sea as a place, a medium and a service.
core.cn: 核心意象：咸海既是场所，也是介质，也是服役对象。

branches.en: SEA AS HABITAT: the adjective marks both the setting and the organisms in it.
branches.cn: 海作为生境：形容词既标场景，也标其中的生物。

branches.en: SEA AS ROUTE: shipping and insurance turn the sea into infrastructure.
branches.cn: 海作为航线：航运与保险把海变成基础设施。

branches.en: SEA AS SERVICE: naval troops and the marine corps make the adjective a rank and a noun.
branches.cn: 海作为军务：海军部队与陆战队使形容词兼作军种名与名词。

branches.en: SEA AS OBJECT OF STUDY: sediments and marine science name what is examined.
branches.cn: 海作为研究对象：沉积物与海洋科学指出被考察之物。

branches.en: SEA AS CLIMATE FORCE: nearby water moderates the air above it.
branches.cn: 海作为气候力量：近旁的水调节其上方的空气。

intro.en: Marine is built on the Latin noun mare 'sea' plus -inus; the same root yields mariner, marina, maritime and the submarine, while sub- and mariculture extend it in modern technical words.
intro.cn: marine 由拉丁名词 mare「海」加 -inus 构成；同一词根衍生 mariner、marina、maritime 与 submarine，而 sub- 与 mariculture 在现代技术词中加以扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin mare 'sea', marinus 'of the sea' and maritimus 'of the coast' are the core ancestors of the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mare「海」、marinus「海的」与 maritimus「海岸的」是这一英语词族的核心祖形。

items.example: Mare is the base of the whole English sea family.
items.exampleCN: mare 是整个英语「海」词族的基础。

items.example: Marinus means belonging to the sea.
items.exampleCN: marinus 意为属于海的。

items.example: Marine algae anchor the coastal food web.
items.exampleCN: 海洋藻类支撑着海岸食物网。

items.example: The mariner read the sky before setting out.
items.exampleCN: 水手出发前先看天色。

items.example: The marina sheltered twenty small boats.
items.exampleCN: 游艇码头停泊着二十条小船。

items.meaning: relating to the sea in law and trade
items.example: Maritime law governs the salvage claim.
items.exampleCN: 海事法管辖这项打捞请求。

items.meaning: a vessel that travels under the sea
items.example: The submarine surfaced beyond the reef.
items.exampleCN: 潜艇在礁石外浮出水面。

items.example: Mariculture rafts cover the sheltered bay.
items.exampleCN: 海水养殖筏铺满受庇护的海湾。

items.example: She studied marine biology at the coastal station.
items.exampleCN: 她在海岸观测站学习海洋生物学。

definition_zh: 淡水；淡水的；淡水生的；内陆水域的；（口语）无经验的水手
definition_en: water that is not salty, found in rivers, lakes and streams; living in or relating to such water
core_image: 山间溪流清澈见底，绕过石头向下流去，远处是咸涩的海湾
scene: 山间的溪流清澈见底，一路向下，与海湾的咸水完全不同。The mountain stream runs clear, a freshwater source far above the salty bay.
sceneCN: 这里 freshwater 指「不咸的淡水」（第 1 个义项：河流湖泊中的非咸水水体）；句意：山间溪流清澈，是一处远高于咸水海湾的淡水源。图中可辨识物件：清浅溪流、溪石、山坡、远处的海湾。

pos.zh: 淡水（河流、湖泊中的非咸水）
淡水的；淡水生的；内陆水域的

senses.title: Water that is not salty
senses.titleCN: 不咸的水（淡水水体）
senses.definition: water with very little dissolved salt, as found in rivers, lakes, ponds and most streams
senses.definitionCN: 溶解盐分极少的水，见于河流、湖泊、池塘与多数溪流
senses.example: The mountain stream runs clear, a freshwater source far above the salty bay.
senses.exampleCN: 山间溪流清澈，是一处远高于咸水海湾的淡水源。
senses.why: the compound simply names water that is fresh in the old sense 'not salt', so the defining contrast is salinity, not temperature or cleanliness.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词只是命名「fresh」旧义「不咸」的水，界定性对照是盐度，而非温度或洁净程度。

senses.title: Living in non-salty water
senses.titleCN: 生活在淡水中的（形容词）
senses.definition: describing organisms that live in rivers and lakes rather than in the sea
senses.definitionCN: 描述生活在河流湖泊而非海中的生物
senses.example: Freshwater snails graze the algae on the pond stones.
senses.exampleCN: 淡水螺啃食池石上的藻类。
senses.why: the noun is used attributively before organism names, turning a water type into a habitat label.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接置于生物名称前作定语，把一种水型变成生境标签。

senses.title: Inland water systems as a whole
senses.titleCN: 内陆水域系统的
senses.definition: relating to the connected rivers, lakes, wetlands and groundwater of the land, as opposed to the sea
senses.definitionCN: 与陆地上相连的河流、湖泊、湿地和地下水有关，与海洋相对
senses.example: Freshwater systems store less water than oceans but support far more species per litre.
senses.exampleCN: 淡水系统储水远少于海洋，但每升水支持的物种却多得多。
senses.why: hydrology and ecology use the adjective for the whole inland network, because its parts exchange water and organisms.
senses.whyCN: 水文学与生态学用这个形容词指整个内陆网络，因为其各部分交换水与生物。

senses.title: Fresh water as a resource
senses.titleCN: 作为资源的淡水
senses.definition: the drinkable or irrigation water that people extract from rivers, lakes and aquifers
senses.definitionCN: 人们从河流、湖泊与含水层取用的饮用水或灌溉水
senses.example: The city's freshwater supply comes from a single upland reservoir.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的淡水供应来自一座高地水库。
senses.why: policy and engineering treat the same water as a stock to be allocated, so the word shifts from medium to commodity.
senses.whyCN: 政策与工程把同一种水当作可分配的存量，词义因此从介质转为商品。

senses.title: Freshwater fishing and farming
senses.titleCN: 淡水渔业与养殖
senses.definition: relating to the catching or farming of fish and other organisms in rivers, lakes and ponds
senses.definitionCN: 与在河流、湖泊、池塘中捕捞或养殖鱼类及其它生物有关
senses.example: Freshwater aquaculture now exceeds capture fishing in several provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 在若干省份，淡水养殖已超过捕捞渔业。
senses.why: the resource sense narrows to an industry, and the compound becomes an ordinary adjective in fisheries economics.
senses.whyCN: 资源义收窄为一种产业，这个复合词便成为渔业经济中的普通形容词。

senses.title: A freshwater sailor: an inexperienced one
senses.titleCN: 习语：没出过海的新手水手
senses.definition: informal, a sailor who has never been to sea, or more generally a person with no experience of a place
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指从未出过海的水手，更泛指对某地毫无经验的人
senses.example: The crew soon saw that the new hand was a freshwater sailor.
senses.exampleCN: 船员们很快看出这个新手是个没出过海的人。
senses.why: fresh water is the opposite of the sailor's element, so calling a sailor freshwater is a mild insult about inexperience.
senses.whyCN: 淡水是水手所处元素的反面，因此把水手称作 freshwater 是对其缺乏经验的轻度讥讽。

senses.title: Freshwater ecology as a category
senses.titleCN: 淡水生态学中的分类范畴
senses.definition: used in ecology and conservation to classify studies and species by low-salinity habitat
senses.definitionCN: 生态学与保护学中按低盐度生境对研究与物种进行分类
senses.example: The report separates freshwater from marine species in its extinction estimates.
senses.exampleCN: 报告在灭绝估计中把淡水物种与海洋物种分开统计。
senses.why: conservation planning needs a category between land and sea, and freshwater fills that gap as a technical label.
senses.whyCN: 保护规划需要陆与海之间的类别，freshwater 作为技术标签正好填补这一空档。

senses.title: The two-word open form
senses.titleCN: 分写形式 fresh water 的用法
senses.definition: the open spelling fresh water, used when the phrase is a plain noun and the salt contrast is being stated directly
senses.definitionCN: 分写形式 fresh water，用于普通名词短语、并直接陈述「不咸」这一对照时
senses.example: The tide pushed fresh water far up the channel after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨后，潮水把淡水推到了河道的很上游。
senses.why: English often keeps a compound open while it still feels like a phrase; the closed form freshwater has become the technical adjective.
senses.whyCN: 当一个复合词仍像短语时，英语常保持分写；闭合形式 freshwater 则成了技术形容词。

intro.en: Freshwater is an English compound of fresh, in its old sense 'not salt', and water. The adjective is Germanic, while the modern sense 'new, lively' was reinforced by Old French fres.
intro.cn: freshwater 是英语复合词，由 fresh（旧义「不咸」）与 water 构成。fresh 属日耳曼语，而现代「新鲜、有活力」义受古法语 fres 影响而加强。

items.en: Old English fersc meant 'not salt' and was used of water long before it meant 'new'; the salt contrast is the oldest sense.
items.cn: 古英语 fersc 意为「不咸」，早在表示「新」之前就用于水；不咸这一对照是最古老的义项。

items.en: The adjective goes back to a Germanic form such as *friskaz, whose own pre-Germanic origin is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 该形容词可追溯到 *friskaz 之类的日耳曼语形式，其日耳曼语之前的来源属重构而非有记录。

items.en: Old French fres 'fresh, new, eager' reinforced the newer sense of English fresh, which is why the word now means both 'not salt' and 'new'.
items.cn: 古法语 fres「新鲜、新、急切」加强了英语 fresh 较新的义项，因此这个词如今既指「不咸」也指「新」。

items.en: Freshwater appears from the late Middle English period as a compound naming inland, drinkable water, and later as an adjective before organism names.
items.cn: freshwater 自中古英语晚期出现，作为复合词指内陆可饮之水，后来又用作生物名称前的形容词。

items.en: In modern ecology and fisheries the closed form freshwater became a technical label opposed to marine and terrestrial.
items.cn: 在现代生态学与渔业中，闭合形式 freshwater 成为与 marine、terrestrial 相对的技术标签。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Germanic shape of fresh is a reconstruction, and the earliest compound citation is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：fresh 的日耳曼语之前形态属重构，复合词最早书证的年代也只能大致确定。

note.en: Group one separates the closed compound from its open spelling and from three words built on the same fresh root; group two contrasts it with neighbouring water categories.
note.cn: 第一组区分闭合复合词与分写形式，并辨明三个同出 fresh 词根的词；第二组对照相邻的水类词语。

entries.definition: The two-word phrase for non-salty water; the closed form freshwater is preferred when the word works as a technical adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指不咸之水的两词短语；当该词作技术形容词时，更常用闭合形式 freshwater。

entries.definition: A sudden rise of water in a stream, especially from rain or melting snow; it shares fresh but names a flood event.
entries.definitionCN: 溪流因降雨或融雪突然涨水；与 fresh 同源，但指一次洪水事件。

entries.definition: To make someone or something feel new again; re- 'again' plus fresh, so it is about renewal, not salinity.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人或某物重新恢复精神；由 re-「再」加 fresh 构成，讲的是更新而非盐度。

entries.definition: A first-year student; fresh here means 'new', so the compound has nothing to do with water.
entries.definitionCN: 一年级新生；此处 fresh 意为「新」，因此该复合词与水无关。

entries.definition: Located away from the coast; it names position, while freshwater names salinity.
entries.definitionCN: 位于远离海岸之处；它命名位置，而 freshwater 命名盐度。

entries.definition: Relating to lakes; it is a narrower technical term inside the freshwater category.
entries.definitionCN: 与湖泊有关的；是淡水范畴内更窄的专门术语。

entries.definition: Relating to rivers and their banks; another narrow member of the freshwater family.
entries.definitionCN: 与河流及其河岸有关的；淡水词族中另一个较窄的成员。

entries.definition: Water containing much dissolved salt; it is the exact antonym that defines freshwater by contrast.
entries.definitionCN: 含大量溶解盐的水；它正是通过对照界定 freshwater 的反义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real fresh and water roots, real compounds and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 fresh 与 water 词根、真实复合词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Fresh in freshwater is the old sense 'not salt', not the modern sense 'newly picked'.
normal.cn: freshwater 中的 fresh 是旧义「不咸」，不是现代「刚采摘的」之义。

normal.en: Freshwater fish, freshwater lake and freshwater marsh are the standard field-guide collocations.
normal.cn: freshwater fish、freshwater lake、freshwater marsh 是野外图鉴的标准搭配。

normal.en: The open form fresh water appears when the phrase is a plain noun phrase.
normal.cn: 当它只是普通名词短语时，用分写形式 fresh water。

normal.en: Freshwater sailor is a fixed idiom for someone who has never been to sea.
normal.cn: freshwater sailor 是固定习语，指从未出过海的人。

normal.en: Ecology pairs freshwater with marine and terrestrial as the three basic habitat labels.
normal.cn: 生态学把 freshwater 与 marine、terrestrial 并列为三个基本生境标签。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of clear water carried down from a mountain, never having touched the sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯从山上带下的清水，从未碰过海水。

abstract.en: Picture a sailor who knows every rope but has never seen a wave larger than a bathtub's.
abstract.cn: 想象一个熟悉每根绳索、却没见过比浴缸更大的浪的水手。

abstract.en: Picture a map where a blue vein runs inland and stops just before the coast.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，一条蓝色细流伸向内陆，在海岸前止住。

examples.en: Freshwater wetlands filter pollutants before they reach the river.
examples.cn: 淡水湿地在污染物进入河流之前将其过滤。

examples.en: The lake holds the largest freshwater reserve in the region.
examples.cn: 这座湖拥有该地区最大的淡水储量。

examples.en: Only a freshwater sailor would moor there without checking the tide.
examples.cn: 只有没出过海的新手才会不查潮汐就把船停在那里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fresh（不咸的、新鲜的）+ water（水）」——不咸的水就是淡水

root: 英语复合词：fresh（古英语 fersc「不咸」，后受古法语 fres「新」影响）+ water（古英语 wæter「水」）；无拉丁语来源，latinEntries 留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from a simple chemical fact, low salinity, and then spread: water itself, the organisms in it, the inland network, the resource, the fishery, the idiom about inexperienced sailors, the ecological category, and finally the open two-word spelling.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一条简单的化学事实「低盐度」出发，随后铺开：水本身、其中的生物、内陆水网、资源、渔业、关于新手水手的习语、生态分类，最后是分写的两词形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: clear water that has never met the sea.
core.cn: 核心意象：从未与海相遇的清甜之水。

branches.en: THE WATER ITSELF: the noun and its open spelling both name low-salinity water.
branches.cn: 水本身：名词与分写形式都指低盐度的水。

branches.en: LIFE AND SYSTEMS: organisms and the connected inland network are labelled by the medium.
branches.cn: 生命与系统：生物与相连的内陆水网按介质被命名。

branches.en: WATER AS STOCK: supply and aquaculture treat fresh water as a resource and an industry.
branches.cn: 水作为存量：供水与养殖把淡水当作资源与产业。

branches.en: INEXPERIENCE: the landlubber idiom borrows the sailor's opposite element as an insult.
branches.cn: 缺乏经验：陆上人的习语借用与水手相反的元素作讥讽。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION: ecology uses the word as one of three basic habitat labels.
branches.cn: 分类：生态学把它用作三个基本生境标签之一。

intro.en: Freshwater is a native English compound, not a Latin derivative. Its parts are the adjective fresh and the noun water, and the same parts build freshet, refresh, freshness and freshwater compounds.
intro.cn: freshwater 是英语本族复合词，并非拉丁派生词。其构件是形容词 fresh 与名词 water，同样的构件还构成 freshet、refresh、freshness 以及各类 freshwater 复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source. Latin aqua dulcis 'sweet water' translates the idea but is not a cognate, so latinEntries is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源。拉丁 aqua dulcis「甜水」只是语义对应，并非同源，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.example: Fresh water gathers in the upland ponds.
items.exampleCN: 淡水积聚在高地池塘里。

items.example: Water carries dissolved salts downstream.
items.exampleCN: 水把溶解的盐带向下游。

items.example: Freshwater species cannot survive in the bay.
items.exampleCN: 淡水物种无法在海湾中存活。

items.meaning: a fish of rivers and lakes
items.example: Freshwater fish dominate the upper river.
items.exampleCN: 淡水鱼在河流上游占多数。

items.meaning: a wetland fed by non-salty water
items.example: The freshwater marsh floods every spring.
items.exampleCN: 这片淡水沼泽每年春天泛滥。

items.meaning: a small flood of fresh water
items.example: A spring freshet cut the road for a day.
items.exampleCN: 春季涨水把道路冲断了一天。

items.example: The freshness of the spring water surprised them.
items.exampleCN: 泉水的清冽让他们惊讶。

items.example: A cold drink refreshed the hikers.
items.exampleCN: 一杯冷饮让徒步者恢复了精神。

items.meaning: a pearl grown by a river mussel
items.example: Freshwater pearls are cultured in shallow ponds.
items.exampleCN: 淡水珍珠在浅池塘中养殖。
