senses.title: Water with much dissolved salt
senses.titleCN: 含大量溶解盐的水（咸水）
senses.definition: water in which a large amount of salt is dissolved, as in the sea or in salt lakes
senses.definitionCN: 溶解了大量盐分的水，如海水或咸水湖
senses.example: The tide pushed saltwater into the fields beside the river mouth, and the rice leaves turned yellow.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水把咸水推进河口旁的田里，稻叶因此发黄。
senses.why: the compound names water by its salt content, so the defining measure is salinity, not the presence of any particular mineral.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词按含盐量命名水，界定尺度是盐度，而非某种特定矿物。

senses.title: Sea water as opposed to fresh water
senses.titleCN: 海水（与淡水相对）
senses.definition: the water of the ocean, used especially when contrasting it with river or lake water
senses.definitionCN: 海洋中的水，尤用于与河流或湖泊的淡水对照时
senses.example: The channel mixes saltwater and river water twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 这条水道每天两次混合海水与河水。
senses.why: seawater is the prototype of salty water, so the compound works as a plain synonym in everyday and technical writing.
senses.whyCN: 海水是咸水的原型，因此这个复合词在日常与技术写作中可作普通同义词。

senses.title: Marine organisms kept in salty water
senses.titleCN: 生活在咸水中的（海生生物）
senses.definition: describing fish, plants and invertebrates that live in sea water rather than fresh water
senses.definitionCN: 描述生活在海水而非淡水中的鱼、植物与无脊椎动物
senses.example: Saltwater fish must drink constantly to avoid dehydrating.
senses.exampleCN: 海水鱼必须不断饮水，以免脱水。
senses.why: the adjective before organism names turns salinity into a habitat label, contrasting with freshwater species.
senses.whyCN: 置于生物名称前作定语时，这个词把盐度变成生境标签，与淡水物种相对。

senses.title: Saltwater aquaculture and aquariums
senses.titleCN: 海水养殖与水族饲养
senses.definition: relating to the farming or tank keeping of marine organisms
senses.definitionCN: 与海水生物的养殖或水族箱饲养有关
senses.example: The saltwater section of the hatchery rears two native shrimp species.
senses.exampleCN: 孵化场的海水区养育着两种本地虾。
senses.why: hobby and industry both need a short label for the saline half of their work, and saltwater fills it.
senses.whyCN: 爱好与产业都需要一个简短标签指其工作的咸水部分，saltwater 正好填补。

senses.title: Brine used in cooking or industry
senses.titleCN: 烹饪或工业用的盐水
senses.definition: strongly salted water used to preserve food or as an industrial fluid
senses.definitionCN: 用于腌制食物或作为工业流体的高盐浓度水
senses.example: The olives were cured in saltwater for three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 橄榄在盐水中腌了三周。
senses.why: the same salt-and-water idea narrows to a prepared brine, where salt is added deliberately rather than geologically present.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「盐加水」的概念收窄为人工配制的盐水，盐是刻意加入的，而非地质存在。

senses.title: Salt water invading a freshwater aquifer
senses.titleCN: 海水入侵（咸水侵入淡水层）
senses.definition: the movement of salty water into coastal groundwater or soils, usually because of overpumping or sea-level rise
senses.definitionCN: 咸水进入沿海地下水或土壤，通常因过量抽水或海平面上升
senses.example: Saltwater intrusion has forced two farms to abandon their wells.
senses.exampleCN: 海水入侵迫使两家农场废弃了水井。
senses.why: the technical sense turns the compound into a named process, where saltwater is the agent and fresh groundwater the victim.
senses.whyCN: 技术义把这个复合词变成一个有名目的过程：咸水是施动者，淡水地下水是受害者。

senses.title: Saline wetlands and lagoons
senses.titleCN: 咸水湿地与潟湖环境
senses.definition: describing coastal marshes, lagoons and pools whose water is brackish or fully salty
senses.definitionCN: 描述水体微咸或全咸的海岸沼泽、潟湖与水池
senses.example: Saltwater marshes absorb storm surge better than sea walls do.
senses.exampleCN: 咸水沼泽比海堤更能吸收风暴潮。
senses.why: coastal ecology uses the adjective for transition zones, where the water is salty enough to exclude most freshwater plants.
senses.whyCN: 海岸生态学用这个形容词指过渡带，那里的咸度足以排除多数淡水植物。

senses.title: A saltwater sailor: an experienced one
senses.titleCN: 习语：真正出过海的老水手
senses.definition: informal, a sailor with long experience of the open sea, as opposed to a freshwater sailor
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指长期在开阔海域航行的老水手，与 freshwater sailor 相对
senses.example: The old saltwater sailor knew the reef by the colour of the water.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老水手能凭水色辨认礁石。
senses.why: salt water is the sailor's true element, so the idiom marks genuine sea experience, mirroring the insult freshwater sailor.
senses.whyCN: 咸水是水手真正的元素，因此这一习语标记真实的海上经验，正好与 freshwater sailor 的讥讽相对。

intro.en: Saltwater is an English compound of salt and water, both native Germanic words. Salt has a genuine Latin cognate in sal, but the English word does not descend from Latin, so no Latin source is claimed.
intro.cn: saltwater 是 salt 与 water 构成的英语复合词，两者都是日耳曼语本族词。salt 与拉丁 sal 确实是同源词，但英语这个词并非由拉丁语派生，因此不称其有拉丁来源。

items.en: Old English sealt 'salt' is the direct ancestor; the noun and the adjective shared one form, as they still do in part.
items.cn: 古英语 sealt「盐」是直接祖形；名词与形容词曾共用一词形，至今仍部分如此。

items.en: The Germanic form *saltaz and the Indo-European base *sal- are reconstructions supported by many related languages, but no single recorded ancestor exists.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式 *saltaz 与印欧语词根 *sal- 都是靠多种亲属语言支持的重构，并不存在单一有记录的祖形。

items.en: Latin sal 'salt' belongs to the same *sal- family, so saline and salinity are cognates of salt rather than its source.
items.cn: 拉丁 sal「盐」属于同一 *sal- 词族，因此 saline 与 salinity 是 salt 的同源词，而非其来源。

items.en: Salt water appears as a plain phrase from the Middle English period, and the closed form saltwater later became the technical adjective.
items.cn: salt water 自中古英语时期便作为普通短语出现，闭合形式 saltwater 后来成为技术形容词。

items.en: The phrase saltwater sailor is recorded in the nineteenth century as the positive counterpart of freshwater sailor.
items.cn: saltwater sailor 这一短语在 19 世纪有记载，是 freshwater sailor 的正面对应说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Germanic and Indo-European forms are reconstructions, and the earliest compound citation is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：日耳曼语之前与印欧语的形式均属重构，复合词最早书证的年代也只能大致确定。

note.en: Group one separates the closed compound from its open spelling and from words built on the salt stock with different referents; group two contrasts it with other saline-water terms.
note.cn: 第一组区分闭合复合词与分写形式，并辨明同出 salt 词族却指别物的词；第二组对照其它咸水词语。

entries.definition: The two-word phrase for salty water; the closed form saltwater is usual when the word modifies another noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指咸水的两词短语；当该词修饰另一名词时，通常用闭合形式 saltwater。

entries.definition: Containing salt, or a salt solution used medically; it comes from Latin salinus, a cognate rather than the source of saltwater.
entries.definitionCN: 含盐的，或医用的盐溶液；来自拉丁 salinus，是 saltwater 的同源词而非其来源。

entries.definition: A thin crisp cracker made with a little salt; the salt root is shared but the referent is food.
entries.definitionCN: 加少量盐的薄脆饼干；盐词根相同，所指却是食物。

entries.definition: Potassium nitrate, a mineral used in gunpowder and fertiliser; its second element is not water, so the resemblance to saltwater is partial.
entries.definitionCN: 硝酸钾，用于火药与肥料；其第二部分并非 water，因此与 saltwater 只是部分形近。

entries.definition: Water of the ocean, typically about three and a half percent salt; it is the concrete case that saltwater generalises.
entries.definitionCN: 海洋中的水，盐度通常约百分之三点五；它是 saltwater 所概括的具体原型。

entries.definition: Water saturated or nearly saturated with salt; it is stronger than ordinary saltwater and usually made deliberately.
entries.definitionCN: 被盐饱和或接近饱和的水；比普通咸水更浓，通常是人工配制的。

entries.definition: Slightly salty, as where river water mixes with sea water; it is weaker than saltwater and marks a transition.
entries.definitionCN: 略咸的，如河水与海水混合处；比 saltwater 淡，标记的是过渡状态。

entries.definition: Water with little dissolved salt; it is the exact antonym that gives saltwater its meaning by contrast.
entries.definitionCN: 溶解盐分很少的水；它正是通过对照赋予 saltwater 意义的反义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real salt and water roots, real compounds and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 salt 与 water 词根、真实复合词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Salt plus water gives the compound, and the open form salt water is still common in ordinary prose.
normal.cn: salt 加 water 构成该复合词，普通散文中仍常见分写形式 salt water。

normal.en: Saltwater fish, saltwater marsh and saltwater intrusion are the standard technical collocations.
normal.cn: saltwater fish、saltwater marsh、saltwater intrusion 是标准技术搭配。

normal.en: Saline and salinity come from Latin sal, a cognate of English salt rather than its ancestor.
normal.cn: saline 与 salinity 来自拉丁 sal，是英语 salt 的同源词而非其祖形。

normal.en: The idiom saltwater sailor marks real sea experience, the opposite of freshwater sailor.
normal.cn: 习语 saltwater sailor 标记真实的海上经验，与 freshwater sailor 相反。

normal.en: Saltwater intrusion names the process by which the sea moves into coastal wells.
normal.cn: saltwater intrusion 指海水侵入沿海水井的过程。

abstract.en: Picture a field turning pale as the tide quietly salts the roots.
abstract.cn: 想象潮水悄悄给根系上盐，田地一点点褪成枯黄。

abstract.en: Picture an old sailor who can taste the reef before he sees it.
abstract.cn: 想象一位老水手，还没看见礁石就先尝出了它的味道。

abstract.en: Picture a well that draws up the sea instead of the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一口井抽上来的不是雨水，而是海水。

examples.en: Saltwater covers most of the planet's surface but is unfit to drink.
examples.cn: 咸水覆盖了地球表面的大部分，却不能饮用。

examples.en: The marsh is fed by saltwater at every high tide.
examples.cn: 每次涨潮，咸水都会灌入这片沼泽。

examples.en: Overpumping the coastal wells invited saltwater intrusion.
examples.cn: 过量抽取沿海水井招来了海水入侵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「salt（盐）+ water（水）」——加了盐的水就是咸水；真正出过海的老水手也叫 saltwater sailor

root: 英语复合词：salt（古英语 sealt「盐」，日耳曼语 *saltaz，与拉丁 sal 同源）+ water（古英语 wæter）；英语词本身无拉丁来源，latinEntries 留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the salt: water itself, the sea, its organisms, aquaculture, prepared brine, the invasion of coastal aquifers, saline wetlands, and finally the old sailor whose element is salt water.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「盐」展开：水本身、海水、其中的生物、海水养殖、人工盐水、沿海含水层入侵、咸水湿地，最后是以咸水为元素的老水手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water carrying enough salt to exclude ordinary life and ordinary crops.
core.cn: 核心意象：含盐量足以排除寻常生命与农作物的水。

branches.en: SALTY WATER ITSELF: the compound names the medium and its largest natural body.
branches.cn: 咸水本身：复合词命名介质及其最大的天然水体。

branches.en: LIFE AND CULTURE: organisms and their farming are labelled by salinity.
branches.cn: 生命与养殖：生物及其养殖按盐度被命名。

branches.en: BRINE: salt is added on purpose, turning water into a tool.
branches.cn: 盐水：盐被刻意加入，水变成工具。

branches.en: SALINE LANDSCAPES: intrusion and coastal marshes show salt water moving into land.
branches.cn: 咸水景观：入侵与海岸沼泽显示咸水向陆地推进。

branches.en: THE SAILOR'S ELEMENT: experience at sea is named by the water itself.
branches.cn: 水手的元素：海上经验直接以这种水命名。

intro.en: Saltwater is a native English compound whose parts, salt and water, also build saltwater fish, saltwater intrusion, saline, salty and salinity; the Latin sal is a cognate, not an ancestor.
intro.cn: saltwater 是英语本族复合词，其构件 salt 与 water 还构成 saltwater fish、saltwater intrusion、saline、salty 与 salinity；拉丁 sal 是同源词而非祖形。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word is the source of saltwater. Latin sal 'salt' is a genuine cognate through Indo-European *sal-, and salinus yields English saline, but neither is an ancestor of this compound.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁词是 saltwater 的来源。拉丁 sal「盐」经印欧语 *sal- 确为同源词，salinus 衍生英语 saline，但两者都不是这个复合词的祖形。

items.meaning: sodium chloride; to preserve with salt
items.example: Salt preserves fish for months.
items.exampleCN: 盐能把鱼保存数月。

items.example: Water dissolves the salt in the estuary.
items.exampleCN: 水溶解河口处的盐。

items.example: Saltwater corrodes the old hull.
items.exampleCN: 海水腐蚀着旧船体。

items.example: Saltwater fish drink sea water continuously.
items.exampleCN: 海水鱼不断饮用海水。

items.example: Saltwater intrusion ruined three wells.
items.exampleCN: 海水入侵毁了三口水井。

items.meaning: a tidal marsh of salty water
items.example: Saltwater marsh grass holds the mud in place.
items.exampleCN: 咸水沼泽的草固定住泥滩。

items.example: The wind left a salty film on the windows.
items.exampleCN: 海风在窗上留下一层盐膜。

items.meaning: the amount of salt in water
items.example: Salinity rises where the river flow falls.
items.exampleCN: 河流流量下降处盐度上升。

items.example: The nurse hung a bag of saline.
items.exampleCN: 护士挂上一袋生理盐水。

definition_zh: 海洋的；大洋的；远洋的；（气候）大洋性的；大洋洲语族的；广阔如海的
definition_en: of or relating to the ocean, especially the open sea far from land; (of climate) controlled by the sea; belonging to the Oceanic branch of languages; figuratively, vast like the sea
core_image: 一片没有陆影的开阔蓝水，涌浪从水天线一路压来，船在正中缩成一个小点
scene: 科考船驶出最后一列岛影，四周只剩水天相接的蓝，涌浪从每个方向压来。Once the last island sank from view, the swell came from every direction and the crew knew the water was oceanic.
sceneCN: 这里 oceanic 指「与远离陆地的开阔海域有关的」（第 2 个义项：远洋的、远离陆地的开阔海域）；句意：最后一座岛屿从视野中消失后，涌浪从四面八方涌来，船员知道这里已是远洋水域。图中可辨识物件：灰蓝色的涌浪、空荡的水天线、船尾的白浪、低垂的云层。

pos.zh: 海洋的；大洋的；远洋的（远离陆地、与开阔海域有关）
（气候、地区）大洋性的，受海洋调节、温差小、湿度大

collocations.zh: 大洋性气候（受海洋调节、温差小的气候）
大洋岛（远离大陆的火山岛或珊瑚岛）
大洋区（远离海底与岸边的水层）
大洋洲语族（太平洋岛屿上的一组语言）

derivatives.zh: 海洋；大洋（去掉形容词后缀的基础名词）
大洋洲（由同一希腊词根构成的专名）

senses.title: Belonging to the ocean
senses.titleCN: 海洋的、属于海洋的（总义）
senses.definition: relating to the ocean as a whole, or belonging to it rather than to the land
senses.definitionCN: 指与整个海洋有关的，或属于海洋而非陆地的
senses.example: The report compares oceanic and continental weather patterns.
senses.exampleCN: 报告比较了大洋与大陆的天气模式。
senses.why: the suffix -ic turns the noun ocean into an adjective of belonging, so this is the broad classifying sense from which the narrower ones fall out.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ic 把名词 ocean 变成表示归属的形容词，这是最宽的分类义，其余义项由此收窄而来。

senses.title: Open sea far from land
senses.titleCN: 远洋的、远离陆地的开阔海域
senses.definition: of the deep open water beyond the shelf, where no land is in sight
senses.definitionCN: 指大陆架以外、看不见陆地的深水开阔海域
senses.example: Beyond the shelf the trawler entered oceanic water.
senses.exampleCN: 拖网渔船越过大陆架，进入远洋水域。
senses.why: the ocean is defined against the coast here: distance from land and depth, not salt alone, make the water oceanic.
senses.whyCN: 这里以海岸为参照来定义：远离陆地、水深，而不只是含盐，才使水域成为远洋。

senses.title: Sea-dominated climate
senses.titleCN: （气候）大洋性的、受海洋调节的
senses.definition: of a climate controlled by the sea, with a small annual temperature range and abundant moisture
senses.definitionCN: 指受海洋控制、年温差小、湿度大的气候
senses.example: Cool summers and mild winters mark an oceanic climate.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季凉爽、冬季温和是大洋性气候的特征。
senses.why: water heats and cools slowly, so a coast facing the sea has mild extremes; the adjective transfers the sea's thermal habit to the air.
senses.whyCN: 水体升温降温都慢，面海的沿岸因此极端值小；这个形容词把海洋的调温习性移到了空气上。

senses.title: Born in the deep basin
senses.titleCN: 大洋岛屿与洋壳的（地质地理义）
senses.definition: formed within the deep ocean basin, as volcanic islands or basaltic crust far from any continent
senses.definitionCN: 指在深海盆地内形成的，如远离大陆的火山岛或玄武岩洋壳
senses.example: Hawaii sits on oceanic crust far from any continent.
senses.exampleCN: 夏威夷位于远离大陆的大洋地壳之上。
senses.why: the adjective marks origin: rock and islands made at sea, in contrast with continental crust and shelf islands.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记来源：在海中生成的岩石与岛屿，与大陆地壳及陆架岛相对。

senses.title: Of ocean science
senses.titleCN: 海洋学的、海洋科学研究的
senses.definition: belonging to the scientific study of the sea, its physics, chemistry, geology and life
senses.definitionCN: 指属于对海洋的科学研究，包括其物理、化学、地质与生物
senses.example: The institute publishes oceanic data from drifting buoys.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究所发布漂流浮标传回的大洋数据。
senses.why: once the sea became an object of measurement, the adjective attached to surveys, data and instruments rather than to the water itself.
senses.whyCN: 海洋成为测量对象之后，这个形容词便附着于调查、数据与仪器，而不只是水面。

senses.title: The Oceanic language family
senses.titleCN: 大洋洲语族的（语言学义）
senses.definition: belonging to the branch of the Austronesian family spoken on the islands of the western and central Pacific
senses.definitionCN: 指属于南岛语系中分布在太平洋中西部岛屿的一支
senses.example: Oceanic languages are spoken from Papua New Guinea to Polynesia.
senses.exampleCN: 大洋洲语族的使用范围从巴布亚新几内亚直到波利尼西亚。
senses.why: here the word is a capitalised family name; the sea is the territory that defines the group, so the same adjective serves linguistics.
senses.whyCN: 此处是首字母大写的语族专名；海洋是划定该群体的地域，因此同一个形容词也用于语言学。

senses.title: Vast and sea-like
senses.titleCN: 广阔如海的（修辞义）
senses.definition: used figuratively for something so wide, open or deep that it suggests the ocean
senses.definitionCN: 比喻极宽广、开阔或深沉，令人想到海洋的事物
senses.example: An oceanic silence filled the empty hall.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵如海般深广的寂静充满了空荡的大厅。
senses.why: the figure keeps only the ocean's scale and openness, dropping salt and water, which is why it can describe sound, space or feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻只保留海洋的尺度与开阔，舍弃盐与水，因此能形容声音、空间或情绪。

senses.title: The pelagic zone
senses.titleCN: 大洋生态区（水层区）
senses.definition: of the open-water layer of the sea, away from both the bottom and the shore, where plankton and swimming animals live
senses.definitionCN: 指海中远离海底与岸边的开阔水层，浮游生物与游泳动物生活其中
senses.example: Tuna hunt across the oceanic zone from dawn to dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 金枪鱼从黎明到黄昏在大洋水层区捕食。
senses.why: ecology cuts the sea into zones; the open-water zone takes the adjective because it is the part defined by distance from solid surfaces.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把海划分为若干区；开阔水层区之所以用这个形容词，是因为它正是以远离固体表面来界定的部分。

intro.en: Oceanic comes from Latin oceanicus, an adjective built on oceanus, which in turn borrowed Greek ōkeanos, the name of the stream believed to encircle the world. The Latin adjective reached English through French océanique in the seventeenth century; the deeper Greek origin is not settled.
intro.cn: oceanic 来自拉丁形容词 oceanicus，后者由 oceanus 构成，而 oceanus 借自希腊语 ōkeanos——古人想象中环绕大地的巨流之名。这个拉丁形容词经法语 océanique 于 17 世纪进入英语；希腊语的更深来源尚无定论。

items.en: Ōkeanos named the great river that was thought to run around the inhabited world, and by extension the outer sea beyond it.
items.cn: ōkeanos 指古人想象中环绕已知世界的大河，并引申指其外的外海。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as oceanus, keeping both the encircling-stream reading and the plain sense 'the outer sea'.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊词借作 oceanus，同时保留「环绕之流」与外海的两层意思。

items.en: The adjective oceanicus 'of the ocean' was formed on oceanus with the suffix -icus, and it passed into French as océanique.
items.cn: 形容词 oceanicus「海洋的」由 oceanus 加后缀 -icus 构成，并传入法语作 océanique。

items.en: French océanique carried the adjective into English in the seventeenth century, where oceanic first appears in learned description of the open sea.
items.cn: 法语 océanique 于 17 世纪把这个形容词带入英语，oceanic 最初出现在描写开阔海域的学术文字中。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the adjective settled into geology, climatology and linguistics, giving oceanic crust, oceanic climate and the Oceanic languages.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，这个形容词在地质学、气候学与语言学中固定下来，形成大洋地壳、大洋性气候与大洋洲语族等术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper Greek origin and exact first date): the pre-Greek form of ōkeanos is not established, and suggestions that it is a Pre-Greek or non-Indo-European word are hypotheses; any earlier form offered is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（希腊语更深词源与确切首见年代）：ōkeanos 的前希腊语形式未得到证明，认为它属前希腊语层或非印欧语的看法均属假说；凡给出的更早形式都是重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close and are all built on the same Greek root, so each entry states what it refers to instead of calling it unrelated. Group two holds genuine near-synonyms that differ in range or register.
note.cn: 第一组的词拼写或读音接近，且都出自同一个希腊词根，因此每条都说明它实际所指，而不把它说成无关词。第二组是范围或语体有差的真近义词。

entries.definition: The sea as a whole, and the noun from which oceanic is formed by adding -ic; same Greek source, different word class.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个海洋，也是加 -ic 构成 oceanic 的基础名词；希腊来源相同，词性不同。

entries.definition: Of Oceania or its peoples; it is built on the continent name, not on the sea, though both go back to the same Greek word.
entries.definitionCN: 指大洋洲或其居民的；它由洲名构成而非直接由海洋，但两者都回溯到同一个希腊词。

entries.definition: One of the sea nymphs said to be daughters of Oceanus; the same root, but a mythical being rather than a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指传说中俄刻阿诺斯的女儿们，即海中仙女；词根相同，但指神话人物而非性质。

entries.definition: An older synonym of oceanography, built with -logy; same root, but it names a discipline rather than describing the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 海洋学的旧称，用 -logy 构成；词根相同，但指一门学科而非描述海洋。

entries.definition: Of the sea and its life or shipping; it is the everyday general adjective, while oceanic stresses the open, deep sea.
entries.definitionCN: 指海洋及其生物或航运的；它是日常通行的总称形容词，而 oceanic 强调开阔深海。

entries.definition: Of the sea in relation to trade, navigation and law; it is used of fleets, ports and statutes, not of water depth.
entries.definitionCN: 指与海运、航海和法律有关的海洋事务；多用于船队、港口与法规，不用于水深。

entries.definition: Of the open water column away from the bottom; it is the technical term closest to the ecological sense of oceanic.
entries.definitionCN: 指远离海底的开阔水层；是与 oceanic 生态义最接近的术语。

entries.definition: Situated or operating at sea away from the shore; it measures distance from land rather than naming the ocean itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指位于或作业于离岸海上的；它衡量离陆地的距离，而非指海洋本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real terms and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的术语与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Learn ocean and oceanic as one pair: the noun names the sea, the -ic adjective says what belongs to it.
normal.cn: 把 ocean 与 oceanic 当一对来记：名词指海洋，加 -ic 的形容词说明什么属于海洋。

normal.en: Oceanic climate is the standard label for the mild, wet, small-range climate of west coasts in the middle latitudes.
normal.cn: 大洋性气候是温带西岸温和多雨、温差小这一气候的标准说法。

normal.en: Geology contrasts oceanic crust with continental crust, so the adjective marks where rock was born.
normal.cn: 地质学把大洋地壳与大陆地壳对立，因此这个形容词标记岩石生成的地方。

normal.en: Oceanic languages is capitalised because it is a family name inside the Austronesian group.
normal.cn: 大洋洲语族首字母大写，因为它是南岛语系内部的一个语族专名。

normal.en: The adverb oceanically is rare; most writing says 'in oceanic conditions' instead.
normal.cn: 副词 oceanically 很少见；多数文字改说 in oceanic conditions 这样的短语。

abstract.en: Picture a map with no coast anywhere near the middle: only blue, and the ship a needle point.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，中部附近没有任何海岸，只有蓝色，船只是一个针尖大的点。

abstract.en: Picture a hall so wide and still that standing in it feels like standing on open water.
abstract.cn: 想象一个又宽又静的大厅，站在里面像站在开阔水面上。

abstract.en: Picture island chains thrown up from the sea floor, each a dot of land in a vast basin.
abstract.cn: 想象一串串从海底隆起的群岛，每一座都是巨大盆地里的一个陆点。

examples.en: Oceanic islands often lack the mammals found on continents.
examples.cn: 大洋岛往往缺少大陆上才有的哺乳动物。

examples.en: The west of Ireland has a mild oceanic climate.
examples.cn: 爱尔兰西部属温和的大洋性气候。

examples.en: Researchers tagged the fish in oceanic water far beyond the shelf.
examples.cn: 研究人员在远离大陆架的远洋水域给鱼挂上标记。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oceanic」读似「欧申尼克」——前两音像「欧申」，后一音像「尼克」，连起来就是「大海的尼克」，专管大洋的事

root: 希腊 ōkeanos「环绕大地的大河、外海」→ 拉丁 oceanus → 拉丁形容词 oceanicus → 英语 oceanic（17 世纪）；希腊语更早形式来源不确定，前希腊语层之说属假说，非定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all answer one question: does this belong to the sea rather than the land? The answer widens from the ocean as a whole to open water, then narrows into climate, crust, science, a language family, a figure of vastness and finally a named ecological zone.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在回答同一个问题：这东西属于海洋而不属于陆地吗？答案从整个海洋放宽到开阔水域，再收窄到气候、洋壳、科学、语族、如海的修辞，最后落到一个有名称的生态分区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: open blue water with no land in sight, swell arriving from every direction.
core.cn: 核心意象：看不见陆地的开阔蓝水，涌浪从四面八方压来。

branches.en: BROAD CLASS: anything belonging to the sea rather than to the land.
branches.cn: 总类：凡属于海洋而非陆地的事物。

branches.en: OPEN WATER: the deep sea and its drifting life occupy the same habitat.
branches.cn: 开阔水域：深海与其漂流生物占据同一个生境。

branches.en: CLIMATE: the sea moderates temperature and keeps the air moist.
branches.cn: 气候：海洋调节温度，使空气湿润。

branches.en: GEOLOGY: islands and crust born in the deep basin.
branches.cn: 地质：岛屿与地壳在深海盆地中生成。

branches.en: EXTENSIONS: a science, a language family and a figure of vastness borrow the adjective.
branches.cn: 延伸：一门学科、一个语族与一种如海的修辞都借用了这个形容词。

intro.en: Oceanic is ocean plus the relational suffix -ic. The family grows with Greek-based combining forms such as -graphy and -arium, and with prefixes that locate the sea: inter- and trans-.
intro.cn: oceanic 是 ocean 加关系后缀 -ic。其词族靠 -graphy、-arium 这类希腊来源的组合成分扩展，也靠标明海域位置的前缀 inter- 与 trans- 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The chain is Greek ōkeanos, Latin oceanus and the Latin adjective oceanicus. Latin also kept Oceanides, the Greek name of the sea nymphs, as a borrowed plural.
latinIntro.cn: 链条是希腊 ōkeanos、拉丁 oceanus 与拉丁形容词 oceanicus。拉丁语还把希腊的海中仙女之名 Oceanides 作为借词复数保留下来。

items.example: The ocean covers most of the planet.
items.exampleCN: 海洋覆盖了这颗行星的大部分。

items.example: The buoy drifted into oceanic water.
items.exampleCN: 浮标漂进了远洋水域。

items.meaning: the scientific study of the sea
items.example: She studied oceanography in Bergen.
items.exampleCN: 她在卑尔根攻读海洋学。

items.meaning: a specialist in the study of the sea
items.example: An oceanographer read the salinity profile.
items.exampleCN: 一位海洋学家解读了盐度剖面。

items.example: The canal is an interoceanic route.
items.exampleCN: 这条运河是一条连接两大洋的航路。

items.example: Transoceanic cables carry most data traffic.
items.exampleCN: 跨洋电缆承载了大部分数据流量。

items.example: Oceanfront lots cost more than inland ones.
items.exampleCN: 临海地块比内陆地块贵。

items.meaning: a large building displaying marine life
items.example: The oceanarium holds a million litres of sea water.
items.exampleCN: 这座大型水族馆蓄有百万升海水。

items.example: Oceanian scholars attended the congress.
items.exampleCN: 大洋洲学者出席了这次大会。

latinEntries.meaning: the ocean; the stream encircling the world

latinEntries.structure: oceanicus, oceanica, oceanicum (adjective, first and second declension)
Oceanides (f., plural, Greek loanword in Latin)
latinEntries.meaning: the sea nymphs, daughters of Oceanus
latinEntries.meaningCN: 海中仙女，俄刻阿诺斯的女儿们

definition_zh: 海岸的；沿海的；沿岸的；海岸带的
definition_en: relating to the coast, the land along the edge of the sea, or to the strip where land and sea meet
core_image: 一条窄窄的陆带贴着海走，内侧是农田与公路，外侧是不断拍岸的白浪
scene: 公路沿着盐沼与沙丘之间的低地延伸，尽头是一座渡口。The road ran through coastal marsh and dune before it reached the ferry.
sceneCN: 这里 coastal 指「沿海的、位于海岸边的」（第 2 个义项：坐落在海岸边或沿海地带的）；句意：公路穿过沿海的盐沼与沙丘，最后到达渡口。图中可辨识物件：盐沼水面、白色沙丘、贴着岸线的公路、渡口栈桥。

pos.zh: 海岸的；沿海的；沿岸的（位于海岸或与海岸有关的）
海岸带的（涉及其生态、工程、管理与规划的）

derivatives.zh: 海岸；沿海地区 / 沿岸航行；（车）滑行
海岸线（整条岸线的走向与轮廓）
沿海航船；杯垫（在桌面滑行的垫片）
海岸警卫队；海岸巡防人员

senses.title: Of the coast
senses.titleCN: 海岸的、与海岸有关的（总义）
senses.definition: relating to the coast, the margin of land that borders the sea
senses.definitionCN: 指与海岸有关的，即与陆地临海边缘有关
senses.example: Coastal roads flood at every spring tide.
senses.exampleCN: 每逢大潮，沿海公路都会积水。
senses.why: the suffix -al makes a relational adjective out of coast, so the word simply says 'having to do with the coast'.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把 coast 变成关系形容词，这个词的基本意思就是「与海岸有关的」。

senses.title: Situated on the shore
senses.titleCN: 沿海的、坐落在海岸边的
senses.definition: situated on or along the shore, as a town, road or plain
senses.definitionCN: 指位于海岸之上或沿海岸延伸的，如城镇、公路、平原
senses.example: Coastal towns grew quickly after the railway arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路通了以后，沿海城镇迅速发展起来。
senses.why: this is the local reading: the adjective marks position relative to the sea, not a subject matter.
senses.whyCN: 这是位置义：形容词标记相对于海的位置，而不是某个主题。

senses.title: Coastal ecology
senses.titleCN: 海岸生态的（盐沼、红树、沙丘等生境）
senses.definition: of the habitats where land and sea meet, such as salt marsh, mangrove, dune and rock pool
senses.definitionCN: 指陆海相接处的生境，如盐沼、红树林、沙丘与岩池
senses.example: Coastal wetlands filter runoff before it reaches the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸湿地在径流入海之前将其过滤。
senses.why: the same adjective now qualifies habitats rather than places, because ecology treats that strip as a distinct system.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词现在修饰生境而非地点，因为生态学把这条窄带视为独特系统。

senses.title: Coastal engineering and defence
senses.titleCN: 海岸工程与防护的
senses.definition: of structures built to hold or protect the shore, such as sea walls, groynes, breakwaters and revetments
senses.definitionCN: 指为固定或保护海岸而建的构筑物，如海堤、丁坝、防波堤与护坡
senses.example: Coastal defences failed during the winter storm.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季风暴期间，海岸防护设施失效。
senses.why: once people build against the sea, the adjective attaches to the works rather than to the land.
senses.whyCN: 人们一旦对着海建造，这个形容词便附着于工程物而非陆地。

senses.title: Coastal communities and economy
senses.titleCN: 沿海居民与沿海经济的
senses.definition: of the people, work and income that depend on the shore, such as fishing, shipping and tourism
senses.definitionCN: 指依赖海岸的人、生计与收入，如渔业、航运与旅游
senses.example: Coastal economies depend on both fishing and visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海经济同时依赖渔业与游客。
senses.why: from the place the adjective passes to the people in it: a coastal town is also a town whose living comes from the sea.
senses.whyCN: 形容词由地点过渡到地点上的人：沿海城镇同时也是靠海为生的城镇。

senses.title: Alongshore navigation
senses.titleCN: 沿岸航行的、近岸水域的
senses.definition: of sailing or shipping that keeps close to land, in the belt of water near the shore
senses.definitionCN: 指贴近陆地航行，或在近岸水带中营运的航运
senses.example: Coastal shipping declined once the motorway opened.
senses.exampleCN: 高速公路通车后，沿岸航运衰落了。
senses.why: the nautical sense keeps the original 'side' idea: the ship works along the edge of the land, not across open sea.
senses.whyCN: 航海义保留了原初的「侧边」意念：船沿着陆地边缘航行，而非横穿外海。

senses.title: Coastal zone management
senses.titleCN: 海岸带管理的（政策与规划义）
senses.definition: of the planning, law and policy that govern the strip where sea and land interact
senses.definitionCN: 指管理陆海相互作用地带的规划、法律与政策
senses.example: Coastal management balances building, farming and habitat.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸带管理在建设、农业与生境之间取得平衡。
senses.why: administration turns the physical strip into a jurisdiction, so the adjective comes to name a field of rules.
senses.whyCN: 行政管理把这条实体窄带变成管辖对象，这个形容词因而指一个规则领域。

senses.title: Coastal climate
senses.titleCN: 沿海气候的、受海岸影响的
senses.definition: of the weather of the shore, shaped by sea breeze and by the sea's slow change of temperature
senses.definitionCN: 指海岸地带的天气，受海风与海水缓慢变温影响
senses.example: Coastal air stays cooler than inland air in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季沿海空气比内陆空气凉爽。
senses.why: the sea beside the land moderates it, so the adjective can describe air as well as ground.
senses.whyCN: 紧邻陆地的海对陆地起调节作用，因此这个形容词也能形容空气而不只是地面。

intro.en: Coastal is coast plus the relational suffix -al. Coast reached English through Old French coste from Latin costa 'rib, side'; the 'shore' sense developed in the Romance languages from the idea of a flank or side. The adjective itself is recorded from the early nineteenth century, and the deeper origin of costa is unsettled.
intro.cn: coastal 是 coast 加关系后缀 -al。coast 经古法语 coste 来自拉丁 costa「肋骨、侧面」；「海岸」义在罗曼语族中由「侧边、侧面」的意思发展而来。该形容词本身在 19 世纪初见于记载，而 costa 的更深来源尚无定论。

items.en: Costa meant 'rib' and, by extension, 'side or wall'; the shore reading is not the classical core but grew later out of 'side, edge'.
items.cn: costa 意为「肋骨」，并引申为「侧面、壁」；「海岸」义并非古典时期的核心义，而是后来由「侧边、边缘」发展出来的。

items.en: Old French coste carried both 'rib' and 'side, slope, shore'; this is the form English borrowed, and Italian costa shows the same shift.
items.cn: 古法语 coste 同时有「肋骨」与「侧面、坡、岸」两义；英语借入的就是这个形式，意大利语 costa 也呈现同样的词义转移。

items.en: English coast is recorded in the fourteenth century for the land edge by the sea, and the verb 'to sail along a coast' follows from it.
items.cn: 英语 coast 在 14 世纪以「临海陆缘」义见于记载，动词「沿岸航行」由此派生。

items.en: The Latin suffix -alis, through French -al, makes relational adjectives; coast plus -al yields the plain meaning 'of the coast'.
items.cn: 拉丁后缀 -alis 经法语 -al 构成关系形容词；coast 加 -al 就得到「海岸的」这一基本意思。

items.en: Coastal is recorded in the early nineteenth century, when coastal survey, coastal trade and coastal defence became routine terms of administration and commerce.
items.cn: coastal 在 19 世纪初见于记载，当时海岸测量、沿岸贸易与海岸防护已成为行政与商业的常用说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of costa and first date of coastal): the pre-Latin form of costa is not established, and any suggested root is a reconstruction; the earliest citation of coastal is only approximately dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（costa 的更深词源与 coastal 的首见年代）：costa 的拉丁语之前形式未得到证明，所拟词根均属重构形式；coastal 的最早书证只有约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike or homophonous words: costal and coastal share one Latin root but went opposite ways, while coast, coastline and coaster are built on the same base. Group two holds true near-synonyms that differ in register or in what part of the edge they name.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或同音词：costal 与 coastal 共用同一个拉丁词根却走向不同，coast、coastline、coaster 则同出一个基础词。第二组是真近义词，差别在语体或所指的岸的哪一部分。

entries.definition: Of the ribs, as in costal cartilage; it is cognate with coastal through Latin costa, but it kept the anatomical sense and never means 'shore'.
entries.definitionCN: 指肋骨的，如肋软骨；它经拉丁 costa 与 coastal 同源，但保留了解剖义，从不表示「海岸」。

entries.definition: The shore itself, and the verb 'to sail along it' or 'to move without power'; same root as coastal, but a noun or verb rather than an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指海岸本身，也指「沿岸航行」或「滑行」的动词；与 coastal 同根，但为名词或动词而非形容词。

entries.definition: The coast considered as a line, especially its shape on a map or over a long stretch; same base, but a compound noun with a geometric image.
entries.definitionCN: 指被看作一条线的海岸，尤其地图上或长距离上的走向；基础词相同，但为带几何意象的复合名词。

entries.definition: A ship that trades along a coast, or a small mat that slides on a table; same root, but it names an object, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿岸贸易的船，或桌上滑动的杯垫；词根相同，但指具体物件而非性质。

entries.definition: Of the shore zone between high and low water and just beyond it; it is the technical ecology term, coastal being the general one.
entries.definitionCN: 指高低潮之间及其外侧的滨岸带；是生态学的术语，coastal 则是通称。

entries.definition: Of the sea in relation to shipping, trade and law; it stresses activity at sea, while coastal stresses position on land.
entries.definitionCN: 指与海运、贸易和法律有关的海洋事务；它强调海上活动，coastal 强调陆上位置。

entries.definition: Of the shore as a place for holidays; it is informal and leisure-oriented, unlike the neutral and technical coastal.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为度假地的海滨；语气随意、偏向休闲，与中性的技术词 coastal 不同。

entries.definition: Situated or working at sea away from the shore; it points outward from the coast rather than lying on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指位于或作业于离岸海上的；它从海岸指向外海，而不是位于岸上。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real collocations of the word, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Coastal is the adjective of coast: the noun names the edge, the adjective says what belongs to or sits on it.
normal.cn: coastal 是 coast 的形容词：名词指那条边缘，形容词说明什么属于它或位于它之上。

normal.en: 'Coastal erosion' and 'coastal defence' usually appear together, because defence is the response to erosion.
normal.cn: 海岸侵蚀与海岸防护常常成对出现，因为防护正是对侵蚀的回应。

normal.en: Coastal plain is a standard landform term: low land built up along a shore by sediment.
normal.cn: 海岸平原是标准的地貌术语：由沉积物沿岸堆积成的低地。

normal.en: Coastal waters is the legal and ecological phrase for the belt of sea nearest the land.
normal.cn: 近岸海域是法律与生态上的固定说法，指紧邻陆地的海带。

normal.en: The base verb coast also means to move without engine power, a meaning that grew from sailing along a shore.
normal.cn: 基础动词 coast 还表示不用动力滑行，这个义项由沿岸航行发展而来。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow ribbon of land with fields on one side and white surf on the other, and a road running down its middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一条窄窄的陆带，一侧是农田，一侧是白色浪花，中间一条公路直贯而下。

abstract.en: Picture a town whose harbour, boats and income all face the same direction, out to sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城镇，港口、船只与收入都朝向同一个方向，即外海。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of stone set against the waves, with grass already growing behind it where the sea used to reach.
abstract.cn: 想象一道石墙迎着浪，墙后原本海水到过的地方已经长出了草。

examples.en: The coastal plain is low, flat and built of river sediment.
examples.cn: 海岸平原地势低平，由河流沉积物堆积而成。

examples.en: Coastal waters are warmer and often greener than the open sea.
examples.cn: 近岸海域比外海温暖，颜色也常常更绿。

examples.en: New rules limit building along the coastal strip.
examples.cn: 新规定限制了海岸地带的建设。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「coastal」读似「扣斯头」——「扣」住海岸，「斯头」听着像石头，石头扣在岸上，就是海岸的

root: 拉丁 costa「肋骨、侧面」→ 古法语 coste「肋骨；侧面、岸」→ 中古英语 coast「海岸」→ 加 -al 成 coastal；costa 的更深来源不确定，所拟词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place something on the narrow strip where land meets sea. The adjective first marks the edge itself, then position, habitat, works, people, navigation, rules and finally air, so the coast becomes a place to live on, build on, sail past and govern.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某样东西放在陆海相接的窄带上。这个形容词先标记边缘本身，再依次标记位置、生境、工程、居民、航行、规则，最后是空气，于是海岸成了居住、建造、航行与治理的对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow strip of land with the sea on one side and fields on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条窄陆带，一侧是海，另一侧是田野。

branches.en: PLAIN RELATION: the adjective simply marks what belongs to the coast.
branches.cn: 基本关系：形容词只标记什么属于海岸。

branches.en: OCCUPIED EDGE: towns, jobs and incomes sit on the strip.
branches.cn: 有人居住的边缘：城镇、工作与收入都落在这条带上。

branches.en: LIVING EDGE: salt marsh, mangrove and dune form one habitat.
branches.cn: 活的边缘：盐沼、红树林与沙丘构成同一个生境。

branches.en: DEFENDED EDGE: walls and breakwaters try to hold the line.
branches.cn: 设防的边缘：海堤与防波堤试图固定这条线。

branches.en: WORKING EDGE: shipping, planning law and sea air all describe uses of the coast.
branches.cn: 使用中的边缘：航运、规划法规与海风都描述海岸的用途。

intro.en: Coastal is coast plus -al. The family runs from the bare noun coast through the compound coastline and the agent-like coaster to prefixed forms such as intercoastal, which locate activity between or along coasts.
intro.cn: coastal 是 coast 加 -al。其词族从光杆名词 coast，经复合词 coastline 与指物的 coaster，一直到 intercoastal 这类加前缀的形式，用于标明活动发生于海岸之间或沿岸。

latinIntro.en: Latin costa 'rib, side' is the source of coast, and -alis, through French -al, supplies the adjective ending. The anatomical sense survived in costal, which is why the same root yields two very different words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 costa「肋骨、侧面」是 coast 的来源，-alis 经法语 -al 提供形容词词尾。解剖义保留在 costal 中，这正是同一词根产生两个差别很大的词的原因。

items.meaning: the shore; to sail along it
items.example: The coast bends west beyond the headland.
items.exampleCN: 海岸在岬角之外向西弯去。

items.example: A coastal path follows the cliffs.
items.exampleCN: 一条沿海小径贴着悬崖延伸。

items.meaning: the coast seen as a line
items.example: The coastline retreats a metre a year here.
items.exampleCN: 这里的海岸线每年后退一米。

items.meaning: a coastal trading ship; a table mat
items.example: A coaster unloaded salt at the quay.

definition_zh: 海岸线；岸线；水陆交界线；（湖泊、水库的）岸线
definition_en: the line where water meets the land, especially along the sea, a lake or a reservoir; also the strip of land and shallow water on either side of that line
core_image: 一条湿沙与干草之间的细线沿着水面弯过去，浪痕刚留在沙上，又被下一道浪抹平
scene: 风暴过后，牧场外的浅滩被水推开了一道新的边，水与草的分界换了位置。After the storm a new shoreline curved across the flooded pasture.
sceneCN: 这里 shoreline 指「水与陆地相交的那条线」（第 1 个义项：水陆交界的那条线）；句意：风暴过后，一条新的岸线蜿蜒穿过被淹的牧场。图中可辨识物件：浅水边缘的湿泥、被水推倒的草、弯曲的水痕、低矮的围栏。

pos.zh: 海岸线；岸线；水陆交界线（可指海、湖、水库）
岸带（交界线两侧的陆地与浅水地带）

senses.title: The water's edge as a line
senses.titleCN: 水陆交界的那条线（海岸线）
senses.definition: the line along which the surface of a sea, lake or other water body meets the land
senses.definitionCN: 海水、湖水等水体表面与陆地相接的那条线
senses.example: The shoreline moved a few metres inland after the winter storms.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季风暴过后，岸线向内陆移动了几米。
senses.why: the compound joins a place word to a geometric one, so the referent is not the wet ground but the boundary drawn along it.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把一个地点词与一个几何词连接起来，所指不是湿地面，而是沿其画出的界线。

senses.title: The shore as a strip
senses.titleCN: 岸带：交界线两侧的陆地与浅水
senses.definition: the belt of land and shallow water on either side of that line, treated as one zone
senses.definitionCN: 交线两侧的陆地与浅水地带，被当作一个整体区域
senses.example: The shoreline zone supports reeds, shellfish and young fish.
senses.exampleCN: 岸带生境养育芦苇、贝类与幼鱼。
senses.why: ecology and planning widen the line into a zone, because processes on land and in water act on each other across the belt.
senses.whyCN: 生态学与规划把这条线放宽为一个带，因为陆上与水中的过程在这条带上相互作用。

senses.title: Lake and reservoir edge
senses.titleCN: 湖岸线与水库岸线（非海洋水体）
senses.definition: the corresponding edge of a lake, reservoir or impounded river, which may rise and fall with the water level
senses.definitionCN: 湖泊、水库或拦河蓄水体的相应边缘，会随水位升降而移动
senses.example: The reservoir shoreline drops sharply each dry season.
senses.exampleCN: 每逢旱季，水库岸线都会大幅下退。
senses.why: line in the compound is neutral about salt water, so the word covers any standing water body with a defined edge.
senses.whyCN: 复合词里的线一词对咸淡并无限定，因此凡有明确边缘的静水体都能用它。

senses.title: Erosion and shifting
senses.titleCN: 岸线侵蚀与迁移
senses.definition: the retreat, advance or reshaping of that line under waves, currents, tides and sediment supply
senses.definitionCN: 在波浪、水流、潮汐与泥沙供给作用下，这条线的后退、前进或改变形状
senses.example: Groynes were built to slow shoreline erosion.
senses.exampleCN: 人们修建丁坝以减缓岸线侵蚀。
senses.why: a line that can be mapped can also be measured over time, so the noun becomes the object of erosion studies.
senses.whyCN: 可以画在图上的一条线也能随时间测量，于是这个名词成了侵蚀研究的对象。

senses.title: Length and shape
senses.titleCN: 岸线长度与形态（测量义）
senses.definition: the measured length and outline of the line, including its curves, headlands and inlets
senses.definitionCN: 这条线的实测长度与轮廓，包括弯折、岬角与湾口
senses.example: The survey recorded a shoreline of eleven kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 测量记录到的岸线长度为十一公里。
senses.why: once the edge is treated as a curve, its length depends on the scale of measurement, which is why shoreline figures are often qualified.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把边缘当作曲线，其长度就取决于测量尺度，因此岸线数值常需注明条件。

senses.title: Shoreline planning and law
senses.titleCN: 岸线规划与管理（政策义）
senses.definition: the planning, rules and permits that decide what may be built or done along that line
senses.definitionCN: 决定沿线可以建造什么、可以做什么的规划、规则与许可
senses.example: Shoreline management plans set new building back from the water.
senses.exampleCN: 岸线管理规划要求新建筑从水边后退。
senses.why: administration needs a fixed object to regulate, so the physical line becomes a legal boundary with setbacks and permits.
senses.whyCN: 行政管理需要一个固定的管制对象，于是实体线变成带有退让距离与许可的法律边界。

senses.title: Shoreline vegetation and habitat
senses.titleCN: 岸线植被与生态
senses.definition: the plants and animals living along the edge, from dune grass and reeds to mangrove and nesting birds
senses.definitionCN: 沿边缘生活的植物与动物，从沙丘草、芦苇到红树林与筑巢鸟类
senses.example: Shoreline vegetation held the sand in place during the gale.
senses.exampleCN: 大风期间，岸线植被把沙固定住了。
senses.why: the strip sense narrows again to its living cover, since roots at the edge are what bind sediment and shelter young animals.
senses.whyCN: 岸带义再收窄到其活体覆盖层，因为正是边缘的根系固定沉积物并庇护幼小动物。

senses.title: The traced outline on maps
senses.titleCN: 地图与影像上的岸线轮廓（制图义）
senses.definition: the drawn or photographed outline of that boundary on maps, charts and aerial images
senses.definitionCN: 在地图、海图与航拍影像上画出的或拍下的该界线轮廓
senses.example: The old chart shows a shoreline now buried under the port.
senses.exampleCN: 旧海图上画出的岸线如今已被港口压在下面。
senses.why: a map must fix one moment of a moving edge, so the noun also names the printed contour rather than the place itself.
senses.whyCN: 地图必须把移动的边缘固定在某一时刻，因此这个名词也指印出的轮廓，而非地点本身。

intro.en: Shoreline is an English compound of shore and line, recorded in the nineteenth century when coastal surveys began mapping the water's edge. Line descends from Latin linea 'thread, plumb line' through Old French. Shore's own origin is unsettled: it is often linked to Middle Low German schore, but that remains a hypothesis.
intro.cn: shoreline 是 shore 与 line 的英语复合词，19 世纪海岸测量开始测绘水边时见于记载。line 经古法语来自拉丁 linea「线、铅垂线」。shore 本身的来源尚无定论：常被联系到中古低地德语 schore，但这仍属假说。

items.en: Shore in the sense 'land bordering a large body of water' is recorded about 1300; English did not inherit it from Old English, which used other words for the coast.
items.cn: shore 以「邻接大片水体的陆地」义约在 1300 年见于记载；英语并未从古英语继承这个词，古英语用别的词表示海岸。

items.en: The usual suggestion is Middle Low German schore 'shore, bank' or Middle Dutch scorre 'land washed by the sea'; the forms are close, but the borrowing route is unproved.
items.cn: 常见的说法是它来自中古低地德语 schore「岸、滩」或中古荷兰语 scorre「受海冲刷的陆地」；词形相近，但借入途径未得到证明。

items.en: Line goes back to Latin linea 'string, linen thread, plumb line', a derivative of linum 'flax', and to the verb lineare 'to make straight'.
items.cn: line 可回溯到拉丁 linea「绳、亚麻线、铅垂线」，由 linum「亚麻」派生，并关联动词 lineare「使成直线」。

items.en: Old French ligne carried the word into Middle English, where line meant both a cord and a drawn mark.
items.cn: 古法语 ligne 把这个词带入中古英语，line 同时指绳索与画出的记号。

items.en: Shoreline is recorded in the nineteenth century, when hydrographic surveys needed a word for the mapped edge of the water.
items.cn: shoreline 在 19 世纪见于记载，当时水文测量需要一个词来指被测绘的水边界线。

items.en: Source uncertain (shore's origin and shoreline's first date): shore's pre-English source is unsettled and the Low German link is only a hypothesis; the earliest citation of shoreline is approximately dated, and any reconstructed ancestor is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（shore 的来源与 shoreline 的首见年代）：shore 在英语之前的来源无定论，与低地德语的关联仅为假说；shoreline 的最早书证只有约略年代，凡重构的祖形均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds spelling-similar words: shore and its compounds share the first element, while shoring is a homonym from a separate word and is not related at all. Group two holds true near-synonyms that differ in scale, water type or register.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写相近的词：shore 及其复合词共享第一个成分，而 shoring 来自另一个同形异义词，完全不同源。第二组是真近义词，差别在尺度、水体类型或语体。

entries.definition: The land along the edge of a sea or lake; the first element of shoreline, but it names the land, not the boundary line.
entries.definitionCN: 指海或湖边缘的陆地；是 shoreline 的第一个成分，但它指陆地，而不是界线。

entries.definition: Timber or metal props holding up a wall, trench or ship; it belongs to a separate verb shore 'to prop', so it has no connection with the coast.
entries.definitionCN: 指支撑墙体、沟槽或船体的木料或金属撑柱；它属于另一个动词 shore「支撑」，与海岸毫无关联。

entries.definition: A bird that feeds along the water's edge, such as a sandpiper; same first element, but it names an animal, not a line.
entries.definitionCN: 指在水边觅食的鸟，如鹬；第一个成分相同，但指动物而非线。

entries.definition: Towards the shore; same first element, but the suffix makes it a direction word rather than a boundary noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指向岸的方向；第一个成分相同，但后缀使它成为方向词而非界线名词。

entries.definition: The edge of the sea seen as a continuous line, often over a long stretch or on a map; shoreline is more local and also covers lakes.
entries.definitionCN: 指被看作连续线的海缘，常指长距离或地图上的走向；shoreline 更局部，也可指湖泊。

entries.definition: The raised edge of a river or channel; it is the usual word for rivers, while shoreline is usual for seas, lakes and reservoirs.
entries.definitionCN: 指河流或水道隆起的边缘；河岸通常用这个词，而海岸、湖岸与水库岸线通常用 shoreline。

entries.definition: The sloping strip of sand or stones at the water's edge; it names the material surface, while shoreline names the boundary itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指水边由沙或砾石构成的斜坡带；它指物质表面，shoreline 指界线本身。

entries.definition: A literary or archaic word for the shore, especially the ground left bare by the tide; it is poetic where shoreline is technical.
entries.definitionCN: 指岸的书面或古旧说法，尤指退潮后露出的地面；它是诗语，而 shoreline 偏技术。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real collocations of the word, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Break the word into its two real parts: shore is the land edge, line is the boundary, and the compound names the boundary itself.
normal.cn: 把词拆成两个真实成分：shore 是陆地边缘，line 是界线，复合词指的就是这条界线。

normal.en: Shoreline change is the standard research term for the measured retreat or advance of the edge.
normal.cn: shoreline change 是衡量岸线后退或前进的标准研究说法。

normal.en: Shoreline management plans are legal documents in many countries, which shows how a physical line becomes policy.
normal.cn: 岸线管理规划在许多国家是有法律效力的文件，这说明一条实体线如何变成政策对象。

normal.en: A reservoir shoreline moves up and down every year, a fact that reminds you the word is not limited to the sea.
normal.cn: 水库岸线每年上下移动，这提醒你这个词并不限于海洋。

normal.en: Shoreline vegetation is the planting used in coastal restoration, because roots at the edge hold sediment.
normal.cn: 岸线植被是海岸修复中采用的种植方式，因为边缘的根系能固定沉积物。

abstract.en: Picture a wet line drawn on sand, erased by the next wave and drawn again a little further in.
abstract.cn: 想象湿沙上画着一条线，下一道浪把它抹掉，又在稍里侧重新画出来。

abstract.en: Picture a map where the blue and the green touch along one thin contour, and that contour is the whole subject.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，蓝与绿沿着一条细轮廓相接，而这条轮廓就是全部主题。

abstract.en: Picture houses set back from the water while the line between water and land creeps towards them year by year.
abstract.cn: 想象房屋从水边后退，而水陆之间的那条线年复一年向它们爬来。

examples.en: The shoreline shifted inland after three days of high waves.
examples.cn: 三天大浪之后，岸线向内陆移动了。

examples.en: Reeds along the shoreline shelter young fish from the current.
examples.cn: 岸线边的芦苇为幼鱼遮挡水流。

examples.en: The lake shoreline is lowest at the end of the dry season.
examples.cn: 旱季末尾，湖岸线退到最低处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「shoreline」读似「秀来恩」——「秀」像岸，「来恩」像一条线，岸上来了线，就是岸线

root: 英语复合词，由 shore + line 构成。shore 来源不确定，一般认为与中古低地德语 schore「岸、滩」、中古荷兰语 scorre 有关，属假说；line 来自拉丁 linea「亚麻线、铅垂线」（经古法语 ligne）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one geometric fact: water and land meet along a line. That line is then widened into a strip, moved to lakes and reservoirs, watched as it shifts, measured, governed, planted, and finally printed on a map.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都始于一个几何事实：水与陆沿着一条线相接。这条线随后被放宽成一条带，移到湖泊与水库，被观察其移动、被测量、被管制、被种上植物，最后被印在地图上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin wet line curving between water and land.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条细而湿的线，在水与陆地之间弯过。

branches.en: THE LINE: the simplest reading, the boundary itself.
branches.cn: 那条线：最简单的读法，即界线本身。

branches.en: THE DRAWN LINE: maps and images turn the boundary into an outline.
branches.cn: 被画出的线：地图与影像把界线变成轮廓。

branches.en: THE ZONE AND OTHER WATERS: the edge as a strip, and the same edge on lakes and reservoirs.
branches.cn: 岸带与其他水体：边缘成了一条带，同样也出现在湖泊与水库上。

branches.en: A LINE THAT MOVES: erosion shifts it, survey measures it.
branches.cn: 会移动的线：侵蚀使它移动，测量把它量出。

branches.en: A LINE THAT IS GOVERNED AND PLANTED: plans set it back, roots hold it.
branches.cn: 被治理与被种植的线：规划让它后退，根系把它固定。

intro.en: Shoreline is a native-English compound, not a suffixed derivation: shore and line each arrive whole, and the compound simply puts the two nouns together. Its wider family comes from compounds and prefixes built on shore, and from the many words built on line.
intro.cn: shoreline 是英语本族复合词，不是加后缀的派生：shore 与 line 各自完整进入，复合词只是把两个名词并置。它更大的词族来自以 shore 构成的复合词与前缀形式，以及由 line 构成的大量词。

latinIntro.en: Only the second element has a Latin source: linea 'thread, plumb line'. Shore has no Latin ancestor; Latin litus 'shore' and ora 'coast' translate the idea but are not related to it, so the entries below cover the line side only.
latinIntro.cn: 只有第二个成分有拉丁来源：linea「线、铅垂线」。shore 没有拉丁语祖先；拉丁 litus「岸」与 ora「海岸」只是语义对应词，并非其来源，因此下列条目只覆盖 line 这一侧。

items.meaning: a long thin mark; a boundary

items.meaning: the edge where water meets land

items.example: The current pushed the boat shoreward.
items.exampleCN: 水流把小船推向岸边。

items.meaning: towards or on the land from the sea

items.meaning: a bird that feeds at the water's edge

definition_zh: 河口湾（河流入海口淡水与海水混合的宽阔水域）；潮汐河口；河口生态系统
definition_en: the wide lower part of a river where fresh water meets the sea and is mixed by the tides
core_image: 浑黄的河水在喇叭形的入海口被咸蓝的海水顶回来，潮水一涨一落，泥滩时而淹没时而露出
scene: 退潮后，喇叭形的入海口露出大片泥滩，海鸥沿着浅水道觅食。At low tide the estuary exposed wide mudflats where gulls fed along shallow channels.
sceneCN: 这里 estuary 指「河流入海处淡水与海水交汇的宽阔水域」（第 1 个义项：河口湾）；句意：退潮时，这片河口湾露出大片泥滩，海鸥在浅水道旁觅食。图中可辨识物件：泥滩上的浅水道、觅食的海鸥、河与海交界处的水色、搁浅的小船。

pos.zh: 河口湾；河口（河流入海处淡水与海水交汇、受潮汐影响的水域）

senses.title: The wide mouth where river meets sea
senses.titleCN: 河口湾：河流入海处的宽阔水域
senses.definition: the wide lower reach of a river where its fresh water meets and mixes with sea water
senses.definitionCN: 河流下游宽阔的河段，淡水在此与海水相遇并混合
senses.example: At low tide the estuary exposed wide mudflats where gulls fed along shallow channels.
senses.exampleCN: 退潮时，这片河口湾露出大片泥滩，海鸥在浅水道旁觅食。
senses.why: the word names the drowned lower valley itself, a body of water wider than the river because the sea has invaded it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指被海水侵入的下游河谷本身；因为海水的进入，它比河道更宽。

senses.title: A tidal reach governed by the tide
senses.titleCN: 受潮汐支配的河口段
senses.definition: the part of a river near its mouth in which the water level and the direction of flow reverse with the tide
senses.definitionCN: 河流近口门、水位与流向随潮汐往复变化的那一段
senses.example: Salt water pushes upstream in the estuary with every flood tide.
senses.exampleCN: 每次涨潮，咸水都沿河口段向上游推进。
senses.why: the tidal sense narrows the first: the same water body is defined by the twice-daily reversal of its current.
senses.whyCN: 潮汐义收窄了第一个义项：同一片水域，以水流一日两次反向为界定特征。

senses.title: A brackish ecosystem
senses.titleCN: 河口生态系统（淡咸水交汇的生境）
senses.definition: the community of plants and animals adapted to water whose salinity changes with the tide
senses.definitionCN: 适应盐度随潮汐变化的河口水的动植物群落
senses.example: Juvenile salmon feed in the estuary before they enter the open sea.
senses.exampleCN: 幼鲑在进入外海之前先在河口育肥。
senses.why: from the place the word passes to what lives in it, a standard shift from a habitat to its community.
senses.whyCN: 由地点转向其中的生物，这是从生境到生物群落的常见转喻。

senses.title: Silt laid down at the river mouth
senses.titleCN: 河口沉积（河流泥沙在口门堆积）
senses.definition: sand and mud carried down by the river and deposited where the current slows at the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 河流带下的砂与泥在口门流速减缓处堆积而成的沉积物
senses.example: Cores from the estuary record two centuries of upstream soil erosion.
senses.exampleCN: 河口沉积柱芯记录了两个世纪的上游水土流失。
senses.why: the estuary is a sediment trap, so its name transfers to the material that fills it.
senses.whyCN: 河口是泥沙的捕集器，因此其名称也转指填在其中的物质。

senses.title: Fishing and farming in estuarine water
senses.titleCN: 河口渔业与养殖
senses.definition: the use of nutrient-rich estuarine water for catching fish or cultivating shellfish
senses.definitionCN: 利用营养丰富的河口水域捕鱼或养殖贝类
senses.example: Oyster farms in the estuary depend on clean water and steady tides.
senses.exampleCN: 河口湾的牡蛎养殖场依赖洁净的水与稳定的潮汐。
senses.why: human activity is named by its setting, as with any fishery; the estuary supplies the nutrients that make the catch possible.
senses.whyCN: 人类活动以所在地命名，正如各类渔场；河口提供养分，才使捕捞成为可能。

senses.title: Pollution where the river meets the sea
senses.titleCN: 河口污染与水质问题
senses.definition: the accumulation of pollutants in estuarine water, where river discharge and sea water mix and currents are slow
senses.definitionCN: 污染物在河口水中的累积，该处河水与海水混合、流速缓慢
senses.example: Nitrogen from farms collects in the estuary and feeds summer algal blooms.
senses.exampleCN: 农田带来的氮在河口积聚，助长夏季藻华。
senses.why: because the estuary is the collecting basin of a whole catchment, its name becomes shorthand for the water-quality problem there.
senses.whyCN: 河口是整个流域的汇集盆，因此其名称成为当地水质问题的代称。

senses.title: A dredged channel for shipping
senses.titleCN: 需要疏浚的河口航道
senses.definition: the navigable channel maintained through an estuary for ships moving between the river and the sea
senses.definitionCN: 为船舶进出河流与海洋而在河口维护的通航水道
senses.example: Dredging keeps the estuary open to ships drawing twelve metres.
senses.exampleCN: 疏浚使河口航道可供吃水十二米的船舶通行。
senses.why: the mouth is the gate of a river port, so the word also names the passage that has to be kept open.
senses.whyCN: 口门是河港的门户，因此这个词也指必须维持畅通的那条通道。

senses.title: A meeting ground of unlike things
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：不同事物的交汇地带
senses.definition: a place or situation in which two different systems meet and influence each other
senses.definitionCN: 两种不同体系相遇并相互影响的地方或处境
senses.example: The festival became an estuary of rural and urban tastes.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节庆成了乡村与城市趣味的交汇地带。
senses.why: the physical mixing of fresh and salt water is generalized into any boundary zone where unlike things blend.
senses.whyCN: 淡水与咸水的物理混合被一般化为任何不同事物交融的边界地带。

intro.en: Estuary comes from Latin aestuarium 'a tract flooded by the tide', from aestus 'tide, surge, heat'. English borrowed it in the sixteenth century. The deeper origin of aestus is uncertain, and the link sometimes proposed with aestas 'summer' is a hypothesis.
intro.cn: estuary 来自拉丁 aestuarium「受潮水淹没的滩地」，后者出自 aestus「潮汐、涌动、热」。英语于 16 世纪借入。aestus 的更深来源不确定，有人提出它与 aestas「夏天」有关，但那只是假说。

items.en: Aestus meant 'tide, surge' and also 'boiling, seething heat'. Roman writers used it for both the movement of the sea and the fever of the body.
items.cn: aestus 意为「潮汐、涌动」，也指「沸腾、灼热」。罗马作家用它既指海水的运动，也指身体的发热。

items.en: Aestuarium was the low ground or channel that the tide fills and empties; the suffix -arium marks a place associated with the action of aestus.
items.cn: aestuarium 指潮水灌入又退出的低地或水道；后缀 -arium 表示与 aestus 这一动作相关的地点。

items.en: English geographers borrowed aestuarium in the 1530s for the widened mouth of a tidal river, and the spelling settled as estuary.
items.cn: 16 世纪 30 年代，英国地理学者借入 aestuarium，用来指受潮汐影响的宽河口；拼写后来固定为 estuary。

items.en: The early English sense kept the tidal idea, so an estuary was a river mouth shaped by the rise and fall of the sea rather than merely the end of a river.
items.cn: 早期英语义保留了潮汐意味，因此河口湾指受海水涨落塑造的河口，而不只是河流的终点。

items.en: The adjective estuarine was formed in the nineteenth century on the model of Latin -inus, and estuarial followed as a rarer variant; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 estuarine 于 19 世纪仿拉丁 -inus 构成，estuarial 作为更少用的变体随后出现；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of aestus): the connection with aestas 'summer' and with Greek aithein 'to burn' are competing hypotheses, and any Indo-European form offered for aestus is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（aestus 的更深词源）：与 aestas「夏天」以及希腊 aithein「燃烧」的联系是并行的假说，凡为 aestus 拟出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates estuary from look-alikes, including one word that shares its Latin root and several that do not; group two contrasts the tidal river mouth with neighbouring water features.
note.cn: 第一组把 estuary 与形近词分开，其中一词共享拉丁词根，其余并无关系；第二组把潮汐河口与相邻的水域概念作对比。

entries.definition: From Latin aestivus 'of summer', built on the same aest- base as aestus; it means 'summery' and does not name a river mouth.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 aestivus「夏天的」，与 aestus 共用 aest- 词干；意为「夏季的」，并不指河口。

entries.definition: The practice of lending money at interest, from Latin usura 'use'; the -ury ending makes it sound like estuary, but the roots differ.
entries.definitionCN: 指放贷取息的行业，来自拉丁 usura「使用」；-ury 词尾使它听起来像 estuary，但词根不同。

entries.definition: To alienate someone, from Latin extraneare 'treat as a stranger'; only the opening letters resemble estuary.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某人疏远，来自拉丁 extraneare「当作陌生人对待」；只有开头几个字母与 estuary 相似。

entries.definition: Concerned with beauty, from Greek aisthanesthai 'to perceive'; the shared opening sound is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 指与美有关的，来自希腊 aisthanesthai「感知」；开头的读音相近只是巧合。

entries.definition: A river mouth where the current slows and splits around deposited sediment; an estuary is instead a drowned valley dominated by tides.
entries.definitionCN: 河流因流速减缓、泥沙堆积而分汊的口门；河口湾则是被海水淹没、以潮汐为主导的河谷。

entries.definition: A Scottish word for a narrow sea inlet or river estuary; it overlaps with estuary but is regional.
entries.definitionCN: 苏格兰语中指狭窄的海湾或河口；与 estuary 语义重叠，但属地域用词。

entries.definition: A narrow opening by which the sea enters the land; it need not receive a river, which an estuary always does.
entries.definitionCN: 海水伸入陆地的狭窄通道；它不一定有河流注入，而河口湾一定有。

entries.definition: The point where a river enters a larger body of water; it is neutral and does not imply tidal mixing or width.
entries.definitionCN: 河流进入更大水域的那一点；语气中立，不含潮汐混合或宽阔水域之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: aestus 'tide' plus -arium 'place': the place that the tide fills and empties.
normal.cn: aestus「潮汐」加 -arium「地点」：潮水灌入又退出的那个地方。

normal.en: The family is estuary, estuarine and estuarial; the adjective is far more common in ecology than the noun is in speech.
normal.cn: 同族词是 estuary、estuarine 与 estuarial；形容词在生态学中的使用远多于名词在日常口语中的使用。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the ecology: estuary ecosystem, estuary sediment, estuary pollution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出生态义：河口生态系统、河口沉积物、河口污染。

normal.en: Geography pairs it with delta: a delta builds outward, while an estuary is a valley drowned inward by the sea.
normal.cn: 地理学把它与三角洲对举：三角洲向外堆出，河口湾则是被海水向内淹没的河谷。

normal.en: British references such as the Thames estuary and the Severn estuary name the tidal type most clearly.
normal.cn: 泰晤士河口与塞文河口这类英国实例最能说明潮汐河口这一类型。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway where two crowds push in opposite directions and neither can move freely.
abstract.cn: 想象一个门口，两股人潮相向而行，谁也走不痛快。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of tea into which cold milk is poured: the boundary is where the colours first mix.
abstract.cn: 想象往一杯热茶里倒入冷牛奶：交界处正是两种颜色最先混开的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a market where two languages trade words across the same counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个市场，两种语言在同一个柜台前交换词语。

examples.en: The estuary supports a nursery for young fish before they reach the open sea.
examples.cn: 这片河口湾为幼鱼提供育肥场所，之后它们才进入外海。

examples.en: Sediment cores from the estuary show how fast the surrounding hills eroded.
examples.cn: 取自河口的沉积柱芯显示周边山地侵蚀得有多快。

examples.en: Ships wait for high water before they enter the shallow estuary.
examples.cn: 船舶等高潮时才驶入这片浅水河口湾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「estuary」读似「爱水求瑞」——河水一路爱水，到海口求个汇合之处，便是河口湾

root: 拉丁 aestuarium「高潮淹没的滩地」< aestus「潮汐、沸腾、热」；英语 16 世纪借入。aestus 更深来源不确定，与 aestas「夏天」及希腊 aithein「燃烧」的联系均属假说，非定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one physical event: a river valley drowned by the sea, where fresh and salt water are stirred twice a day. From that place come the tidal reach, the brackish community, its sediment, its fisheries, its pollution, its shipping channel, and finally any zone where two worlds mix.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由同一个自然事件展开：河谷被海水淹没，淡水与咸水一日两次被搅动。由此依次生出潮汐河段、淡咸水生物群落、河口沉积、渔业、污染、航道，最后泛指任何两个世界交融的地带。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river mouth flooded by the tide, where fresh and salt water are stirred together.
core.cn: 核心意象：被潮水灌入的河口，淡水与咸水在此搅在一起。

branches.en: DROWNED MOUTH: the widened lower valley and its twice-daily reversal of flow.
branches.cn: 被淹的口门：加宽的下游河谷，以及一日两次反向的水流。

branches.en: BRACKISH COMMUNITY: the living community that tolerates shifting salinity.
branches.cn: 淡咸水群落：能耐受盐度变化的生物群落。

branches.en: SILT TRAP: the mouth as a basin where river sediment settles.
branches.cn: 泥沙捕集：口门作为河流沉积物沉降的盆地。

branches.en: WORKING WATER: fishing, pollution and navigation all concentrate at the same mouth.
branches.cn: 作业水域：渔业、污染与航运都集中在这同一个口门。

branches.en: MEETING GROUND: the physical mix becomes an image for any boundary between two systems.
branches.cn: 交汇地带：物理混合成为任何两个体系边界的意象。

intro.en: Estuary is a Latin loan whose parts can still be read: the root aestus 'tide' plus the place suffix -arium. English then added -ine and -al for the adjectives and joined the noun to native nouns in compounds.
intro.cn: estuary 是拉丁借词，其构词成分仍可读出：词根 aestus「潮汐」加地点后缀 -arium。英语随后加 -ine 与 -al 构成形容词，并与本族名词组合成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin aestus gives aestuarium and the verb aestuare 'to surge, boil'. Latin aestas 'summer' is a possible relative, but the link is debated rather than established.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 aestus 衍生 aestuarium 与动词 aestuare「涌动、沸腾」。拉丁 aestas「夏天」可能是其亲属，但这一联系仍有争议，尚未确立。

items.example: Aestus is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: aestus 是整个词族的词根。

items.meaning: a place associated with an action
items.example: The suffix turns an action into a place.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把一个动作变成一处地点。

items.example: The estuary opens into a cold sea.
items.exampleCN: 这片河口湾通向一片寒冷的海。

items.example: Estuarine mud supports dense worm populations.
items.exampleCN: 河口湾的淤泥养育了密集的沙蚕种群。

items.meaning: of an estuary, a rarer variant
items.example: Estuarial waters warm slowly in spring.
items.exampleCN: 河口湾水域在春季升温缓慢。

items.meaning: the outer opening of a tidal river
items.example: Fishing boats crossed the estuary mouth at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 渔船在黎明时越过河口湾口门。

items.meaning: a brackish habitat within an estuary
items.meaningCN: 河口湾内的淡咸水生境
items.example: The estuarine habitat shifts with every tide.
items.exampleCN: 河口的生境随每次潮汐而改变。

items.meaning: an estuary dominated by tidal flow
items.meaningCN: 以潮汐水流为主导的河口
items.example: A tidal estuary reverses its current twice a day.
items.exampleCN: 潮汐河口的水流一日两次反向。

items.meaning: a variety of English associated with the Thames estuary
items.meaningCN: 与泰晤士河口相关的英语口音
items.example: Estuary English spread far beyond its home region.
items.exampleCN: 河口英语传播到了其发源地区之外很远的地方。

definition_zh: 河流的；沿河的；河岸的；河流生态的
definition_en: relating to a river, to its banks, or to the plants and animals that live in and along it
core_image: 一条河穿过干旱平原，两岸的树、堤路和村庄被它拉成一条细长的绿带
scene: 洪水退去后，两岸的村庄开始修补被冲坏的堤坝。The riverine villages rebuilt the dikes that line both banks after the flood.
sceneCN: 这里 riverine 指「沿河而设、依河而居的」（第 2 个义项：沿河、河岸的）；句意：洪水过后，沿河的村庄重修了两岸的堤坝。图中可辨识物件：两岸堤坝、柳树、村庄屋顶、退水留下的泥痕。

pos.zh: 河流的；沿河的；河岸的；生长在河中的

derivatives.zh: 小溪（拉丁 rivulus，rivus 的指小形式）
竞争对手；与……竞争（拉丁 rivalis 原指共用同一条溪水的人）
沿河地；以河流的方式（少用）
河流廊道（沿河连续的带状生境）
河岸湿地（受河流涨落影响的湿地）

senses.title: Of a river itself
senses.titleCN: 河流本身的，属于河流的
senses.definition: belonging to a river as a watercourse, or produced by the action of flowing water
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为水道的一条河流，或由流水作用产生的
senses.example: Riverine currents sort the gravel into long bars.
senses.exampleCN: 河流的水流把砾石分选成长条状的砾石坝。
senses.why: the adjective is built on Latin rivus 'stream', so its first job is to qualify the channel and the water in it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词建于拉丁 rivus「溪流」之上，因此首要功能是修饰河道与其中的水。

senses.title: Along the banks of a river
senses.titleCN: 沿河的、河岸的
senses.definition: situated on or beside the banks of a river, or organised around the river's edge
senses.definitionCN: 位于河岸之上或河岸旁边，或以河岸为中心组织起来的
senses.example: The riverine villages rebuilt the dikes that line both banks after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，沿河的村庄重修了两岸的堤坝。
senses.why: from the water the adjective moves to the land beside it, because a river's edge is where people build and plant.
senses.whyCN: 形容词由水面转向旁边的陆地，因为河岸正是人们建房与耕种的地方。

senses.title: The river-and-floodplain ecosystem
senses.titleCN: 河流生态系统
senses.definition: the habitat formed by a river together with its floodplain, including the species that depend on seasonal flooding
senses.definitionCN: 河流与其洪泛区共同构成的生境，包括依赖季节性泛滥的物种
senses.example: Riverine forests survive on the silt that spring floods spread across their roots.
senses.exampleCN: 河岸林靠春汛铺到根部的淤泥存活。
senses.why: ecology treats channel and floodplain as one unit, so the adjective names a system rather than a single line.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把河道与洪泛区视为一个单元，因此这个形容词命名的是一套系统，而不只是一条线。

senses.title: Landforms shaped by running water
senses.titleCN: 由流水塑造的河川地貌
senses.definition: the landforms and deposits produced by a river, such as terraces, bars and levees
senses.definitionCN: 由河流造成的地形与沉积，如阶地、砾石坝与天然堤
senses.example: Riverine terraces mark the older, higher courses of the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 河流阶地标出这条溪流更古老、更高的河道。
senses.why: geomorphology extends the adjective from the water to the shapes the water has left behind.
senses.whyCN: 地貌学把这个形容词从水扩展到水留下的形状。

senses.title: Riparian settlement and culture
senses.titleCN: 河岸居民与河岸文化
senses.definition: the people, settlements and ways of life that cluster along a river
senses.definitionCN: 沿河聚居的人群、聚落与生活方式
senses.example: Riverine communities share boats, nets and a common calendar of floods.
senses.exampleCN: 河岸社区共享船只、渔网以及一套共同的洪水历法。
senses.why: a river is a road and a larder, so the adjective also describes the human life that grows along it.
senses.whyCN: 河流既是道路也是食源，因此这个形容词也描述沿河生长的人类生活。

senses.title: Transport by river
senses.titleCN: 河流运输
senses.definition: the movement of goods or passengers along a river rather than by road or rail
senses.definitionCN: 沿河道而非经公路或铁路运送货物或旅客
senses.example: Riverine transport is cheaper than road haulage along this stretch.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一段，河流运输比公路货运便宜。
senses.why: the channel is a route, so the adjective qualifies a mode of transport that uses the water as its road.
senses.whyCN: 河道是一条路线，因此这个形容词修饰一种把水当路用的运输方式。

senses.title: Flood hydrology and river regime
senses.titleCN: 河流洪水与水文情势
senses.definition: the seasonal behaviour of a river's flow, including floods, low water and sediment load
senses.definitionCN: 河流流量的季节变化，包括洪水、枯水与输沙
senses.example: Riverine flooding is predicted from snowpack and spring rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 河流洪水依据积雪与春季降雨来预测。
senses.why: hydrology uses the adjective for the river's own behaviour in time, not for a place beside it.
senses.whyCN: 水文学用这个形容词指河流自身随时间变化的行为，而非旁边的地点。

senses.title: Life that lives in or by the river
senses.titleCN: 河生生物（生活在河中的生物）
senses.definition: organisms adapted to life in flowing fresh water or on its banks
senses.definitionCN: 适应在流动淡水中或河岸上生活的生物
senses.example: Riverine insects lay their eggs on stones that stay wet all year.
senses.exampleCN: 河生昆虫把卵产在常年湿润的石头上。
senses.why: the habitat sense narrows to its inhabitants, as with marine and terrestrial, which likewise name both realm and biota.
senses.whyCN: 生境义收窄到其中的居民，正如「海洋的」与「陆地的」这类词同样既指领域又指生物。

intro.en: Riverine is a nineteenth-century English formation: Latin rivus 'small stream' plus the adjective suffix -ine. It is not derived from English river, which came through Old French riviere from Latin ripa 'bank'. The two Latin words are different, and the similarity of the English forms hides that.
intro.cn: riverine 是 19 世纪英语造出的词：拉丁 rivus「小溪」加形容词后缀 -ine。它并非由英语 river 派生；river 经古法语 riviere 来自拉丁 ripa「河岸」。这两个拉丁词并不相同，只是英语词形相近，掩盖了这一区别。

items.en: Rivus meant 'small stream, brook'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the common reconstruction from an Indo-European root meaning 'to flow, run' is a reconstructed form, not a attested ancestor.
items.cn: rivus 意为「小溪、溪流」。其更深来源不确定；通常拟出的、意为「流动、奔跑」的印欧语词根属重构形式，并非有书证可查的祖形。

items.en: Ripa meant 'bank, shore' and is the source of English river through Old French riviere. River and riverine therefore look related but descend from different Latin nouns, a distinction that historical dictionaries make explicit.
items.cn: ripa 意为「河岸、岸」，经古法语 riviere 成为英语 river。因此 river 与 riverine 看似同族，实则出自不同的拉丁名词，历史词典对此有明确区分。

items.en: The suffix -ine, from Latin -inus 'belonging to', was already productive in English adjectives such as marine and feline when riverine was formed.
items.cn: 后缀 -ine 出自拉丁 -inus「属于……的」；在 riverine 造出时，它已能产于 marine、feline 这类英语形容词。

items.en: Riverine was coined in the nineteenth century, most likely in geographical and natural-history writing, to supply an adjective for the river and its banks; the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: riverine 于 19 世纪造出，最可能出现在地理与博物学写作中，用来为河流及其两岸提供一个形容词；确切的最早书证年代不确定。

items.en: In the twentieth century ecology and hydrology adopted the word for whole river-floodplain systems and for a river's seasonal behaviour, which is why it now appears in technical compounds.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，生态学与水文学采用该词指整个河流—洪泛区系统以及河流的季节性行为，因此它如今多见于技术性复合词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): rivus has no settled Indo-European etymology, and the earliest English use of riverine is not precisely dated; the Latin base itself, however, is certain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：rivus 没有定论的印欧语词源，riverine 最早的英语用例也缺乏确切年代；但它的拉丁词基本身是确定的。

note.en: Group one separates riverine from look-alikes, above all English river, which descends from Latin ripa and is not its base; group two places it beside the other adjectives of wetland science.
note.cn: 第一组把 riverine 与形近词分开，尤其是英语 river——它出自拉丁 ripa，并非 riverine 的词基；第二组把它与湿地科学中的其他形容词并列。

entries.definition: English river comes through Old French riviere from Latin ripa 'bank, shore', not from rivus 'stream'; it is the everyday noun that riverine describes, but not its morphological base.
entries.definitionCN: 英语 river 经古法语 riviere 来自拉丁 ripa「河岸、岸」，而非 rivus「溪流」；它是 riverine 所描述的日常名词，却不是其构词词基。

entries.definition: From Latin rivulus, a diminutive of rivus, so it is a genuine cousin; it means a small stream, not a river bank.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 rivulus，是 rivus 的指小形式，因此确为同族；意为小溪，而非河岸。

entries.definition: From Latin rivalis, originally one who draws water from the same stream; the root is rivus, but the modern meaning is a competitor.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 rivalis，原指从同一条溪流取水的人；词根是 rivus，但今义为竞争者。

entries.definition: A deep narrow valley, from Latin rapina 'violent seizure'; it sounds like riverine but belongs to a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 指深邃狭窄的谷地，来自拉丁 rapina「强夺」；读音近似 riverine，但词根不同。

entries.definition: Of rivers and the action of flowing water, from Latin fluvius 'river'; it is the geological and technical counterpart of riverine.
entries.definitionCN: 指河流以及流水作用的，来自拉丁 fluvius「河流」；是 riverine 在地质与技术语境中的对应词。

entries.definition: Relating to the banks of a river, from Latin ripa; it overlaps with riverine in the bank sense but is rooted in ripa, not rivus.
entries.definitionCN: 指与河岸有关的，来自拉丁 ripa；在河岸义上与 riverine 重叠，但词根是 ripa 而非 rivus。

entries.definition: Of lakes, from Latin lacus; it is the lake equivalent of riverine in the classification of wetland and water habitats.
entries.definitionCN: 指湖泊的，来自拉丁 lacus；在湿地与水域生境分类中，它是 riverine 的湖泊对应词。

entries.definition: Of marshes, from Latin palus; in the same classification it names the marsh class beside riverine and lacustrine.
entries.definitionCN: 指沼泽的，来自拉丁 palus；在同一分类体系中，它与 riverine、lacustrine 并列，指沼泽类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: rivus 'stream' plus -ine 'of': 'of a stream' is the core reading, not 'of a river bank'.
normal.cn: rivus「溪流」加 -ine「属于」：核心读法是「溪流的」，而不是「河岸的」。

normal.en: False-friend alert: river comes from ripa 'bank', while riverine comes from rivus 'stream'; the English spellings hide two different Latin nouns.
normal.cn: 易错点提醒：river 出自 ripa「岸」，riverine 出自 rivus「溪流」；英语拼写掩盖了两个不同的拉丁名词。

normal.en: The -ine wetland family lines up as riverine, riparian, lacustrine and palustrine: river, bank, lake, marsh.
normal.cn: 以 -ine 结尾的湿地词族可排成 riverine、riparian、lacustrine、palustrine：河流、河岸、湖泊、沼泽。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the applied senses: riverine ecosystem, riverine landscape, riverine transport.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出应用义：河流生态系统、河川景观、河流运输。

normal.en: Rival descends from the same rivus: two people who share one stream end up competing for its water.
normal.cn: rival 也出自同一个 rivus：共用一条溪流的人，最终会为水而竞争。

abstract.en: Picture a green thread stitched along a dry brown cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绿线，沿着干燥的棕色布面缝下去。

abstract.en: Picture houses standing in a single row because the water decides where they may stand.
abstract.cn: 想象房屋排成一列，因为水决定了它们只能站在哪里。

abstract.en: Picture a road and a river running side by side, each carrying what the other cannot.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路与一条河并排延伸，各自运送对方运不了的东西。

examples.en: Riverine forests survive on the seasonal flood that spreads silt across their roots.
examples.cn: 河岸林靠季节性洪水把淤泥铺到根部而存活。

examples.en: The riverine villages moved their kitchens and boats to the higher bank.
examples.cn: 沿河的村庄把厨房和船只搬到了较高的河岸上。

examples.en: Riverine transport is cheaper than road haulage along this stretch.
examples.cn: 在这一段，河流运输比公路货运便宜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「riverine」读似「瑞沃润」——河两岸被水润着，所以 riverine 就是沿河的、河岸的

root: 拉丁 rivus「小溪、溪流」+ 英语后缀 -ine（19 世纪仿拉丁 -inus 造词）；rivus 的印欧来源一般拟为 *rei-，属重构形式。注意：英语 river 出自拉丁 ripa「河岸」经古法语 riviere，与 riverine 并非同一词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line of water: the stream itself, the bank beside it, the river-floodplain system, the landforms it builds, the settlements along it, the traffic on it, the floods it sends, and the life adapted to it. The adjective keeps moving outward from the channel to everything the channel shapes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条水线展开：溪流本身、旁边的河岸、河流—洪泛区系统、流水造出的地貌、沿河的聚落、河上的运输、河流带来的洪水，以及适应它的生物。这个形容词不断由河道向外扩展，指向河道所塑造的一切。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow ribbon of water and trees drawn across dry country.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条水与树构成的细带，画在干旱的大地上。

branches.en: OF THE RIVER ITSELF: the adjective qualifies the channel and its flowing water.
branches.cn: 河流本身：这个形容词修饰河道与其流水。

branches.en: OF THE BANK: the same adjective shifts from the water to the land beside it.
branches.cn: 河岸：同一个形容词由水面转向旁边的陆地。

branches.en: OF THE SYSTEM AND ITS SHAPE: ecology and geomorphology treat river and floodplain as one unit.
branches.cn: 系统与形状：生态学与地貌学把河流与洪泛区视为一个单元。

branches.en: OF PEOPLE AND TRAFFIC: settlement and transport follow the bank line.
branches.cn: 人与交通：聚落与运输都沿着河岸线展开。

branches.en: OF FLOOD AND LIFE: the flood that builds the habitat is also the hazard, and the biota depends on both.
branches.cn: 洪水与生命：造出生境的洪水也是灾害，而生物同时依赖这两面。

intro.en: Riverine is a Latin root plus an English adjective suffix. The root rivus is also visible in rivulet and rival, while the suffix -ine recurs across wetland science in lacustrine and palustrine.
intro.cn: riverine 由一个拉丁词根加一个英语形容词后缀构成。词根 rivus 也见于 rivulet 与 rival；后缀 -ine 则在 lacustrine、palustrine 等湿地科学词汇中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin rivus 'stream' yields rivulus, the source of rivulet, and rivalis, the source of rival. Latin ripa 'bank' is a different noun and yields English river; the two Latin families must not be merged.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rivus「溪流」衍生 rivulus，即 rivulet 的来源，也衍生 rivalis，即 rival 的来源。拉丁 ripa「岸」是另一个名词，衍生英语 river；两个拉丁词族不可合并。

items.example: Rivus is the base of the whole riverine family.
items.exampleCN: rivus 是整个 riverine 词族的词基。

items.meaning: belonging to; of the nature of
items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表示归属的形容词。

items.meaning: of a stream or its banks
items.example: Riverine silt built the low terrace.
items.exampleCN: 河流带来的淤泥堆成了低阶地。

items.example: A rivulet ran under the stone bridge.
items.exampleCN: 一条小溪从石桥下流过。

items.meaning: one who shares the same stream; a competitor
items.meaningCN: 共用同一条溪水的人；竞争者
items.example: Two rivals drew from the same channel.
items.exampleCN: 两个竞争者从同一条水道取水。

items.meaning: of a river bank; note the different Latin base
items.meaningCN: 河岸的；注意其拉丁词基不同
items.example: Riparian willows hold the bank together.
items.exampleCN: 河岸的柳树把岸固定在一起。

items.example: Lacustrine deposits fill the old basin.
items.exampleCN: 湖泊沉积填满了古老的盆地。

items.example: Palustrine soils stay saturated all summer.
items.exampleCN: 沼泽土壤整个夏天都保持饱和。

items.meaning: a continuous strip of river habitat
items.example: The riverine corridor links the upland forest to the delta.
items.exampleCN: 河流廊道把高地森林与三角洲连接起来。

latinEntries.structure: rivulus, rivuli (noun, second declension; diminutive of rivus)

latinEntries.meaning: bank, shore (the source of English river, not of riverine)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 河岸；岸（英语 river 的来源，而非 riverine 的来源）

definition_zh: 浮游生物（随水漂流、不能自主逆流的微小动植物的总称）；浮游生物量
definition_en: the tiny plants and animals that drift in seas and lakes and cannot swim strongly enough to move against a current
core_image: 一滴海水在显微镜下被放大，圆形硅藻、带刺藻类与细小甲壳类悬浮在光柱里，随水缓慢旋转
scene: 夜里，船桨搅动海水，水面沿船身泛起一片蓝光。At night the plankton glowed blue along the hull whenever the oars stirred the water.
sceneCN: 这里 plankton 指「随水漂流、不能自主逆流的微小生物总称」（第 1 个义项：浮游生物总称）；句意：夜里，每当船桨搅动海水，浮游生物就沿船身泛出蓝光。图中可辨识物件：泛蓝光的水面、船体、桨划出的水纹、暗色夜空。

pos.zh: 浮游生物（不可数集合名词，指随水漂流的微小动植物）

forms.label: 形容词（浮游的，学术变体）

derivatives.zh: 浮游生物的；浮游生活的
浮游生物个体（单个浮游生物）

senses.title: The drifting community as a whole
senses.titleCN: 浮游生物总称
senses.definition: the whole assemblage of small aquatic organisms that drift with currents and cannot make headway against them
senses.definitionCN: 随水流漂移、无法逆流前进的微小水生生物的整体
senses.example: At night the plankton glowed blue along the hull whenever the oars stirred the water.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里，每当船桨搅动海水，浮游生物就沿船身泛出蓝光。
senses.why: the word is a collective mass noun, so it names the community rather than one creature; the Greek source means 'the wandering thing'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是不可数集合名词，命名的是群落而非单个生物；其希腊语来源意为「漂泊之物」。

senses.title: Plant plankton that photosynthesises
senses.titleCN: 浮游植物
senses.definition: the photosynthetic part of the plankton, mostly single-celled algae and diatoms, living near the sunlit surface
senses.definitionCN: 浮游生物中进行光合作用的部分，多为单细胞藻类与硅藻，生活在有阳光的表层
senses.example: Spring light lets phytoplankton double their numbers in a few days.
senses.exampleCN: 春季的光照使浮游植物在几天内数量翻倍。
senses.why: the collective splits by nutrition: plant-like drifters are phytoplankton, and the prefix phyto- 'plant' marks the class.
senses.whyCN: 这个集合按营养方式划分：类植物的漂流者即浮游植物，前缀 phyto-「植物」标出这一类。
