senses.title: Animal plankton that grazes
senses.titleCN: 浮游动物
senses.definition: the animal part of the plankton, from tiny crustaceans to jellyfish larvae, feeding on phytoplankton or on each other
senses.definitionCN: 浮游生物中的动物部分，从微小甲壳类到水母幼体，以浮游植物或彼此为食
senses.example: Zooplankton rise toward the surface at night and sink by day.
senses.exampleCN: 浮游动物夜间升向表层，白天则下沉。
senses.why: the prefix zoo- 'animal' marks the grazing half of the community, which migrates vertically with the light.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 zoo-「动物」标出群落中取食的那一半，它们随光照做垂直迁移。

senses.title: A local plankton assemblage
senses.titleCN: 某一水域的浮游生物群落
senses.definition: the particular set of plankton species present in one water body at one time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻、某一水域中实际存在的特定浮游生物物种组合
senses.example: The lake's plankton shifted from diatoms to green algae after the spring melt.
senses.exampleCN: 春雪融尽后，湖中的浮游生物由硅藻转为绿藻。
senses.why: ecology counts a community at a place and time, so the mass noun also serves as a countable unit of study.
senses.whyCN: 生态学按地点与时间统计群落，因此这个集合名词也可作为可数的研究单位。

senses.title: Biomass and sudden blooms
senses.titleCN: 生物量与藻华暴发
senses.definition: the total mass of plankton in a volume of water, or a rapid population increase visible as discoloured water
senses.definitionCN: 单位水体中浮游生物的总质量，或表现为水色改变的快速增殖
senses.example: A plankton bloom turned the bay green for three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 一次浮游生物暴发使海湾变绿达三周之久。
senses.why: abundance is measured as mass, and when that mass grows fast it becomes an event with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 丰度以质量计量，而当质量快速增长时，它就成为一个有专名的事件。

senses.title: The base of the aquatic food chain
senses.titleCN: 水生食物链的基础
senses.definition: the first link of the pelagic food web, converting sunlight and nutrients into food for larger animals
senses.definitionCN: 远洋食物网的第一环，把阳光与养分转化为较大动物可食的物质
senses.example: Small fish filter plankton from the water and pass the energy upward.
senses.exampleCN: 小鱼从水中滤食浮游生物，把能量向上传递。
senses.why: from the organisms the word passes to their ecological role: whatever eats them begins a chain.
senses.whyCN: 由生物本身转向其生态角色：凡以它们为食者，都从这一环开始一条食物链。

senses.title: The biological carbon pump
senses.titleCN: 生物泵与碳循环
senses.definition: the process by which plankton fix carbon near the surface and carry part of it to the deep sea as they die and sink
senses.definitionCN: 浮游生物在表层固定碳，并在死亡下沉时把其中一部分带到深海的过程
senses.example: Sinking plankton move carbon out of the surface layer for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 下沉的浮游生物把碳带离表层，一存就是几个世纪。
senses.why: the same drifting and sinking that defines the organisms becomes a planetary mechanism in climate science.
senses.whyCN: 界定这些生物的漂流与下沉，在气候科学中成为一套行星尺度的机制。

senses.title: Fossil plankton and ancient oceans
senses.titleCN: 化石浮游生物与古海洋
senses.definition: the mineral shells of plankton preserved in sediment, used to reconstruct past water temperatures and currents
senses.definitionCN: 保存在沉积物中的浮游生物矿质壳，用于重建古代水温与洋流
senses.example: Fossil plankton in the core place the ancient shoreline within the tropics.
senses.exampleCN: 岩芯中的化石浮游生物把古代海岸线定位在热带范围内。
senses.why: hard parts survive where soft bodies do not, so the community leaves a readable record in rock.
senses.whyCN: 硬壳在软体无法保存的地方留存下来，因此这个群落能在岩石中留下可读的记录。

intro.en: Plankton was coined in German as Plankton in 1887 by the marine biologist Victor Hensen, from Greek planktos 'wandering, drifting', the verbal adjective of plazesthai 'to wander'. English adopted it soon after. The word is wholly Greek and has no Latin cognate.
intro.cn: plankton 由海洋生物学家亨森于 1887 年以德语 Plankton 造出，源自希腊 planktos「漂泊的」——动词 plazesthai「漫游」的动词形容词。英语随后借入。该词纯属希腊来源，没有拉丁同族词。

items.en: Plazesthai meant 'to wander, roam, drift about'. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and not all the Greek verbal forms built on the same base are securely related; any Indo-European ancestor is a reconstruction.
items.cn: plazesthai 意为「漫游、徘徊、漂移不定」。其更深来源不确定，建于同一词基的希腊动词形式也并非都可靠同源；凡拟出的印欧语祖形均属重构形式。

items.en: Planktos is the verbal adjective 'wandering, drifting', formed from the same verb; it describes what is carried about rather than what moves itself.
items.cn: planktos 是由同一动词构成的动词形容词，意为「漂泊的、漂移的」；它描述被水流带着走的东西，而非自己移动的东西。

items.en: Victor Hensen introduced German Plankton in 1887 for the drifting community, contrasting it with nekton, the swimmers, and benthos, the bottom dwellers.
items.cn: 亨森于 1887 年提出德语 Plankton，指漂流生物群落，与自游的 nekton、底栖的 benthos 相对。

items.en: English borrowed plankton in the late nineteenth century; the exact first English citation is uncertain, but the term was established in marine science by the 1890s.
items.cn: 英语于 19 世纪末借入 plankton；最早的英语书证年代不确定，但到 19 世纪 90 年代该词已确立于海洋科学。

items.en: Phytoplankton and zooplankton were coined soon afterwards to separate the photosynthetic from the animal members, and bacterioplankton followed in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 此后不久便造出 phytoplankton 与 zooplankton，以区分光合成员与动物成员；bacterioplankton 于 20 世纪出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): Hensen's 1887 coinage is documented, but the pre-Greek origin of plazesthai is reconstructed, and the precise first English use is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：亨森 1887 年的造词有文献可证，但 plazesthai 在希腊语之前的来源属重构，英语最早用例的确切年代亦无定论。

note.en: Group one separates plankton from look-alikes, including a Greek cousin in meaning and several unrelated words; group two places it among the other ecological categories of water life.
note.cn: 第一组把 plankton 与形近词分开，其中有一个意义上的希腊远亲，其余并无关系；第二组把它放进水中生物的其他生态类别中。

entries.definition: A flat length of timber, from Old French planche and Latin planca; the shared plank- string is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 指一块扁平的木板，来自古法语 planche 与拉丁 planca；共同的 plank- 字母串只是巧合。

entries.definition: Loud and mournful, from Latin plangere 'to strike, lament'; it resembles plankton in sound but comes from a Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指响亮而哀伤的，来自拉丁 plangere「击打、哀悼」；读音近似 plankton，但出自拉丁动词。

entries.definition: From Greek planetes 'wanderer', built on planasthai 'to wander'; it shares the notion of wandering with plankton, but the relation between the two Greek verbs is disputed and the referent is a heavenly body.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 planetes「漫游者」，建于 planasthai「漫游」；它与 plankton 共享「漂泊」这一意念，但两个希腊动词之间的关系有争议，且所指为天体。

entries.definition: The singular term for one planktonic organism, formed from plankton; it is a derivative, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个浮游生物的术语，由 plankton 构成；它是派生词，并非另一词根。

entries.definition: The photosynthetic subset of plankton; it is a part of plankton, not a synonym for the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 浮游生物中行光合作用的子集；它是浮游生物的一部分，并非整体的同义词。

entries.definition: The animal subset of plankton, grazing on phytoplankton; again a part, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 浮游生物中的动物子集，以浮游植物为食；同样是部分而非整体。

entries.definition: Organisms that can swim against a current, such as fish; Hensen coined it as the opposite of plankton.
entries.definitionCN: 能逆流游泳的生物，如鱼类；亨森把它作为 plankton 的对立类别而造出。

entries.definition: Organisms living on or in the bottom sediment; it contrasts with plankton, which lives suspended in the water.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在底部沉积物表面或其中的生物；与悬浮在水中的浮游生物相对。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek planktos 'wandering' plus the noun ending -on: the wandering mass, named in 1887 by Hensen.
normal.cn: 希腊 planktos「漂泊」加名词词尾 -on：漂泊的一团，由亨森于 1887 年命名。

normal.en: Hensen's three categories: plankton drifts, nekton swims, benthos rests on the bottom.
normal.cn: 亨森的三分法：浮游生物漂流，自游生物游泳，底栖生物栖于水底。

normal.en: Compounds split the community: phytoplankton, zooplankton, bacterioplankton.
normal.cn: 复合词把群落分开：浮游植物、浮游动物、浮游细菌。

normal.en: The adjective is planktonic, the individual is a plankter, and the science is planktology.
normal.cn: 形容词是 planktonic，单个个体是 plankter，学科是 planktology。

normal.en: Plankton is a mass noun: ecologists treat it as a plural community, while 'planktons' is used only for separate types.
normal.cn: plankton 是集合名词：生态学者把它当作复数群体，而 planktons 只用于指不同类群。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd carried along a moving escalator, unable to walk back up.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人被移动的扶梯带着走，谁也没法逆着走回去。

abstract.en: Picture dust in a shaft of sunlight: each speck is tiny, but together they dim the room.
abstract.cn: 想象阳光柱里的尘埃：每一粒都极小，合起来却让屋子变暗。

abstract.en: Picture a slow snowfall in reverse, flakes rising to feed everything above them.
abstract.cn: 想象一场倒放的慢雪，雪片向上飘，供养上方的一切。

examples.en: Plankton form the base of the food web in both open ocean and lakes.
examples.cn: 无论在开阔大洋还是湖泊，浮游生物都构成食物网的基础。

examples.en: A sudden plankton bloom can deplete oxygen when it decays.
examples.cn: 突然暴发的浮游生物在腐烂时会耗尽水中的氧。

examples.en: Plankton shells in the sediment record past sea temperatures.
examples.cn: 沉积物中的浮游生物壳记录了过去的海洋温度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「plankton」读似「扑浪啃」——微小生物扑在浪上，随浪漂流啃食，正是浮游生物

root: 希腊 planktos「漂泊的」，为 plazesthai「漫游」的动词形容词；1887 年亨森造德语 Plankton，随后进入英语；纯希腊来源，无拉丁同族；plazesthai 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the community to its parts, then to its mass, its role in the food web, its carbon pump and its fossil record. The single image is a cloud of small bodies that goes where the water goes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由群落整体移向其组成部分，再到生物量、食物网中的角色、碳泵与化石记录。贯穿其中的意象只有一团微小躯体：水去哪里，它们就去哪里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloud of tiny bodies suspended in water, moving only as the water moves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团悬浮在水中的微小躯体，只随水的运动而运动。

branches.en: THE COLLECTIVE: the mass noun names a community, whether global or local.
branches.cn: 集合体：这个集合名词命名的是一群落，无论全球还是局部。

branches.en: TWO HALVES: plants that photosynthesise and animals that graze.
branches.cn: 两半：行光合作用的植物与取食的动物。

branches.en: MEASURED MASS: abundance becomes biomass and then a visible bloom.
branches.cn: 可测的质量：丰度化为生物量，再化为肉眼可见的藻华。

branches.en: PLANETARY ROLE: food for fish and a pump that sinks carbon.
branches.cn: 行星角色：既是鱼类的食物，又是把碳沉下去的一台泵。

branches.en: DURABLE TRACE: shells survive as fossils and record ancient water.
branches.cn: 耐久的痕迹：壳作为化石留存，记录古代的水况。

intro.en: Plankton is Greek throughout: the root plankt- 'drifting' plus the noun ending -on. English builds the adjectives with -ic, the individual with -er, and the science with -logy and -logist; compounds add Greek combining forms.
intro.cn: plankton 从头到尾都是希腊语：词根 plankt-「漂泊」加名词词尾 -on。英语用 -ic 构成形容词，用 -er 指单个个体，用 -logy 与 -logist 指学科与学者；复合词则加入希腊语构词成分。

latinIntro.en: Plankton has no Latin source and no Latin cognate. Latin-based terms such as suspension are only semantic equivalents, not relatives, so the list of Latin entries is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: plankton 没有拉丁语来源，也没有拉丁同族词。像 suspension（悬浮物）这样的拉丁系词只是语义对应，并非亲属，因此拉丁条目留空。

items.example: Planktos describes what the current carries.
items.exampleCN: planktos 描述被水流带走的东西。

items.example: The root plankt- joins the word to new compounds.
items.exampleCN: 词根 plankt- 把这个词接入新的复合词。

items.example: Plankton drifts with the current.
items.exampleCN: 浮游生物随水流漂移。

items.example: Planktonic larvae spend weeks in the open water.
items.exampleCN: 浮游幼虫在开阔水域度过数周。

items.example: Planktic foraminifera leave chalky shells.
items.exampleCN: 浮游有孔虫留下白垩质的壳。

items.example: Each plankter is too small to swim against the tide.
items.exampleCN: 每个浮游生物都太小，无法逆潮游动。

items.example: Phytoplankton supply half of the oxygen we breathe.
items.exampleCN: 浮游植物提供我们呼吸所需氧气的一半。

items.example: Zooplankton graze the spring bloom.
items.exampleCN: 浮游动物取食春季的藻华。

items.example: Bacterioplankton recycle nutrients in the dark water.
items.exampleCN: 浮游细菌在暗水中循环养分。

definition_zh: 浮游植物；光合浮游生物；浮游植物群落；藻华（浮游植物大量繁殖）；初级生产；碳固定；群落组成与季节演替；生态监测与遥感对象
definition_en: the community of microscopic, photosynthetic organisms that drift in the sunlit upper layers of lakes and seas and form the base of most aquatic food webs
core_image: 阳光照进水面下几十米，无数比头发丝还细的绿色细胞悬在水中，随水流慢慢漂
scene: 远洋的表层水里，微小到看不见的绿色细胞随洋流漂走，把阳光变成整条食物链的第一环。In the open sea, phytoplankton drift wherever the current takes them and turn sunlight into the first link of the food web.
sceneCN: 这里 phytoplankton 指「随水流漂移的光合微生物群落」（第 1 个义项：水体中营浮游生活的光合生物总称）；句意：在开阔海面上，浮游植物随洋流漂到哪里就在哪里，把阳光转化成食物网的第一环。图中可辨识物件：透光的表层水、悬浮的绿色微粒、缓慢的水流线、俯视的海面。

pos.zh: 浮游植物（营浮游生活、进行光合作用的微小生物群落，通常作不可数集合名词）
（生态学）某水域或某季节的浮游植物类群与组成

forms.label: 名词（单个浮游植物个体）

derivatives.zh: 浮游植物的；由浮游植物构成的
单个浮游植物个体（生态学用语）
浮游植物藻华（细胞数骤增、肉眼可见的水色变化）
以浮游植物为基础的（如以浮游植物为基础的食物网）

senses.title: The drifting photosynthetic community
senses.titleCN: 随水漂移的光合微生物群落（浮游植物总称）
senses.definition: the whole assemblage of microscopic algae and cyanobacteria that live suspended in water and drift with currents rather than swimming against them
senses.definitionCN: 悬在水中、随水流漂移而不逆流游动的微小藻类与蓝细菌的总体
senses.example: In the open sea, phytoplankton drift wherever the current takes them and turn sunlight into the first food of the food web.
senses.exampleCN: 在开阔海面上，浮游植物随洋流漂到哪里就在哪里，把阳光转化成食物网的第一份食物。
senses.why: phyto- marks the plant-like, photosynthetic half of plankton, so the word names a functional community rather than a single species.
senses.whyCN: phyto- 标出 plankton 中「像植物、能进行光合作用」的那一半，因此这个词指的是一类功能群，而非某一个物种。

senses.title: One drifting cell
senses.titleCN: 单个浮游植物细胞（个体义）
senses.definition: one individual cell or organism of this community, counted in cell counts, cultures and net samples
senses.definitionCN: 这一群落中的单个细胞或个体，在细胞计数、培养与网采样品中逐个统计
senses.example: A single phytoplankton cell may divide twice a day when nutrients are plentiful.
senses.exampleCN: 养分充足时，一个浮游植物细胞一天可以分裂两次。
senses.why: collective nouns for tiny organisms are regularly used countably once sampling makes the individual the unit of measurement.
senses.whyCN: 微小生物的集合名词一旦进入采样统计、个体成为计量单位，就常被当作可数名词使用。

senses.title: Photosynthetic plankton, bacteria included
senses.titleCN: 光合浮游生物（含蓝细菌，不严格限于植物）
senses.definition: all sunlight-driven drifting producers, including cyanobacteria that are bacteria rather than true plants
senses.definitionCN: 所有靠阳光获取能量的漂浮生产者，包括属于细菌而非真正植物的蓝细菌
senses.example: Much of the open-ocean phytoplankton is actually cyanobacteria of the genus Prochlorococcus.
senses.exampleCN: 开阔洋面的浮游植物中，很大一部分其实是原绿球藻属的蓝细菌。
senses.why: the name was coined before the bacterial nature of cyanobacteria was understood, and it has kept a plant-like label for the function rather than the taxonomy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在人们认识蓝细菌的细菌本质之前就已造出，此后沿用的是功能上的「像植物」，而非分类上的归属。

senses.title: A dense surface accumulation
senses.titleCN: 藻华：浮游植物在水面大量聚集
senses.definition: a sharp, visible rise in cell numbers that stains the water green, brown or red and can deplete oxygen when the cells decay
senses.definitionCN: 细胞数量骤增并肉眼可见，使水呈绿、褐或红色，细胞死亡分解时会耗尽水中的氧
senses.example: A spring phytoplankton bloom turned the bay milky green within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一场春季浮游植物藻华在一周内把海湾染成了乳绿色。
senses.why: when the community multiplies beyond the control of grazers it becomes an event with its own name, and speakers use the same noun for that event.
senses.whyCN: 当群落增殖到摄食者无法控制时，它就成了一个有独立名称的事件，说话人便用同一个名词指称该事件。

senses.title: Primary production at the base of the web
senses.titleCN: 初级生产：把无机碳变成新的生物量
senses.definition: the conversion of dissolved carbon into new organic matter by these organisms, measured as production per unit area or volume
senses.definitionCN: 这些生物把溶解态碳转化为新的有机物质，以单位面积或体积的生产量计量
senses.example: Satellite colour data estimate ocean phytoplankton production over whole basins.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星颜色数据可以估算整个海盆的浮游植物生产量。
senses.why: the producers and their activity share one name because ecology studies the standing stock and its growth rate together.
senses.whyCN: 在生态学中，现存生物量与其增长速率是一起研究的，因此生产者与其活动用同一个词指称。

senses.title: Carbon fixed and carried down
senses.titleCN: 碳固定与向深层输出的碳
senses.definition: the carbon drawn out of seawater by photosynthesis and the part of it that sinks as particles into deep water
senses.definitionCN: 光合作用从海水中取走的碳，以及其中以颗粒形式下沉到深水的那一部分
senses.example: Phytoplankton fix carbon near the surface, and a fraction of that carbon reaches the seabed.
senses.exampleCN: 浮游植物在表层固定碳，其中一部分最终到达海底。
senses.why: because fixation happens inside these organisms, the word stands for the flux they drive in climate and carbon-cycle writing.
senses.whyCN: 固定发生在这些生物体内，因此在气候与碳循环文献中，这个词直接代表它们驱动的通量。

senses.title: Which species dominate, and when
senses.titleCN: 群落组成与季节演替
senses.definition: the mix of species and size classes present, and the ordered change from diatoms to flagellates and back through the year
senses.definitionCN: 现存的物种与粒级组合，以及一年中从硅藻到鞭毛藻再返回的有序更替
senses.example: The phytoplankton shifts from diatoms in spring to small flagellates in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 浮游植物在春季以硅藻为主，到夏季转为小型鞭毛藻。
senses.why: community ecology treats the assemblage as a study object with composition and succession, and the noun carries that abstract sense.
senses.whyCN: 群落生态学把这一组合当作有组成、有演替的研究对象，名词便承载了这一抽象含义。

senses.title: An object of monitoring and remote sensing
senses.titleCN: 生态监测与遥感观测的对象
senses.definition: the variable tracked by chlorophyll sensors, water-colour satellites and long-term plankton records to judge water quality and change
senses.definitionCN: 通过叶绿素传感器、水色卫星与长期浮游生物记录追踪的变量，用于判断水质与变化
senses.example: Scientists monitor phytoplankton from space to detect harmful blooms early.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家从太空监测浮游植物，以便及早发现有害藻华。
senses.why: anything measured routinely becomes a shorthand for the measurement programme, so the organism's name doubles as the name of the monitoring target.
senses.whyCN: 凡被例行测量的对象，其名称常兼指整套测量工作，于是这种生物的名字也成了监测目标的名称。

intro.en: Phytoplankton is a scientific compound of the late nineteenth century: Greek phyton 'plant' joined to plankton, a term coined in 1887 by the German biologist Viktor Hensen for the community that drifts in water. Both elements are Greek, and there is no Latin source.
intro.cn: phytoplankton 是 19 世纪后期出现的科学复合词：希腊语 phyton「植物」加上 plankton，后者由德国生物学家 Hensen 于 1887 年为水中漂移的生物群落创制。两个构件都来自希腊语，没有拉丁语来源。

items.en: Phyton meant 'plant', from phyein 'to grow'; the same verb underlies physis 'nature'. The Indo-European base behind phyein is reconstructed as bheue- 'to be, exist, grow', a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: phyton 意为「植物」，源于 phyein「生长」；同一个动词也构成 physis「自然」。phyein 之前的印欧语词根被重构为 bheue-「存在、生长」，那只是重构形式，并非有记载的词形。

items.en: Planktos 'wandering, drifting' is a verbal adjective of planasthai 'to wander'. The deeper origin of planasthai is uncertain, and the link sometimes drawn to a root meaning 'to strike or drive' is a hypothesis only.
items.cn: planktos「漫游的、漂荡的」是动词 planasthai「漫游」的动形容词。planasthai 的更早来源不确定；有人把它与意为「击打、驱赶」的词根相联系，那只是假说。

items.en: In 1887 Hensen proposed Plankton for the small organisms that float in the sea and cannot swim against currents; the German form was taken into English within a few years.
items.cn: 1887 年，Hensen 提出用 Plankton 指那些漂浮在海中、无法逆流游动的小型生物；这一德语词形在几年内被英语采用。

items.en: Phytoplankton is recorded from the 1890s, built by attaching phyto- to plankton in order to separate the photosynthetic half of the drifting community from the animal half.
items.cn: phytoplankton 自 19 世纪 90 年代起见于记载，做法是把 phyto- 接到 plankton 前，以把漂流群落中行光合作用的一半与动物的一半分开。

items.en: Phyto- then became a productive scientific prefix in phytohormone, phytolith and phytoremediation, always carrying the sense 'plant'.
items.cn: 此后 phyto- 成为能产的科技术语前缀，见于 phytohormone、phytolith、phytoremediation，始终带「植物」之义。

items.en: Source partly uncertain: the exact first English citation is not fixed, and the pre-Greek origin of planasthai is unsettled, so any Indo-European base given for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源部分不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：确切的最早英语书证尚无定论；planasthai 在希腊语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为其给出的印欧语词根均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that overlap with phytoplankton in spelling or in one Greek element, some genuinely related and some not; group two holds terms from the same ecological field whose scope differs.
note.cn: 第一组是与 phytoplankton 拼写相近或共享某个希腊语构件的词，其中有真同源，也有仅形近；第二组是同一生态领域内范围不同的术语。

entries.definition: Shares the -plankton element and means all drifting organisms, both photosynthetic and animal; phytoplankton is only its plant-like half.
entries.definitionCN: 共享 -plankton 构件，指全部漂移生物，既有光合的也有动物的；phytoplankton 只是其中像植物的一半。

entries.definition: The animal counterpart, built from the same plankton with Greek zōion 'animal'; the two words divide the drifting community by kingdom, not by size.
entries.definitionCN: 动物的一半，用同一个 plankton 加希腊语 zōion「动物」构成；两词按界而非按体径划分漂流群落。

entries.definition: A size fraction of plankton between about 2 and 20 micrometres, containing both algae and tiny animals; it is not a synonym because the criterion is size.
entries.definitionCN: 粒径约 2 至 20 微米的浮游生物粒级，藻类与小动物都有；因为划分标准是体径，所以并非同义词。

entries.definition: A flat piece of timber; the resemblance to plankton is accidental, since plank comes through Old French from Latin planca, with no link to Greek planktos.
entries.definitionCN: 一块平板木料；与 plankton 的相似纯属偶然，plank 经古法语来自拉丁 planca，与希腊 planktos 无关。

entries.definition: Microscopic algae as a group, including attached and bottom-dwelling forms; phytoplankton is the drifting subset, so the two overlap only partly.
entries.definitionCN: 微小藻类的总称，包括附着与底栖种类；phytoplankton 是其中漂移的那一部分，两者只部分重合。

entries.definition: The whole class of algal organisms, from seaweeds to single cells; phytoplankton names those of them that live suspended and drifting.
entries.definitionCN: 藻类整体的类群名，从海藻到单细胞都有；phytoplankton 专指其中悬在水里漂移的那些。

entries.definition: Everything suspended in a water column, living plankton plus dead matter and mineral particles; it is broader and includes non-living material.
entries.definitionCN: 水柱中悬浮的一切，包括活体浮游生物、死有机物与矿物颗粒；范围更宽，含非生命物质。

entries.definition: Any organism that builds organic matter from sunlight or chemical energy; phytoplankton is the main aquatic case, but the term also covers land plants.
entries.definitionCN: 任何借阳光或化学能制造有机物的生物；phytoplankton 是水中的主要例子，但该词也涵盖陆地植物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Phyto- is the Greek prefix for 'plant', so phytoplankton is literally the plant-like plankton.
normal.cn: phyto- 是希腊语「植物」前缀，因此 phytoplankton 字面就是「像植物的浮游生物」。

normal.en: The pair phytoplankton and zooplankton splits drifting life by kingdom; both remain plankton.
normal.cn: phytoplankton 与 zooplankton 一对词按界划分漂流生物；两者都仍属于 plankton。

normal.en: Diatoms and coccolithophores are the best-known members, single cells with silica or chalk shells.
normal.cn: 硅藻与颗石藻是最知名的成员，都是带硅质或钙质外壳的单细胞。

normal.en: Blooms are often named by colour, and green, brown and red water all come from phytoplankton pigments.
normal.cn: 藻华常按颜色命名，绿水、褐水与红水都来自浮游植物的色素。

normal.en: Satellites read chlorophyll, so phytoplankton shows up in climate and water-quality reports as a measured quantity.
normal.cn: 卫星读取叶绿素，因此浮游植物在气候与水质报告中以一个被测量的量出现。

abstract.en: Picture a sunlit surface layer full of green dust that no net can hold still.
abstract.cn: 想象一层被阳光照透的表层水，满是网也留不住的绿色微尘。

abstract.en: Picture a bloom as paint poured into a bay, thick enough to change the colour of the whole coast.
abstract.cn: 想象藻华像颜料倒进海湾，浓到改变了整条海岸的颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a slow snow of dead cells falling through the dark water toward the seabed.
abstract.cn: 想象一场由死细胞组成的慢雪，穿过黑暗的水层落向海底。

examples.en: Phytoplankton in the Southern Ocean bloom when iron-rich dust falls on the surface.
examples.cn: 南大洋的浮游植物在富铁尘埃落到海面时大量繁殖。

examples.en: The lake's phytoplankton community shifted from diatoms to cyanobacteria after the fertilizer runoff.
examples.cn: 化肥径流进入后，湖里的浮游植物群落从硅藻转为蓝细菌。

examples.en: Chlorophyll measurements let researchers track phytoplankton across entire ocean basins.
examples.cn: 叶绿素测量让研究者得以追踪整个海盆的浮游植物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「phyto」读似「肥头」、「plankton」读似「扑浪腾」——肥头小植物扑在浪里腾着漂，正是浮游植物；纯属谐音，非词源

root: 希腊语 phyton「植物」（源于 phyein「生长」）+ plankton「漂泊者」（希腊 planktos「漂荡的」，源自 planasthai「漫游」）；plankton 由德国生物学家 Hensen 于 1887 年创制，phyto- 为希腊语构词成分。planasthai 的更早来源不确定，相关印欧语词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: sunlight entering water and being captured by drifting cells. The community is named first, then the single cell, then the bacterial members, and from the community's behaviour come the bloom, the production rate, the carbon flux, the seasonal turnover and finally the monitoring target.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个意象展开：阳光进入水中，被漂移的细胞捕获。先指整个群落，再指单个细胞，再指其中的细菌成员；由群落的行为又引出藻华、生产速率、碳通量、季节更替，最后是被监测的对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sunlight caught by microscopic cells that drift instead of swimming.
core.cn: 核心意象：阳光被微小细胞捕获，这些细胞靠漂移而非游动移动。

branches.en: THE COMMUNITY AND THE CELL: one word for the assemblage, one countable reading for a single cell.
branches.cn: 群落与细胞：同一个词既指整个组合，也可数地指单个细胞。

branches.en: FUNCTION, NOT TAXONOMY: the label follows photosynthesis, so bacteria are included.
branches.cn: 按功能而非分类：标签跟着光合作用走，因此细菌也被算入。

branches.en: BLOOM AS EVENT: unchecked multiplication turns the community into a visible occurrence.
branches.cn: 藻华作为事件：不受控的增殖把群落变成可见的事件。

branches.en: PRODUCTION, FLUX AND TURNOVER: the same cells are read as a rate, a carbon flow and a seasonal sequence.
branches.cn: 生产、通量与更替：同一批细胞被读成速率、碳流与季节序列。

branches.en: MEASURED OBJECT: what is sensed by satellite becomes a variable in reports.
branches.cn: 被测量的对象：卫星感知到的东西成了报告里的变量。

intro.en: Phytoplankton is built entirely from Greek material: the combining form phyto- 'plant' plus plankton 'that which drifts'. Both parts remain productive in scientific English.
intro.cn: phytoplankton 完全由希腊语材料构成：构词成分 phyto-「植物」加 plankton「漂移之物」。两部分在科技英语中至今能产。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in phytoplankton; both components are Greek, and the ending -on is a Greek neuter ending that only looks Latin. Latin-based words such as algae translate the idea but are not sources, so latinEntries is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: phytoplankton 中没有拉丁语构件；两个成分都是希腊语，词尾 -on 是希腊语中性词尾，只是看起来像拉丁语。algae 这类拉丁语系的词只是语义对应，并非来源，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.example: Phyto- appears in phytotoxin and phytolith.
items.exampleCN: phyto- 出现在 phytotoxin 与 phytolith 中。

items.meaning: a plant, literally the thing that has grown
items.meaningCN: 植物，字面是「长出来的东西」
items.example: The Greek phyton is the source of the combining form.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 phyton 是这个构词成分的来源。

items.structure: plankton (Greek adjective used as a noun, 'drifting thing')
items.example: Plankton was first used as a scientific collective in 1887.
items.exampleCN: plankton 于 1887 年首次作为科学集合名词使用。

items.example: Planktos describes anything that is carried about by water.
items.exampleCN: planktos 描述任何被水带着走的东西。

items.example: Phytoplankton fuels the open-ocean food web.
items.exampleCN: 浮游植物支撑着开阔洋面的食物网。

items.meaningCN: 浮游植物的；属于浮游植物的
items.example: The phytoplanktonic layer sits in the top metre of water.
items.exampleCN: 浮游植物层位于水体最上面一米。

items.meaning: one individual member of the community
items.example: Each phytoplankter is a single cell a few micrometres wide.
items.exampleCN: 每个浮游植物个体都是宽几微米的单细胞。

items.meaningCN: 粒径 2 至 20 微米的浮游生物粒级
items.example: Nanoplankton often dominates the summer cell counts.
items.exampleCN: 夏季细胞计数中，微型浮游生物常占多数。

items.meaning: the animal half of the drifting community
items.meaningCN: 漂流群落中动物的一半
items.example: Zooplankton graze on phytoplankton after dark.
items.exampleCN: 浮游动物在天黑后摄食浮游植物。

definition_zh: 浮游动物；浮游动物群落；摄食浮游植物的浮游动物；昼夜垂直迁移；次级生产；群落结构与指示物种；鱼类饵料；生物泵与碳输出
definition_en: the community of small animals, larvae and protozoans that drift in water, feed on phytoplankton and other particles, and pass that energy up the food web
core_image: 夜里成群的微小甲壳类从深水升到水面进食，天亮又沉回暗处，像一层会呼吸的地毯上下移动
scene: 入夜后，成群的微小甲壳类从数百米深处升到水面进食，天亮前又沉回暗处。After sunset, zooplankton rise hundreds of metres to feed near the surface and sink back into the dark before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 zooplankton 指「夜晚上浮摄食、黎明下沉的浮游动物」（第 4 个义项：昼夜垂直迁移）；句意：日落后，浮游动物上升到数百米浅处进食，黎明前又沉回黑暗的深处。图中可辨识物件：夜间的表层水、成群的微小甲壳类、标示深浅的水层剖面、水面上的月光。

pos.zh: 浮游动物（营浮游生活的小型动物与原生动物群落，通常作不可数集合名词）
（生态学）某水域或某水层的浮游动物类群与组成

forms.label: 名词（单个浮游动物个体）

derivatives.zh: 浮游动物的；由浮游动物构成的
单个浮游动物个体（生态学用语）
摄食浮游植物的浮游动物（牧食者）
以浮游动物为基础的（如以浮游动物为基础的食物链）

senses.title: The drifting animal community
senses.titleCN: 随水漂移的动物群落（浮游动物总称）
senses.definition: the whole assemblage of small animals, larvae and protozoans that live suspended in water and are carried by currents rather than swimming against them
senses.definitionCN: 悬在水中、被水流带走而不逆流游动的小型动物、幼体与原生动物总体
senses.example: After sunset, zooplankton rise hundreds of metres to feed near the surface and sink back into the dark before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 日落后，浮游动物上升到数百米浅处进食，黎明前又沉回黑暗的深处。
senses.why: zoo- marks the animal half of plankton, so the word names a functional community defined by drifting, not by a single phylum.
senses.whyCN: zoo- 标出 plankton 中属于动物的那一半，因此这个词定义的是一个靠漂移为生的功能群，而非单一门类。

senses.title: One drifting animal
senses.titleCN: 单个浮游动物个体
senses.definition: one individual animal or protozoan of this community, counted per litre or per net haul
senses.definitionCN: 这一群落中的单个动物或原生动物，按每升水或每网次计数
senses.example: A single zooplankton can filter several millilitres of water an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 一个浮游动物每小时能滤过好几毫升水。
senses.why: once samples are counted individual by individual, the collective noun is used countably for one organism.
senses.whyCN: 样品一旦逐个计数，集合名词就被当作可数名词指一个个体。

senses.title: Grazers that crop the phytoplankton
senses.titleCN: 摄食浮游植物的牧食者
senses.definition: the herbivorous part of the community, which filters or bites phytoplankton and controls how much of it remains
senses.definitionCN: 群落中植食的那一部分，通过滤食或咬食浮游植物，控制其留存数量
senses.example: Zooplankton grazing can end a phytoplankton bloom within days.
senses.exampleCN: 浮游动物的摄食能在几天内终结一场浮游植物藻华。
senses.why: the word often stands for the grazing link itself, because the animals' main ecological function is cropping the producers.
senses.whyCN: 这些动物的主要生态功能就是收割生产者，因此这个词常直接指这条牧食关系。

senses.title: The nightly rise and dawn descent
senses.titleCN: 昼夜垂直迁移
senses.definition: the daily movement of the community from deep, dark water by day to shallow, food-rich water at night
senses.definitionCN: 群落每天从白天所在的深暗水层移动到夜间饵料丰富的浅层
senses.example: Lunar light can suppress zooplankton migration on clear nights.
senses.exampleCN: 晴朗的夜里，月光会抑制浮游动物的垂直迁移。
senses.why: the migration is so regular and so visible on sonar that the noun often names the movement rather than the animals.
senses.whyCN: 这场迁移如此规律，在声呐上如此显眼，名词便常指这一移动本身而非动物。

senses.title: Secondary production
senses.titleCN: 次级生产：把植物性食物转成动物生物量
senses.definition: the new animal biomass built from phytoplankton and other food, measured as growth per unit area or volume
senses.definitionCN: 由浮游植物等食物转化成的新的动物生物量，以单位面积或体积的增长量计量
senses.example: Zooplankton production links algal growth to the fish catch.
senses.exampleCN: 浮游动物生产量把藻类生长与渔获量连接起来。
senses.why: in ecology the standing stock and its growth rate share one name, so the animals also stand for the production they generate.
senses.whyCN: 在生态学中，现存量与其增长率共用一个名称，因此这些动物也代表它们产生的生产量。

senses.title: Community structure and indicator value
senses.titleCN: 群落结构与指示物种
senses.definition: the species mix and size spectrum of the community, which reflects water mass, temperature and pollution and is read as an indicator
senses.definitionCN: 群落的物种组成与粒径谱，反映水团、温度与污染状况，并被读作指示
senses.example: The zooplankton assemblage indicated a cold, recently upwelled water mass.
senses.exampleCN: 浮游动物群落表明这里是一团刚涌升上来的冷水。
senses.why: because different assemblages track different water bodies, the community itself becomes a diagnostic sign in monitoring.
senses.whyCN: 不同群落对应不同水团，群落本身在监测中便成了诊断标志。

senses.title: Forage for fish and fisheries
senses.titleCN: 鱼类饵料与渔业基础
senses.definition: the prey base of fish larvae and small pelagic fish, whose abundance partly determines recruitment and catch
senses.definitionCN: 鱼苗与小型中上层鱼类的饵料基础，其丰度部分决定补充量与渔获
senses.example: Young cod depend on zooplankton during the first weeks after hatching.
senses.exampleCN: 鳕鱼幼鱼在孵化后的头几周依赖浮游动物。
senses.why: seen from the fish's side the community is simply food, and fisheries writing uses the word in that role.
senses.whyCN: 从鱼的角度看，这个群落就是食物，渔业文献便以这一角色使用该词。

senses.title: The biological pump
senses.titleCN: 生物泵：把碳送往深层
senses.definition: the process by which sinking animals, faecal pellets and dead bodies carry surface carbon into deep water and sediment
senses.definitionCN: 下沉的动物、粪粒与遗体把表层碳带入深水与沉积物的过程
senses.example: Zooplankton excretion and sinking pellets make the biological pump efficient.
senses.exampleCN: 浮游动物的排泄与下沉粪粒使生物泵更为高效。
senses.why: the animals act as the machinery of the pump, so their name is used for the carbon-export process they drive.
senses.whyCN: 这些动物是泵的机械部件，因此其名称被用来指它们驱动的碳输出过程。

intro.en: Zooplankton is a late nineteenth-century scientific compound: Greek zōion 'animal' plus plankton, the term coined in 1887 by Viktor Hensen for the community that drifts in water. Both elements are Greek, and there is no Latin source.
intro.cn: zooplankton 是 19 世纪后期的科学复合词：希腊语 zōion「动物」加上 plankton，后者由 Hensen 于 1887 年为水中漂移的生物群落创制。两个构件都来自希腊语，没有拉丁语来源。

items.en: Zōion 'animal' derives from zōos 'alive' and the noun zōē 'life'. The Indo-European base behind this family is reconstructed as gʷeyh₃- 'to live', a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: zōion「动物」源自 zōos「活的」与名词 zōē「生命」。这一词族背后的印欧语词根被重构为 gʷeyh₃-「活着」，那只是重构形式，并非有记载的词形。

items.en: Planktos 'wandering, drifting' is a verbal adjective of planasthai 'to wander'. The deeper origin of planasthai is uncertain, and the link sometimes drawn to a root meaning 'to strike or drive' is a hypothesis only.
items.cn: planktos「漫游的、漂荡的」是动词 planasthai「漫游」的动形容词。planasthai 的更早来源不确定；有人把它与意为「击打、驱赶」的词根相联系，那只是假说。

items.en: Hensen's Plankton covered all drifting organisms; the animal part was separated by adding zoo- to the same second element.
items.cn: Hensen 的 Plankton 涵盖全部漂移生物；把 zoo- 加到同一个第二构件前，就把其中动物的那一部分分了出来。

items.en: Zooplankton is recorded from the 1890s, in parallel with phytoplankton, so that the two halves of the drift community could be counted and discussed separately.
items.cn: zooplankton 自 19 世纪 90 年代起见于记载，与 phytoplankton 平行出现，使漂流群落的两半可以被分别计数与讨论。

items.en: Zoo- became a productive element in zoology, zoospore and zooxanthellae, always carrying the sense 'animal' or 'animal-like'.
items.cn: zoo- 成为能产构件，见于 zoology、zoospore、zooxanthellae，始终带「动物」或「似动物的」之义。

items.en: Source partly uncertain: the exact first English citation is not fixed, and the pre-Greek origin of planasthai is unsettled, so any Indo-European base given for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源部分不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：确切的最早英语书证尚无定论；planasthai 在希腊语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为其给出的印欧语词根均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that overlap with zooplankton in spelling or in one Greek element, some genuinely related and one not; group two holds terms from the same ecological field whose scope differs.
note.cn: 第一组是与 zooplankton 拼写相近或共享某个希腊语构件的词，其中有真同源，也有纯属形近；第二组是同一生态领域内范围不同的术语。

entries.definition: Shares the -plankton element and covers all drifting organisms; zooplankton is only its animal half.
entries.definitionCN: 共享 -plankton 构件，涵盖全部漂移生物；zooplankton 只是其中动物的一半。

entries.definition: The plant-like counterpart, built from the same plankton with Greek phyton 'plant'; it is the food of zooplankton rather than a name for it.
entries.definitionCN: 类植物的一半，用同一个 plankton 加希腊语 phyton「植物」构成；它是浮游动物的食物，而非其别称。

entries.definition: A swimming spore produced by some algae and fungi; it shares zoo- in the older sense 'moving' but is a reproductive cell, not a drifting animal.
entries.definitionCN: 某些藻类与真菌产生的游动孢子；它共享 zoo- 的旧义「会动的」，但属于生殖细胞，不是浮游动物。

entries.definition: To move quickly, or the action of a camera lens; it is imitative in origin and has no link to Greek zōion, so the resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 指快速移动，或相机镜头的变焦动作；该词源于拟声，与希腊语 zōion 无关，相似纯属偶然。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for the same community; zooplankton is its technical single-word form and can replace it in most contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 指同一群落的日常说法；zooplankton 是它技术化的单词形式，在多数语境中可替换使用。

entries.definition: The fraction between about 20 and 200 micrometres, mostly ciliates and small copepods; it is a part of zooplankton, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 粒径约 20 至 200 微米的部分，多为纤毛虫与小桡足类；它是浮游动物的一部分，而非全部。

entries.definition: The larger fraction, including krill and big copepods; again a size class inside the community rather than a synonym for it.
entries.definitionCN: 较大的部分，包括磷虾与大形桡足类；同样只是群落内的一个粒级，而非同义词。

entries.definition: A shrimp-like crustacean among the largest and most abundant zooplankton, especially in polar seas; it names one group inside the community.
entries.definitionCN: 一种似虾的甲壳类，是体型最大、数量最多的浮游动物之一，尤其在极地海域；它指群落中的一个类群。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Zoo- is the Greek element for 'animal', so zooplankton is literally the animal plankton.
normal.cn: zoo- 是希腊语「动物」构件，因此 zooplankton 字面就是「动物性的浮游生物」。

normal.en: The pair phytoplankton and zooplankton divides the drift community by kingdom, and the second eats the first.
normal.cn: phytoplankton 与 zooplankton 一对词按界划分漂流群落，后者吃前者。

normal.en: Copepods, krill and water fleas are the familiar members; fish larvae and protozoans are also counted in.
normal.cn: 桡足类、磷虾与溞类是熟悉的成员；鱼苗与原生动物也计入其中。

normal.en: Diel vertical migration is the standard example of daily behaviour in the open ocean.
normal.cn: 昼夜垂直迁移是开阔大洋中日常行为的经典例子。

normal.en: Echosounders see the migrating layer as a false sea floor, the so-called deep scattering layer.
normal.cn: 回声探测仪把迁移的水层看成假的「海底」，即所谓深散射层。

abstract.en: Picture a living carpet that climbs toward the moon and drops back before sunrise.
abstract.cn: 想象一张活的地毯，向着月亮爬升，又在日出前落回原处。

abstract.en: Picture a grazer that clears a green field overnight and then sinks out of sight.
abstract.cn: 想象一群食草者一夜之间清空绿野，然后沉出视野。

abstract.en: Picture a slow elevator of small bodies carrying carbon down into black water.
abstract.cn: 想象一部缓慢的电梯，载着小小的躯体把碳送进黑水。

examples.en: Zooplankton in the lake are dominated by copepods and water fleas.
examples.cn: 湖里的浮游动物以桡足类与溞类为主。

examples.en: At night the zooplankton layer rises close enough to the surface for divers to see it.
examples.cn: 夜里，浮游动物层升到离水面足够近的地方，潜水员都能看见。

examples.en: Warming water shifted the zooplankton community toward smaller species.
examples.cn: 水温升高使浮游动物群落转向更小的物种。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「zoo」读似「祖」、「plankton」读似「扑浪腾」——祖辈小动物扑在浪里腾着漂，正是浮游动物；纯属谐音，非词源

root: 希腊语 zōion「动物」（源自 zōos「活的」、zōē「生命」）+ plankton「漂泊者」（希腊 planktos「漂荡的」，源自 planasthai「漫游」）；zoo- 为希腊语构词成分。planasthai 的更早来源不确定，相关印欧语词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: small animals that rise at night to graze and sink at dawn. The community is named first, then the single animal, then its grazing, its migration, its growth, its composition, its role as fish food and finally its work in the carbon pump.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个意象展开：小动物夜里上升进食，黎明下沉。先指群落，再指单个动物，然后是它的摄食、迁移、生长、组成、作为鱼饵的角色，最后是它在碳泵中的工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small animals that rise at night to graze and sink at dawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：小动物夜里升上来进食，天亮又沉下去。

branches.en: THE COMMUNITY AND THE ANIMAL: one word for the assemblage, one countable reading per organism.
branches.cn: 群落与个体：同一个词既指整个组合，也可按个体计数。

branches.en: THE GRAZING LINK: the animals are named by what they do to the producers.
branches.cn: 牧食关系：这些动物按它们对生产者所做的事来命名。

branches.en: DAILY RISE, ONGOING GROWTH: migration is behaviour, secondary production is the biomass it builds.
branches.cn: 每日上升与持续增长：迁移是行为，次级生产是它积累的动物生物量。

branches.en: COMPOSITION AND PREY: the assemblage indicates water bodies and feeds fish.
branches.cn: 组成与饵料：群落既指示水团，也喂养鱼类。

branches.en: THE PUMP: sinking bodies turn the community into a carbon conveyor.
branches.cn: 生物泵：下沉的躯体把群落变成一条碳的传送带。

intro.en: Zooplankton is built entirely from Greek material: the combining form zoo- 'animal' plus plankton 'that which drifts'. Both parts remain productive in scientific English.
intro.cn: zooplankton 完全由希腊语材料构成：构词成分 zoo-「动物」加 plankton「漂移之物」。两部分在科技英语中至今能产。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in zooplankton; both components are Greek, and the ending -on is a Greek neuter ending. Latin and Latin-based words that translate the idea are semantic counterparts, not sources, so latinEntries is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: zooplankton 中没有拉丁语构件；两个成分都是希腊语，词尾 -on 是希腊语中性词尾。翻译这一概念的拉丁语及拉丁语系词只是语义对应，并非来源，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.example: Zoo- appears in zoology and zoogeography.
items.exampleCN: zoo- 出现在 zoology 与 zoogeography 中。

items.example: The Greek zōion is the source of the combining form.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 zōion 是这个构词成分的来源。

items.structure: plankton (Greek adjective used as a noun, 'drifting thing')
items.example: Plankton was first used as a scientific collective in 1887.
items.exampleCN: plankton 于 1887 年首次作为科学集合名词使用。

items.example: Planktos describes anything carried about by water.
items.exampleCN: planktos 描述任何被水带着走的东西。

items.example: Zooplankton feeds the fish of the open sea.
items.exampleCN: 浮游动物喂养着开阔海域的鱼类。

items.meaningCN: 浮游动物的；属于浮游动物的
items.example: The zooplanktonic layer is thin by day and thick by night.
items.exampleCN: 浮游动物层白天薄、夜里厚。

items.meaning: one individual member of the community
items.example: Each zooplankter was counted under the microscope.
items.exampleCN: 每个浮游动物个体都在显微镜下被计数。

items.meaningCN: 粒径 20 至 200 微米的浮游动物部分
items.example: Microzooplankton graze most of the small algae.
items.exampleCN: 微型浮游动物摄食了大部分小型藻类。

items.structure: zoo- + Greek xanthos 'yellow' + Latinised plural ending
items.meaning: single-celled algae living inside coral tissues
items.meaningCN: 生活在珊瑚组织内的单细胞藻
items.example: Zooxanthellae give reef corals their colour.
items.exampleCN: 虫黄藻赋予礁珊瑚颜色。

definition_zh: 藻类（总称）；单细胞藻（微藻）；大型海藻；淡水藻；藻华与赤潮；生物燃料与养殖；共生藻；化石藻与古环境
definition_en: the large and varied group of mainly aquatic organisms that photosynthesise without true roots, stems or leaves, ranging from single cells to seaweeds
core_image: 退潮后的礁石上覆着一层滑腻的褐绿色薄膜，远处海带的长带随浪摆动
scene: 退潮后的礁石上覆着一层滑腻的褐绿色薄膜，浅水里还有成片的长带随浪摆动。At low tide the rocks are covered with a slippery brown-green film of algae, and longer ribbons sway in the shallows.
sceneCN: 这里 algae 指「附生在湿石与浅水中的藻类」（第 1 个义项：藻类总称，从单细胞到大型海藻）；句意：退潮时岩石上覆着一层滑腻的褐绿色藻膜，较长的带状藻体在浅水中摆动。图中可辨识物件：退潮后的礁石、褐绿色薄膜、浅水、随浪摆动的长带状藻体。

pos.zh: 藻类（拉丁复数，常作集合名词，指从单细胞到大型海藻的一大类光合生物）
藻（拉丁单数 alga 的复数形式，指一个或多个藻体）

derivatives.zh: 褐藻胶；褐藻酸盐（从褐藻中提取的增稠剂）

senses.title: The group as a whole
senses.titleCN: 藻类总称（一大类行光合作用的水生生物）
senses.definition: the whole assemblage of photosynthetic organisms that lack true roots, stems and leaves, from single cells to giant kelps
senses.definitionCN: 一大类没有真正的根、茎、叶而行光合作用的生物总体，从单细胞到巨型海带都包括在内
senses.example: At low tide the rocks are covered with a slippery brown-green film of algae, and longer ribbons sway in the shallows.
senses.exampleCN: 退潮时岩石上覆着一层滑腻的褐绿色藻膜，较长的带状藻体在浅水中摆动。
senses.why: the Latin plural is used collectively for the group, exactly as a class name is used in botany.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁复数被用作整类的集合名称，正如植物学中使用类群名那样。

senses.title: Single-celled algae
senses.titleCN: 单细胞藻（微藻）
senses.definition: one-celled forms such as diatoms and green flagellates, often cultured or counted cell by cell
senses.definitionCN: 硅藻、绿色鞭毛藻这类单细胞形态，常被培养或逐个细胞计数
senses.example: Single-celled algae in the pond were small enough to pass through the filter.
senses.exampleCN: 池里的单细胞藻小到能穿过滤网。
senses.why: because the plural can be counted, it names individual cells when the context is a sample or a culture.
senses.whyCN: 复数可以计数，因此在样品或培养的语境中它就指一个个细胞。

senses.title: Seaweeds and large attached forms
senses.titleCN: 大型海藻（海带、石莼等）
senses.definition: large multicellular algae attached to rock or seabed, with holdfasts and fronds rather than roots and leaves
senses.definitionCN: 附着在岩石或海底的大型多细胞藻，以固着器与叶状体代替根和叶
senses.example: Brown algae along this coast form dense beds at the low-tide line.
senses.exampleCN: 这一带的褐藻在低潮线形成密集藻床。
senses.why: the same plural covers the seaweeds because they are algae by descent, only larger and attached.
senses.whyCN: 海藻在亲缘上仍是藻，只是更大且附着生长，因此同一个复数也涵盖它们。

senses.title: Freshwater algae
senses.titleCN: 淡水藻（水绵、颤藻等）
senses.definition: algae of lakes, rivers and ponds, including green filaments and cyanobacterial mats that float or coat surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 湖泊、河流与池塘中的藻，包括漂浮或覆盖表面的绿色丝状体与蓝细菌藻席
senses.example: Filamentous green algae choked the shallow end of the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 丝状绿藻塞满了湖的浅水端。
senses.why: habitat rather than form separates this use: the word stays the same, only the water changes.
senses.whyCN: 这一用法靠生境而非形态区分：词形不变，只是水换了。

senses.title: Bloom and red tide
senses.titleCN: 藻华与赤潮（有害藻华）
senses.definition: a mass proliferation of algae that discolours water, depletes oxygen or releases toxins harmful to fish and people
senses.definitionCN: 藻类大规模增殖，使水变色、耗尽氧气或释放对鱼与人有害的毒素
senses.example: Toxic algae closed the shellfish beds for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 有毒藻类使贝类养殖区关闭了一个月。
senses.why: when the group multiplies out of control it becomes an event, and the class name is used for that event.
senses.whyCN: 当这一类群失控增殖，它就成了一个事件，类群名便被用来指该事件。

senses.title: Cultivation, feed and fuel
senses.titleCN: 藻类养殖、饲料与生物燃料
senses.definition: algae grown in ponds or closed reactors for oil, animal feed, fertiliser or wastewater treatment
senses.definitionCN: 在池塘或密闭反应器中培养的藻，用于制油、做饲料、作肥料或处理废水
senses.example: Algae grown in shallow ponds can be harvested for oil.
senses.exampleCN: 在浅池中培养的藻可收获用于制油。
senses.why: from the wild group the word passes to the industrial crop, because the same organisms are now farmed.
senses.whyCN: 从野生类群过渡到工业作物，因为被养殖的正是同一批生物。

senses.title: Symbiotic algae inside other organisms
senses.titleCN: 共生藻（地衣、珊瑚体内的藻）
senses.definition: algae living inside lichens, corals or sponges, giving them photosynthesis in exchange for shelter
senses.definitionCN: 生活在地衣、珊瑚或海绵体内的藻，以光合产物换取庇护
senses.example: Algae living in coral tissues supply most of the reef's energy.
senses.exampleCN: 生活在珊瑚组织里的藻提供礁体的大部分能量。
senses.why: the relationship, not the habitat, defines this use: the algae are inside another body.
senses.whyCN: 定义这一用法的是共生关系而非生境：藻在另一个生物体内。

senses.title: Fossil algae and ancient environments
senses.titleCN: 化石藻与古环境
senses.definition: algal remains such as stromatolites, diatomite and calcareous nannofossils used to date rocks and reconstruct past water
senses.definitionCN: 叠层石、硅藻土与钙质超微化石这类藻类遗存，用于测定岩层年代与重建古水体
senses.example: Fossil algae in the core showed that the lake had once been saline.
senses.exampleCN: 岩芯中的化石藻表明这个湖曾经是咸水。
senses.why: hard parts and mats preserve well, so the group name also covers its fossil record and the evidence it provides.
senses.whyCN: 坚硬部分与藻席易于保存，因此类群名也涵盖其化石记录与所提供的证据。

intro.en: Algae is the Latin plural of alga 'seaweed, water plant', borrowed into English in the seventeenth century and used collectively ever since. The deeper origin of Latin alga is uncertain: no Indo-European source is agreed, and comparisons with other words for seaweed are hypotheses.
intro.cn: algae 是拉丁语 alga「海藻、水草」的复数，17 世纪借入英语，此后一直作集合名词使用。拉丁 alga 的更深来源不确定：没有公认的印欧语语源，与其它语言中「海藻」词的比较均属假说。

items.en: Latin alga is recorded for seaweed and water plants in classical texts. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and proposals linking it to other European words for seaweed are unproven.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alga 在古典文本中已用于指海藻与水草。其更深来源不确定，把它与其它欧洲语言中「海藻」词相联系的提议未获证实。

items.en: Alga belongs to the first declension, so its nominative plural is algae; English took the plural form first and kept the Latin ending.
items.cn: alga 属第一变格法，其主格复数为 algae；英语先借入复数形式，并保留了这个拉丁语词尾。

items.en: Algae enters English in the seventeenth century as a learned Latin plural, at first in botanical and medical writing.
items.cn: algae 于 17 世纪作为学术性的拉丁复数进入英语，最早见于植物学与医学写作。

items.en: In the nineteenth century algae became the name of a major group in botany, contrasted with fungi, and the singular alga was revived for a single organism.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，algae 成为植物学中一个主要类群的名称，与真菌相对；单数 alga 也被重新启用，指单个藻体。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word spread from taxonomy to water management, aquaculture and fuel research, where it is often treated as a mass noun.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词从分类学扩散到水质管理、水产养殖与燃料研究，在这些领域常被当作不可数名词使用。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and exact first date): the pre-Latin source of alga is unknown, and the first English citation is only approximate; any Indo-European form proposed for alga is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与确切首见年代）：alga 在拉丁语之前的来源不明，最早的英语书证只能给约数；凡为 alga 提出的印欧语词形均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like algae or share its Latin stem, some genuinely related and one not; group two holds field terms whose scope is narrower or different.
note.cn: 第一组是与 algae 形近或共享拉丁词干的词，其中有真同源，也有纯属形近；第二组是范围更窄或所指不同的同领域术语。

entries.definition: The singular of algae, used for one individual thallus; the plural in -ae is the form English borrowed first.
entries.definitionCN: algae 的单数形式，指一个单独的藻体；英语最早借入的其实是 -ae 的复数形式。

entries.definition: An English adjective meaning 'of or relating to algae', formed from alga plus -al; it is neither a plural nor a species name.
entries.definitionCN: 英语形容词，意为「藻的、与藻有关的」，由 alga 加 -al 构成；它既不是复数，也不是物种名。

entries.definition: A salt of alginic acid extracted from brown algae and used as a thickener; it is a substance made from algae, not another name for them.
entries.definitionCN: 从褐藻中提取的褐藻酸盐，用作增稠剂；它是用藻做出的物质，而非藻的别称。

entries.definition: Cold or chilly, from Latin algere 'to be cold'; it resembles alga- in spelling but has no connection with algae.
entries.definitionCN: 意为寒冷的，来自拉丁 algere「发冷」；拼写与 alga- 相近，但与藻类毫无关系。

entries.tag: everyday word for large marine algae
entries.definition: The everyday term for large marine algae seen on shores; it excludes most single-celled forms, which algae includes.
entries.definitionCN: 指海岸上见到的大型海生藻类的日常说法；它排除多数单细胞形态，而 algae 包含这些。

entries.definition: Microscopic algae, cultured or counted individually; it is a size-based part of the broader group.
entries.definitionCN: 微小的藻，可培养或逐个计数；它是更大类群中按体径划分的一部分。

entries.definition: Photosynthetic bacteria formerly classed as blue-green algae; under modern classification they are not true algae.
entries.definitionCN: 过去被归为蓝藻的光合细菌；按现代分类它们并非真正的藻类。

entries.definition: The drifting, photosynthetic members of the algae along with cyanobacteria; it selects by lifestyle, not by taxonomy.
entries.definitionCN: 藻类中漂移且行光合作用的成员，并包括蓝细菌；它按生活方式而非分类来选取。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real stems, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词干、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Algae is a plural in -ae, so one organism is an alga and two are algae; the adjective is algal.
normal.cn: algae 是以 -ae 结尾的复数，因此一个藻体是 alga，两个才是 algae；形容词是 algal。

normal.en: Colour names organise the group: green, red and brown algae differ in pigments and storage products.
normal.cn: 颜色名把这一类群分成几支：绿藻、红藻与褐藻的色素与储藏物质不同。

normal.en: Blue-green algae is the old name for cyanobacteria, which are bacteria and not algae at all.
normal.cn: blue-green algae 是蓝细菌的旧名，而蓝细菌属于细菌，根本不是藻。

normal.en: Algal bloom is the standard technical phrase; algae bloom is the looser everyday variant.
normal.cn: algal bloom 是标准技术说法；algae bloom 是较松散的日常变体。

normal.en: Alginate from brown algae thickens ice cream, and algaculture now grows algae for fuel and feed.
normal.cn: 褐藻来的褐藻胶给冰淇淋增稠，藻类养殖则为燃料与饲料培养藻。

abstract.en: Picture a wet rock painted with a thin green skin that no one notices until it slips.
abstract.cn: 想象一块湿石头被涂上一层薄薄的绿皮，没人注意，直到踩上去打滑。

abstract.en: Picture a pond turning soup-green overnight while the fish gasp at the surface.
abstract.cn: 想象池塘一夜之间变成汤一样的绿色，鱼在水面喘气。

abstract.en: Picture a coral animal farming tiny green cells inside its own tissue.
abstract.cn: 想象一只珊瑚动物在自己的组织里种着微小的绿色细胞。

examples.en: Algae range from single cells to kelps tens of metres long.
examples.cn: 藻类从单细胞到数十米长的海带都有。

examples.en: The aquarium glass was thick with green algae within a month.
examples.cn: 一个月内水族箱玻璃上就长满了厚厚的绿藻。

examples.en: Researchers grow algae in open ponds to produce oil.
examples.cn: 研究者在露天池塘中培养藻类以生产油脂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「algae」读似「爱尔吉」——海藻爱在水里长、爱在石上滑；纯属谐音，非词源

root: 拉丁语 alga「海藻、水草」的复数 algae；alga 的更深来源不确定，无公认的印欧语语源，与其它语言中「海藻」词的比较均属假说。英语 17 世纪借入，单数 alga，复数按拉丁第一变格法 -a → -ae。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: a green film on a wet surface, repeated at every scale. The group is named first, then the single cell, then the seaweed, the freshwater form, the bloom, the crop, the symbiont and finally the fossil.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个意象展开：湿表面上的一层绿膜，在各个尺度上重复。先指整个类群，再指单细胞、大型海藻、淡水藻，然后是藻华、养殖作物、共生体，最后是化石。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green film that lives where water stays.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层绿膜，长在水停留的地方。

branches.en: GROUP AND CELL: one collective plural, one countable reading for single cells.
branches.cn: 类群与细胞：一个集合复数，也可数地指单细胞。

branches.en: BIG AND FRESH: the same word covers seaweeds and lake filaments by habitat and size.
branches.cn: 大型与淡水：同一个词按生境与体径涵盖海藻和湖中丝状体。

branches.en: BLOOM: excess turns the group into a water-quality event.
branches.cn: 藻华：过量使这一类群变成水质事件。

branches.en: CROP: the same organisms become feed, fertiliser and fuel.
branches.cn: 作物：同一批生物成了饲料、肥料与燃料。

branches.en: PARTNER AND FOSSIL: algae live inside other bodies, and their remains tell past water.
branches.cn: 共生与化石：藻可生活在别的生物体内，其遗存也能说明古代水体。

intro.en: Algae is a Latin noun borrowed whole, so its family is built from the Latin stem alg- plus English suffixes and combining forms.
intro.cn: algae 是整体借入的拉丁名词，因此其词族由拉丁词干 alg- 加英语后缀与构词成分构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin alga 'seaweed, water plant' gives the English singular alga and the plural algae; the same stem appears in the adjective algal and in alginate, named from alginic acid. The pre-Latin origin of alga is unknown, so no further Latin relative is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 alga「海藻、水草」给出英语单数 alga 与复数 algae；同一词干还见于形容词 algal 与得名于褐藻酸的 alginate。alga 在拉丁语之前的来源不明，因此不再列出更远的拉丁同族词。

items.example: Alga is the singular used for one thallus.
items.exampleCN: alga 是单数，指一个藻体。

items.example: Algae is the plural form that English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: algae 是英语借入的复数形式。

items.example: Algal mats cover the rock surface.
items.exampleCN: 藻席覆盖着岩石表面。

items.example: Algology began as a branch of botany.
items.exampleCN: 藻类学最初是植物学的一个分支。

items.example: An algologist identified the bloom species.
items.exampleCN: 一位藻类学家鉴定出了藻华的物种。

items.meaning: a salt of alginic acid from brown algae
items.meaningCN: 褐藻中提取的褐藻酸盐
items.example: Alginate thickens the ice cream.
items.exampleCN: 褐藻胶使冰淇淋变稠。

items.example: Algaculture supplies feed and fuel.
items.exampleCN: 藻类养殖提供饲料与燃料。

items.example: Copper sulfate serves as an algicide in reservoirs.
items.exampleCN: 硫酸铜在水库里用作杀藻剂。

items.example: Microalgae are grown in closed reactors.
items.exampleCN: 微藻在密闭反应器中培养。

latinEntries.example: Latin alga names the plant cast up on the shore.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁 alga 指被冲上岸的水生植物。

latinEntries.example: The Latin plural algae passed into English unchanged.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁复数 algae 原样进入了英语。
